summary:
KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- Engines: 1.5-litre K15B petrol (1462cc, 103 bhp @ 6000 rpm, 138 Nm @ 4400 rpm, mild-hybrid); 1.5-litre DDiS225 diesel (94 bhp @ 4000 rpm, 225 Nm @ 1500-2500 rpm, non-hybrid).  
- Transmissions: Petrol – 5-speed manual or 4-speed torque converter automatic; Diesel – 6-speed manual only.  
- Hybrid Tech: Petrol features Maruti’s SHVS mild-hybrid system (dual battery, start-stop, brake regeneration).  
- Fuel Economy: Petrol ARAI 20.04–20.65 kmpl; Diesel ARAI 26.82 kmpl; Diesel real-world 18.5–21.1 kmpl.  
- Safety: Dual front airbags, ABS with EBD, ISOFIX mounts, seatbelt reminder, high-speed alert system; ESP and hill hold on the automatic; ASEAN NCAP 4-star rating.  
- Ride and Handling: Soft suspension tuned for comfort; absorbs bumps well, feels clunky on sharper impacts; secure and planted at normal speeds; lifeless steering feedback across versions.  
- Exterior Dimensions: Length ~4.5 metres; Wheelbase ~2.7 metres; longest in segment; large sedan proportions.  
- Wheels: 16-inch precision-cut alloy wheels (top variants); 15-inch on lower variants.  
- Lighting: Full LED headlamps with DRLs, LED fog lamps, LED taillights; updated grille and bumpers in facelift.  
- Interior Quality: Functional, well-finished with dull wood grain and satin chrome accents; extensive hard plastics but do not feel cheap; faux leather in some variants.  
- Space/Practicality: Class-leading cabin (rear legroom, shoulder room); 3-abreast rear seat with ample headroom; large 510-litre boot class-best; high driving position, good front/rear visibility.  
- Infotainment: Maruti SmartPlay with touchscreen; Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, Bluetooth, USB/AUX; simple UI, but dated graphics; average sound quality.  
- Instrumentation: 4.2-inch colour MID (driver info, trip data, hybrid/drive feedback); analogue dials for core info.  
- Convenience Features: Automatic single-zone climate control, rear AC vents, cruise control, auto LED headlamps, multifunction steering, remote keyless entry, electric mirrors, rear sunshade (some variants).  
- Seating: Large, supportive front seats; low seat base for rear under-thigh support; manually height-adjustable driver seat; tilt steering only (no telescopic or reach).  
- Service/Ownership: Annual service cost ~Rs 4,413; benefit of Maruti’s strong service/dealer network, high resale.  
- Price Range: Petrol Rs 8.19–10.97 lakhs (ex-showroom); Diesel Rs 9.98–11.38 lakhs (ex-showroom).  
- Variants: Petrol and diesel – Delta, Zeta, Alpha trims; top trims with extra features and larger wheels.  
- Distinct Misses: No 6-speed auto or diesel AT, no ADAS, no sunroof, no front parking sensors or 360 camera, no rear center three-point seatbelt, no curtain/side airbags, no soft-touch surfaces.

---

REVIEW SUMMARY

1. OVERVIEW
- The Maruti Suzuki Ciaz, reviewed by CarWale (Kapil Angane, et al.), is a value-focused, practical C-segment sedan with segment-leading space, excellent fuel efficiency, and an updated engine lineup, but lacks modern feature and performance trappings of some rivals.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
- Petrol: 1.5L K15B (103 bhp/138 Nm), mild-hybrid; offers strong low-speed power, spike past 3,000 rpm; manual box is engaging, automatic (4-speed) is smooth but slow/traditional, ideal for city crawl but outdated for enthusiasts.
- Diesel: 1.5L DDiS225 (94 bhp/225 Nm); new unit is notably quieter and more refined than previous 1.3L, good low and midrange torque, minimal turbo lag (vs old engine), cruises at 100 km/h around 1900rpm in sixth, but lacks outright punch.
- No mention of 0-100 km/h times; reviewers note neither engine is sporty nor eager at top-end.
- Handling: Steering is light and direct at parking speeds but vague/lifeless on center; not confidence-inspiring at highway speeds.
- Ride: Soft suspension yields comfort on most surfaces, absorbs bumps well (especially at low speeds), but clunky/noisy over sharp edges, some body movement on big bumps.
- Braking: Not specified; no quantitative stopping figures.
- NVH: Petrol engine sounds harsh at high rpm; diesel quieter than before but suspension noise still comes through.

3. EXTERIOR
- Contemporary, balanced design with chrome highlights, new grille, revised bumpers, LED projector headlamps with DRLs, LED fog lamps, striking LED taillights.  
- Largest sedan in class; length ~4.5m, wheelbase ~2.7m (best in segment).  
- Eye-catching 16-inch alloy wheels (top variants), 15-inch on lower trims.  
- Overall, styling is mature but now looks dated compared to newer rivals; lacks design excitement.

4. INTERIOR
- Layout largely unchanged post-facelift, but gains dull wood grain accents, satin chrome on dashboard/doors, faux leather on higher variants.
- Functional, durable feel; notable hard plastics throughout but not cheap-feeling.
- Segment-benchmark space, especially at rear (ample legroom, headroom, shoulder room).
- Rear seat can seat three comfortably, but under-thigh support is only average due to short seat base; rear sunshade included.
- Boot: 510 litres – class-leading for segment, easily fits family/weekend luggage.
- Driving position is high with good visibility; easy seat ergonomics, manual driver height adjustment, pedals well-placed with dead pedal.
- Storage: Multiple bottle holders, practical cubbies.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
- Infotainment: Touchscreen SmartPlay, Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, Bluetooth, USB/AUX, straightforward interface, but graphics/look now dated; sound quality only average.
- Instrumentation: 4.2-inch multi-information driver display (trip data, hybrid feedback, range, settings for lights/locks).
- Convenience: Automatic climate control, rear AC vents, cruise control, auto headlamps, keyless entry, driver seat height adjust, multifunction steering wheel; notable rear sunshade.
- No telematics/connected car, wireless charging, 360-camera or sunroof.
- Settings customization available for lights and locks via MID.

6. SAFETY
- Dual front airbags, ABS/EBD, ISOFIX child seat mounts, high-speed alert, seatbelt reminders (driver, front passenger) standard.
- ESP and hill hold for automatic variants.
- ASEAN NCAP 4-star rating.
- Does NOT offer: Front parking sensors, 360-degree camera, rear center 3-point belt, curtain/side airbags, traction/multicollision systems.
- Crash test results apart from ASEAN NCAP not available.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
- Petrol: Claimed 20.04–20.65 kmpl (manual/auto/mild-hybrid); real-world figures not specified.
- Diesel: ARAI 26.82 kmpl; reviewer achieved up to 21.1 kmpl highway, 18.5 kmpl city, avg. ~19.8 kmpl.
- Mild-hybrid tech in petrol aids efficiency via start-stop/brake regeneration; not present in diesel at review time.
- Both engines among the most efficient in segment.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
- Petrol: Rs 8.19–10.97 lakh (ex-showroom).
- Diesel: Rs 9.98–11.38 lakh (ex-showroom).
- Undercuts segment rivals (Hyundai Verna, Honda City) by Rs 1.6–3 lakh.
- Annual service cost: ~Rs 4,413.
- Resale: Strong, due to Maruti branding and mainstream acceptance.
- Warranty: Not mentioned in review.
- Maintenance: Noted as affordable; widespread dealer support.

9. PROS AND CONS

PROS
- Exceptional rear seat and boot space; spacious cabin (benchmark in segment).
- Great value, lower price than segment peers.
- Comfortable, absorbent ride in the city.
- Highly efficient engines (petrol with hybrid/stop-start, diesel impressive too).
- Easy to drive (light clutch, visibility, light steering).
- Loaded with key convenience features and usable tech.
- Strong Maruti brand: reliable, affordable to maintain, excellent resale, widespread aftersales.

CONS
- Performance and gearboxes lack excitement; petrol auto is dated and slow, diesel lacks auto option.
- Steering feels disconnected, lifeless at higher speeds.
- Feature list falling behind segment standards: lacks modern amenities (ADAS, sunroof, telematics, more airbags).
- Cabin uses hard plastics, no soft-touch materials.
- Suspension is noisy and feels unsettled on rough patches.
- Outdated styling and interior design/graphics.
- No engine/variant choice for those seeking powerful or fun-to-drive experience.
- No diesel automatic.
- Only tilt steering, no reach adjustment.

10. COMPETITORS
- Primary segment rivals: Honda City, Hyundai Verna, Toyota Yaris, Volkswagen Vento TSI.
- City and Verna: Have higher prices, more features, more advanced automatics, but less space.
- Vento TSI: More engaging to drive, higher-end AT, but pricier and less rear-seat comfort.
- Unique Ciaz selling points: Best cabin/boot space, value-oriented pricing, lower maintenance, fuel economy, ease of use.
- Lacks excitement or feature set of newer rivals but stands out for space, comfort, and price.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
- Main trims: Delta, Zeta, Alpha for both engines.
- Top Alfa variant recommended for maximum features (touchscreen, alloys, cruise, LED lighting, rear sunshade).
- Lower trims miss out on larger wheels and some convenience features.
- Petrol available with both manual and auto; diesel manual only.
- No variant offers an all-round, fully loaded package with modern features.

12. VERDICT
- Maruti Suzuki Ciaz excels at core sedan virtues: cabin and boot space, ride comfort, ease of use, and value for money.
- Weaknesses in performance engagement, transmission tech, modern features, and cabin refinement.
- Ideal buy for pragmatic customers who prioritize space, comfort, and low running costs over driving excitement or feature-loaded luxury.
- Rating: Not numerically specified, but sentiment is strongly positive for city- and family-focused buyers; less so for those seeking excitement or new tech.
model_summary: Spacious, fuel-efficient sedan ideal for families and city driving; delivers comfort, huge boot, easy maintenance, but lacks advanced features.

summary:
KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- Powertrain: Dual electric motors with a combined output of 300kW (408bhp) and 664Nm torque; enables quattro all-wheel drive.
- Battery: 95kWh lithium-ion battery, mounted below the passenger compartment for low center of gravity and protected against underbody impacts.
- Range: Theoretical range up to 400km per charge; real-world test suggests over 350km is realistic, depending on usage.
- Regenerative Braking: Adjustable levels via steering-mounted paddle shifters; can recuperate up to 30% of range through energy recovery.
- Acceleration: 0-60km/h in 2.88 seconds; 0-100km/h in 5.35 seconds; 40-100km/h in 3.53 seconds.
- Charging: Supports 22kW AC charger (standard); 11kW AC home charger can provide full charge in 8.5 hours; compact mobile charging system charges battery to 80% in 4.5 hours; dual charging ports (AC/DC on driver’s side, AC on passenger side) for convenience.
- Adaptive Air Suspension: Provides adjustable ride height, improves ride comfort, assists in protecting battery over rough roads.
- Infotainment: Dual large touchscreen displays (upper: main infotainment; lower: climate controls); digital instrument cluster (Audi’s Virtual Cockpit); supports advanced navigation, media, and vehicle settings.
- Premium Features: Panoramic sunroof, Matrix LED headlamps, soft-closing doors, 16-speaker Bang & Olufsen sound system, four-zone climate control, ambient lighting, heads-up display.
- Interior Space: Seats four adults comfortably with generous legroom and shoulder room; wide front seats, supportive rear bench, flat floor for middle rear passenger legroom.
- Build Quality: High standard, consistent with Audi’s flagship SUVs; quality materials throughout cabin.

---

REVIEW SUMMARY STRUCTURE

1. OVERVIEW
   - Audi e-tron is Audi’s first all-electric production model, targeting luxury SUV and EV buyers. The review is by Kaustubh Gandhi for CarWale. The e-tron promises a conventional Audi experience with modern electric performance and luxury appointments.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
   - Uses dual motors (one per axle) for all-wheel drive, total output 408bhp/664Nm. 0-60km/h in 2.88s, 0-100km/h in 5.35s; 40-100km/h in 3.53s. Delivers instantaneous acceleration typical of EVs; strong in-gear performance. Adaptive air suspension ensures cushyride over rough surfaces while maintaining body control. Steering feel and body control similar to Q7. However, handling is less agile compared to lighter SUVs; mass makes it less dynamic during spirited driving. Braking integrates regenerative system with strong power adjustment via paddles. Transmission is single-speed reduction gear, offers seamless and instant torque delivery.

3. EXTERIOR
   - Design features similar to Audi’s large SUVs; size between Q5 and Q7. Matrix LED headlamps and distinctive Audi grille. Muscular body lines, large presence on the road. Available with Matrix LED lighting, panoramic sunroof, and soft-closing doors. Virtual mirrors available in some global markets, not confirmed for India. Range of exterior colors not specified in review.

4. INTERIOR
   - Premium cabin with two large touchscreens; high-quality materials and solid build. Spacious interior, seats four adults comfortably. Wide front seats, ample rear legroom and shoulder room; flat floor benefits middle occupant. Rear windows small, creating a slightly claustrophobic feel for three passengers. No transmission tunnel, but knee room compromised for middle rear due to climate control panel. Infotainment screens are attractive but fingerprint-prone. Storage and practicality details not specifically highlighted beyond luggage-carrying suitability.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
   - Infotainment: Dual touchscreens, Audi Virtual Cockpit digital driver display. 16-speaker Bang & Olufsen system, four-zone climate control, heads-up display, ambient lighting, wireless charging standard. Adaptive air suspension with adjustable ride height. Charging system includes both AC/DC ports and dual-side accessibility. Connectivity options (Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, Bluetooth) not explicitly mentioned but likely given segment standards. Driver assistance features like parking sensors and others not specified in review.

6. SAFETY
   - Official safety ratings not mentioned. Expected to feature standard segment safety like multiple airbags, ABS, electronic stability. Innovative safety noted in form of adaptive suspension protecting battery. Optional 360-degree cameras, blind-spot monitoring, or virtual mirrors not confirmed for Indian market.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
   - Claimed range: up to 400km per charge. Real-world test drive indicated about 330km in mixed driving (200km driven, 130km estimated remaining). Regeneration system can account for up to 30% of total range. Segment comparison suggests range is competitive with direct rivals.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
   - Price not officially stated in review; expected to be competitive with Mercedes EQC and Jaguar I-Pace (~₹1.3 crore on-road). Value assessment strong if Audi can offer price advantage. Warranty and maintenance details not mentioned.

9. PROS AND CONS
   - Pros: Instantaneous performance, comfortable and refined ride quality, premium build, spacious interior, strong real-world range, advanced features.
   - Cons: Handling not as dynamic as lighter SUVs ("lazy handling"), charging durations still lag behind refueling ease, rear window area reduces sense of space for some back seat occupants.

10. COMPETITORS
    - Main rivals: Mercedes EQC, Jaguar I-Pace. e-tron’s strengths include quicker acceleration, familiar high-quality Audi experience, comfortable ride. Whether it can outperform on pricing is key; EQC and I-Pace priced at ₹1.3 crore, so e-tron needs aggressive pricing to stand out.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
    - Only the e-tron 55 quattro variant mentioned for Indian market; global markets have other variants with differing specs. Feature content comprehensive in current variant; recommended variant not specified in review.

12. VERDICT
    - e-tron successfully combines the familiarity and luxury of Audi SUVs with the instant performance and innovation of modern EVs. Especially recommended for those seeking an all-electric, premium SUV that rides like a conventional luxury vehicle. If priced under direct rivals, it is a top luxury EV contender. Overall score or rating not provided in the review.

summary:
KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- Engine: 1.0-litre K10C, 3-cylinder petrol, 998cc; dual-jet, dual-VVT technology; idle start-stop function; BS6 Phase Two compliant. Available in petrol and CNG versions.
- Power/Torque (Petrol): 66bhp, 89Nm; CNG version produces 56bhp, 82.1Nm.
- Transmission: Five-speed manual or AGS (AMT) automatic; CNG only available with 5-speed manual.
- Fuel Efficiency: Claimed ARAI mileage for petrol between 24.97kmpl and 26.68kmpl depending on variant; CNG version claimed at 34.43km/kg. Real-world test: city 18.42kmpl, highway 23.18kmpl, combined 19.61kmpl.
- Safety: Six airbags (standard), ABS with EBD, ESP, front disc brakes, hill hold assist (AMT), rear parking sensors, speed alert, child lock. No official crash test rating yet. Rear camera not available.
- Platform: Maruti Suzuki Heartect, reduced vehicle weight for efficiency and nimble handling.
- Dimensions: Considerably larger than previous generation; accommodates five adults; boot capacity 313 litres (non-CNG). Tall roof for improved headroom; wide-opening doors for easy ingress/egress.
- Steering and Seats: Height-adjustable driver’s seat (top variants), tilt steering, fixed headrests (no rear adjustable headrests), comfortable front seats, rear bench best for two adults.
- Interior: All-black theme with brushed aluminium/silver inlays. Seven-inch SmartPlay Studio touchscreen infotainment with Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, voice commands, steering controls, four speakers.
- Convenience: Electrically adjustable and auto-folding ORVMs, keyless entry with push-button start/stop (both front doors), rear wash/wipe with defogger, cup holders in console, one-litre door bottle holders, ample cabin storage.
- Lighting: Bulbous halogen headlamps, fog lamps (top trims), ORVM turn indicators, rear wiper.
- Colours: Silky Silver, Glistening Grey, Fire Red, Speedy Blue, Bluish Black, Caffeine Brown, Arctic White.
- Pricing: Ex-showroom from Rs 4.99 lakh to Rs 6.94 lakh; top ZXI Plus AMT at Rs 7.00 lakh ex-showroom, approx Rs 8.15 lakh on-road Mumbai (as tested).
- Maintenance: Approximate annual service cost Rs 4,050.
- Unique Features: Idle start-stop technology (segment-first), factory-fitted CNG in VXI trim.
- Standout Practicality: High seating, good visibility, compact footprint for easy driving/parking, wide doors aid elderly, versatile boot for the class.
- Drawbacks: Window and central locking switches positioned on center console (not door), dated pull-type door handles, absence of premium features found in rivals like Teago (e.g. projector headlamps, rear camera, cooled glove box, extra audio, etc.).

---

REVIEW SUMMARY

1. OVERVIEW
   - The Maruti Suzuki Celerio (latest generation, ZXI Plus AMT tested, reviewed by CarWale and others) is positioned as an ideal, practical city hatchback targeting first-time car buyers and those seeking a second household car. Reviewers concur it justifies its price with increased desirability, space, and features, though value-for-money perception has dropped with the price hike.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
   - 998cc K10C 3-cylinder engine; 66bhp (petrol), 56bhp (CNG), 89Nm (petrol), 82.1Nm (CNG).
   - Potent low and mid-range makes urban driving and overtaking easy; not sporty, estimated 0-100km/h in around 10 seconds; top performance more about efficiency and drivability than speed.
   - Manual gearbox: short throws, smooth shifts, light clutch for engaging drive. AMT (AGS): well-calibrated for city, convenient in traffic, but can feel jerky at low speeds, holds low gears too long, slightly erratic throttle at startup, better in manual mode.
   - Ride/Handling: Light, nimble, settled at 110-120km/h. Handling is agile for segment thanks to low weight, but steering is slow to respond, offers little feedback. Ride can get busy and noisy over poor surfaces, suspension slow to settle after bumps.
   - Noise/Vibrations: Impressively refined for a 3-cylinder, minimal NVH at idle, some engine noise at higher RPMs.
   - Brakes: Standard front discs, balanced, fade not reported.
   - Engine mounts (pendulum system) effectively suppress typical 3-cylinder vibrations.
   - CNG variant: Reduced power/torque but retains city usability.

3. EXTERIOR
   - Notable for quirky, curvy, youthful design; large bulbous halogen headlamps, chrome-accented grille; tall-boy stance.
   - Blacked-out alloy wheels (top spec), chrome elements.
   - Seven colour options including new Caffeine Brown.
   - Modern width and length upgrades over predecessor, higher roof aids headroom.
   - Some elements (pull-type door handles, keyholes) feel dated next to rivals.

4. INTERIOR
   - Upgraded all-black, hard plastic cabin with brushed aluminium/silver accents, high level of fit and finish.
   - Dashboard, switchgear, seat fabric design borrowed from Wagon R.
   - High-mounted 7-inch touchscreen, large driver’s display.
   - Ergonomics: Height-adjustable driver’s seat (top trim) and tilt steering deliver good driving position. Front seats comfortable for long durations; rear: fixed headrests, short on thigh support, best for two, but three can squeeze in.
   - Rear seat ingress/egress: Excellent (wide opening, high seats).
   - Practicality: Cupholders, 1-litre bottle holders in each door, glovebox, centre console storage (limited space for phone).
   - Boot: 313 litres (non-CNG), deep floor boosts luggage accommodation.
   - Negative: Window/lock switches in centre console (unusual, inconvenient), especially rear switch placement.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
   - Seven-inch SmartPlay Studio touchscreen (Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, Bluetooth, voice commands), four speakers, smooth touch interface.
   - Steering-mounted controls, tachometer, engine start/stop button, keyless entry (request buttons on both front doors).
   - Electrically adjustable, auto-folding ORVMs; rear wash/wipe and defogger, height-adjustable driver’s seat (top trims), tilt steering.
   - Hill hold assist (AMT), push-button start/stop.
   - No rear camera even on top variant. Limited advanced features versus some rivals (no cooled glovebox, projector headlamps, rear camera, etc.).
   - Some minor issues with connectivity (USB port position/behavior).

6. SAFETY
   - Six airbags standard (current update).
   - ABS with EBD, ESP, child locks, rear parking sensors, hill hold assist (AMT), front disc brakes.
   - Speed alerts, impact-sensing auto door unlock, speed-sensitive auto lock.
   - No official NCAP crash test rating; not tested yet.
   - Lacks rear camera, rear seat lacks adjustable headrests.
   - CNG variants get same core safety equipment profile.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
   - Petrol ARAI: 24.97–26.68kmpl (variant-dependent).
   - Real-world (CarWale): City 18.42kmpl, highway 23.18kmpl, combined 19.61kmpl.
   - CNG: 34.43km/kg claimed.
   - Segment-leading efficiency, among the highest for hatchbacks.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
   - Price ex-showroom: Rs 4.99 lakh (base) to Rs 6.94 lakh (top AMT). Top-spec ZXI Plus AMT at Rs 7.00 lakh (ex), Rs 8.15 lakh (on-road, Mumbai).
   - Annual service cost: Rs 4,050.
   - Now significantly costlier (Rs 1.40 lakh hike vs previous gen, Rs 95,000 premium for CNG over VXI).
   - Feature list not as rich as some direct rivals (e.g., Tiago top-spec).
   - Justifies premium through improved engine/drivetrain, space, safety, but not outstanding VFM.
   - Notable warranty/maintenance terms not mentioned in review.

9. PROS AND CONS
   Pros:
   - Exceptionally easy, practical city car; compact size, great visibility, and light controls; ingress/egress especially good for elderly.
   - Segment-leading real-world and claimed fuel efficiency. Efficient both for petrol and CNG variants.
   - Smooth, peppy, and refined motor, particularly in urban conditions. Manual is engaging, AMT convenient.
   - Upgraded, more desirable looks and cabin; solid boot space for segment.
   - Six airbags, robust core safety suite.
   - Good standard feature list on top variants.
   Cons:
   - Price premium over previous generation and rivals, especially considering limited headlining features vs competitors.
   - AMT gearbox at low speeds is jerky, holds low gears too long; manual smoother for spirited driving.
   - Rear seat: fixed headrests, short thigh support, comfort for three not ideal.
   - Steering response slow, lacks feedback.
   - Ride quality busy and less composed on poor surfaces.
   - No rear camera, infotainment shortcut logic not intuitive; USB performance/connectivity quirks.
   - Pull-type door handles, central console switchgear feel dated/inconvenient.

10. COMPETITORS
   - Tata Tiago (strongest rival), Hyundai Grand i10 Nios, Maruti Suzuki Wagon R, Suzuki Swift (lower variants).
   - Compared to Tiago and Nios: Celerio leads in fuel efficiency, is lighter, easier to drive, but loses on feature count (Tiago offers projector headlamps, LED DRL, cooled glovebox, rear camera, richer infotainment, more speakers).
   - Unique proposition: light weight, segment-best real world/claimed mileage, compact-yet-airy cabin, factory CNG.
   - Not segment-best on premium features or value for money.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
   - Available in multiple trims: LXi, VXi, ZXi, ZXi+, with both manual and AMT; CNG factory-fitted only in VXI Manual.
   - AMT and CNG options broaden appeal for city buyers and value-seekers.
   - ZXi Plus recommended for top features, but falls short vs rivals on equipment; CNG VXI suits high-mileage buyers.

12. VERDICT
   - The Maruti Suzuki Celerio is a highly practical, easy-to-drive urban hatchback delivering unmatched fuel economy and improved safety. It is best suited for first-time buyers or as a city runabout. Its appeal lies in low running costs, light weight, and daily comfort, but the price hike and omissions in feature content prevent it from being a clear value champion. Choose for efficiency, practicality, and safety, not for outright feature richness or premium feel. No rating score provided in review.

---

## REVIEW SUMMARY STRUCTURE

### 1. OVERVIEW
- Comprehensive off-roader available in multiple powertrains, body styles, and trims. Reviewers: CarWale, multiple automotive journalists.
- Stands as an icon reimagined; serious off-road capabilities with sophisticated features; unique design blending classic and modern elements.
- Road presence, customisability, go-anywhere ability, and ride quality are signature attributes.

### 2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
- Engines: Choice of strong four, six, and V8 engines, all with automatic (8-speed TC) and AWD.
- P300 2.0 petrol: Effortless everyday performance, smooth at low revs, snarly under hard acceleration, 0–100km/h in 7.4sec.
- D350 3.0 diesel: Smooth twin-turbo, immense torque (700Nm), 0–100km/h in 6.8sec.
- P635 4.4 V8: Ferocious acceleration, 0–100km/h in 4.0sec, dramatic exhaust note, dynamic driving transforms handling, but brakes lack bite under hard use.
- Off-road: Class-leading angles, air suspension, wade sensing for 900mm water crossings; advanced 4x4 system with multiple off-road modes; tackled all CarWale off-road tests with ease.
- Test results: 
  - Hill Descent (slowest = best): 41.97s (Defender, 1st)
  - 0–40m Gravel Acceleration: 4.50s (joint 2nd fastest)
  - Slalom: 13.97s (3rd, within half a second of G-Class)
  - Beaker Ride Quality: 420ml water remaining (2nd, only 10ml behind winner)
  - Timed Lap: 55.68s (3rd, 4s behind fastest)
- Ride comfort: Absorbent and plush, even on big wheels; well-damped air suspension, some thuds on sharp edges.
- Steering: Light, not highly precise, but agility from short wheelbase; body roll controlled (especially in Dynamic/V8 mode).
- Braking: V8's pedal feel described as "wooden" under heavy braking.
- Transmission: 8-speed auto smooth, but marginally slow to aggressive throttle.

### 3. EXTERIOR
- Design: Modern riff on rugged classic, squared lines, short overhangs, high ground clearance.
- Distinctive character: Available in two body types; Defender 90 is stubbier, 110 more practical.
- Details: Matte shades, black chrome, machined tow hooks (Octa), signature front/rear, unique safari roof windows.
- Segment-leading approach (38°), departure (40°), breakover (31°) angles.
- Strong road presence; not mistaken for any other SUV.

### 4. INTERIOR
- Cabin: Bold utilitarian design (rubber components, exposed bolts), soft-touch where needed, digital displays.
- Seating: 2nd row surprisingly roomy in 90, even better in 110; multiple seat layouts; 3rd row/boot usability varies by variant.
- Visibility: Excellent, thanks to large glass area and roof panels.
- Practicality: Storage ample (console box doubles as cooler, usable door bins, rear armrest with cupholders). Fixed rear windows and reduced cargo space on 90 version noted negatives.
- Configurable lighting, panoramic roof, safari windows.
- Military-inspired theme on Octa may underwhelm at the price.

### 5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
- Infotainment: Pivi Pro (large touchscreen), fast response, wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, Meridian audio.
- Digital cluster, wireless charging, configurable cabin lighting.
- Climate: Four-zone climate control standard.
- Advanced tech: ClearSight digital rearview; 360°+Ground View cameras, terrain response controls, multiple drive/off-road modes.
- Storage: Central console cooler box, ample USB ports.

### 6. SAFETY
- Euro NCAP 5-star rating.
- 6 airbags, electronic stability and roll control, ABS, emergency brake assist.
- ADAS: Adaptive cruise control, lane keep assist, hill descent control, all-terrain progress control.
- 360° camera (incl. Ground View), wade sensing, sturdy aluminium monocoque chassis.
- Some safety tech (ADAS) described as intrusive on regular roads.

### 7. FUEL ECONOMY

### 8. VALUE AND PRICING
- Pricing: Wide range depending on variant, powertrain, and trim; up to approx. ₹3 crore for Octa V8.
- Assessment: Expensive, especially higher-end/military-style interiors may not match expectations for luxury at this price point.
- Running costs: V8 maintenance/upkeep will be significant, but not quantified.
- Warranty/service: Not mentioned in review.

### 9. PROS AND CONS

**Pros:**
- Distinctive and commanding road presence.
- Very high off-road ability with advanced traction, wading, and suspension tech.
- Wide engine/powertrain choice, all with strong real-world performance.
- Comfortable and absorbent ride, especially compared to traditional off-roaders.
- Excellent glass area for bright, airy cabin and visibility.
- Leading off-road approach angles and water-wading depth.
- Broadly customisable via Land Rover options.
- Multiple body styles/trims for varied needs and budgets.
- Five-star Euro NCAP safety rating, full suite of ADAS.

**Cons:**
- Brakes (V8) lack power and feel under hard driving.
- City driving and parking cumbersome due to size.
- 3-door (90) version less practical for families/daily use; rear-seat access challenging, fixed rear windows.
- Interiors (esp. Octa/military theme) do not feel as luxurious as the price may suggest.
- High price for top models; maintenance on V8 version likely expensive.
- Some advanced safety/tech features can be intrusive or non-intuitive.
- Fewer novelty/novel tech features than cutting-edge rivals.

- Direct rivals: Mercedes-Benz G-Class (G-Wagon), Toyota Hilux, MG Gloster, Mahindra Thar, Maruti Suzuki Jimny (from off-road comparison).
- Strengths vs. competitors: Best hill descent (41.97s vs. next-best G-Wagon’s 29.5s), near fastest acceleration (0–40m 4.5s), competitive in slalom and beaker ride test.
- Unique selling points: Unmatched off-road electronics, blend of utility and modern luxury, huge wading depth, and segment-best ground clearance with air suspension.
- Weaknesses: Brake performance (V8), less raw luxury than G-Class at top price point. Gloster wins on comfort ride (beaker test); G-Wagon edges out on acceleration/slalom.

- Vast personalisation: Land Rover packages allow further custom tailoring for luxury or off-road use.

### 12. VERDICT
- The Defender remains a segment icon, adept at combining serious go-anywhere ability with refinement, comfort, and unique style.
- Best fit for buyers seeking a statement SUV with genuine off-roading prowess, plush ride, and a unique cabin environment—but who can compromise on interior luxury versus German luxury competitors at the top echelon.
- 90 variant is a lifestyle choice/weekend toy; 110 is the daily-friendly option.
- Not the most tech-laden or luxurious at the price, but none can match its off-road credentials, street presence, and customisability.

   Pros:

summary:
KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- Engine Options: 1.5L K15C four-cylinder petrol (102bhp/136Nm); factory-fitted CNG (K15C, 87bhp/121.5Nm in CNG mode, 100bhp/136Nm in petrol mode, CNG tank: 60L).
- Transmission: Five-speed manual or new six-speed torque converter automatic (AT includes paddle shifters, a first for Nexa/XL6); CNG variant manual only.
- Dimensions & Platform: Six-seater MPV, built on Suzuki’s TECT platform (lighter and up to 10% more torsional rigidity than predecessor).
- Suspension & Ride: Updated suspension for added weight; ride height increased with 16-inch alloy wheels (replacing 15-inch).
- Fuel Efficiency: Petrol manual 20.97kmpl (ARAI); petrol automatic 20.27kmpl (ARAI); CNG 26.32km/kg.
- Real-World Economy: Petrol AT returned 9.88kmpl (city), 22.50kmpl (highway), overall 13.03kmpl in independent test (start-stop disabled).
- Exterior Features: Redesigned front grille with chrome, smoked tail lights, roof-mounted spoiler, new dual-tone 16-inch alloy wheels, three dual-tone exterior shades plus signature colors (Nexa Blue, Grandeur Grey, Arctic White).
- Interior: All-black dashboard with soft-touch materials, contrast white seat stitching, faux-wood trim, premium roof lining; captain seats in second row with roof-mounted AC vents; adjustable and split-folding third-row seats; boot space 209L (up to 550L with third row folded flat).
- Technology: 7-inch or 9-inch SmartPlay Pro touchscreen infotainment system (varies by trim), wired Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, Suzuki Connect telematics (remote aircon, lock/unlock, live tracking, voice command), 360-degree camera, ventilated front seats, tyre pressure monitoring system (TPMS), front footwell lights, cooled cupholders.
- Practicality: Numerous small storage spaces, cooled bottle holders, 12V sockets in multiple rows, captain seat walkthrough access to third row, three-point seatbelts, sizeable cupholders.
- Safety: Four airbags (front, side), ESP, hill-hold assist, ABS with EBD, rear parking sensors, ISOFIX child seat anchors, Suzuki’s TECT platform (increased rigidity), TPMS, captain seats with one-touch recline and slide (no rear airbags), three-star Global NCAP (Ertiga reference), no direct XL6 crash test data.
- Variants: Four trims (entry Zeta, Alpha, Alpha+, others); CNG available only with Zeta trim; Alpha+ adds ventilated seats, 360-degree cam, cosmetic enhancements; leatherette seats and leather-wrapped steering from Alpha onwards.
- Warranty: Standard two years/40,000km (lower than rival Kia Carens’ three years/unlimited km).
- Price: Rs 11.29 – 14.55 lakh (ex-showroom for petrol); CNG Zeta at Rs 12.24 lakh; premium of Rs 1.3 lakh over petrol variant.
- Unique/Segment-Firsts: Paddle shifters (first for XL6/Nexa), 360-degree camera, cooled cupholders, ventilated seats, Suzuki Connect app.

---

REVIEW SUMMARY

1. OVERVIEW  
- Maruti Suzuki XL6 is a premium six-seater MPV, recently updated with a new engine, six-speed AT, cosmetic changes, added connectivity and safety features. Reviews from CarWale (Kapil Angane, Kaustubh Gandhi) and Hindi channels highlight improved practicality but incremental changes versus costlier price.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING  
- Engine: 1.5L K15C petrol (102bhp/136Nm); refined, silent at idle, responsive above 2000rpm, gets noisy >4500rpm.
- CNG engine: 87bhp/121.5Nm (CNG), 100bhp/136Nm (petrol).
- Transmission: New 6-speed torque converter AT (with paddle shifters), 5-speed manual; AT 15kg heavier than predecessor; seamless gearshifts, more responsive with paddles than in auto mode.
- Acceleration: Not quantified; described as brisk in manual; speed builds steady, not urgent in AT.
- Drivability: Good low-end torque; city driving is effortless; engine cruises at 2500–3000rpm at 100km/h.
- Ride & Handling: Revised suspension handles added weight; absorbs rough patches and bumps; remains flat on highway; slight body roll, light steering at low speed, predictable on highways.
- Braking: Satisfactory for daily and highway use; stopping distances not specified.

3. EXTERIOR  
- Freshened front with new mesh grille and thick chrome stripe, smoked LED tail lamps, roof-mounted spoiler, new 16-inch dual-tone machine-cut alloys (replacing 15-inch), chrome touches.  
- Dimensions: Large MPV, six-seater class.  
- Colour Options: Three dual-tone (Brave Khaki, Splendid Silver, Opulent) + Nexa Blue, Grandeur Grey, Arctic White.  
- Distinctive Design: Premium crossover styling sets it apart from Ertiga.

4. INTERIOR  
- Layout: All-black theme, soft-touch armrest, premium roof lining, faux-wood dash accents; not extensively changed from outgoing model; modern but not flashy.
- Seating: 6 seats (captain seats in second row), spacious and supportive seats, especially for middle row; large windows, decent third-row head/knee room, third row best for short journeys.
- Storage & Usability: Excellent practicality with cooled and regular bottle holders, storage slots, 12V sockets in all rows, split-fold/folding seatbacks, versatile for luggage and people.
- Boot: 209L (all rows up); up to 550L (third row folded); high loading lip is a minor issue.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES  
- Infotainment: 9-inch or 7-inch SmartPlay Pro touchscreen (trim-dependent), wired Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, improved interface.
- Connectivity: Upgraded Suzuki Connect app (remote aircon, lock/unlock, tracking, OTA updates, voice command), 360-degree camera (clear display), TPMS, cooled cupholders, ventilated front seats (Alpha+), cruise control, Smart key.
- User Experience: Smooth touchscreen, intuitive interface, all controls within reach; paddle shifters enhance driving engagement.
- Driver Assistance: 360-degree camera, parking sensors, hill-hold assist, ESP, TPMS.
- Notable Omissions: No wireless charging, sunroof, ambient lighting, air purifier, or drive modes (all found in some rivals).

6. SAFETY  
- Airbags: Four total (front, side); no rear passenger airbags.
- Ratings: Global NCAP 3 stars (Ertiga reference), XL6 not crash-tested directly.
- Structure: Suzuki TECT architecture (lighter, stiffer), additional safety claims.
- Features: ESP, hill-hold, ISOFIX, ABS/EBD, TPMS, parking sensors, rear camera; top trims add some features.
- Note: Some rivals offer six airbags and additional safety for rear passengers.

7. FUEL ECONOMY  
- Claimed (ARAI): Petrol manual 20.97kmpl; petrol AT 20.27kmpl; CNG 26.32km/kg.
- Real-World (CarWale): Petrol AT 9.88kmpl (city), 22.5kmpl (highway), combined 13.03kmpl.
- CNG Range: 60L tank (actual boot space use unspecified).
- Segment Comparison: On par with MPV rivals for petrol; CNG competitive for cost-focused buyers.

8. VALUE AND PRICING  
- Price: Rs 11.29–14.55 lakh (petrol); CNG Zeta Rs 12.24 lakh; CNG premium Rs 1.3 lakh over petrol.
- Value Assessment: Premium justified by features (six-speed AT, ventilated seats, 360 cam) but interior and exterior changes are limited for the price hike; some features missing versus price.
- Warranty: Two years/40,000km—less than Kia Carens (three years/unlimited km).
- Maintenance: Service intervals not mentioned.

9. PROS AND CONS  
Pros:
- Practical, easy to live with.
- Excellent second-row comfort (captain seats, spacious).
- Smooth, refined engine; seamless AT; paddle shifters.
- Well-equipped (360 cam, cooled cupholders, ventilated seats, Suzuki Connect).
- Good ride quality; easy storage usability.
- Nexa aftersales network.

Cons:
- Incremental design/interior upgrades for a major price jump.
- Missing features: Wireless charger, sunroof, six airbags, ambient lighting.
- Only four airbags; rear passenger protection limited.
- Top variants costly; CNG only in entry trim.
- Fit/finish inconsistent in places.
- Rides less flat at high speed on bad roads; some engine noise at high rpm.

10. COMPETITORS  
- Direct rivals: Kia Carens, Mahindra Marazzo, Toyota Innova Crysta.
- Compared to Kia Carens: Kia offers six airbags, sunroof, wireless charger, longer warranty, but XL6 matches on practical comfort, storage, and now drivetrain tech (AT+ paddle shifters).
- Unique Selling Propositions: Paddle shifters, ventilated seats, 360 cam, Nexa experience, CNG in premium MPV.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT  
- Four trims: Zeta (entry, only CNG option), Alpha, Alpha+ (top; ventilated seats, 360 cam, leatherette, cosmetic upgrades).
- Leather-wrapped steering, leatherette from Alpha up.
- CNG option not available in higher trims, so buyers miss some features if opting for CNG.
- Recommended variant not explicitly stated in review.

12. VERDICT  
- The updated XL6 builds on its core strengths of practicality, comfort, and driveability, while new six-speed AT and added features address key rivals. Lacks extensive upgrades or certain important features for the price jump, yet remains a strong, user-friendly family MPV, especially for those valuing comfort and practicality over flashiness or max equipment. Suited for buyers seeking a refined, reliable, and comfortable six-seater with modern essentials, now with the option of CNG for economy-focused users. No explicit rating score provided in reviews.
model_summary: Ideal for families needing spacious, comfortable six-seater practicality, refined petrol/CNG options, smooth automatic, captain seats, 360° camera, ventilated seats.

summary:
### KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- **Engine Options**: 1.5-litre K15C dual-jet, dual VVT petrol (103 bhp, 138 Nm); K15C S-CNG (87 bhp, 121 Nm).
- **Smart Hybrid System**: Available on petrol (assists torque and auto start-stop); not on CNG.
- **Gearbox Choices**: 5-speed manual standard; new 6-speed torque converter automatic with paddle shifters available (first on Maruti Suzuki Arena vehicles); no automatic for CNG variant.
- **Fuel Types**: Petrol; CNG (switchable via button while driving).
- **Claimed Mileage**: Petrol MT 20.51 kmpl; Petrol AT 20.3 kmpl; CNG 26.11 km/kg (real-world: 22.41 km/kg, city 18.01 km/kg, highway 35.6 km/kg).
- **Seating**: 7-seater with split-fold (60:40 2nd row, 50:50 3rd row), adjustable headrests on all rows, all rows claimed comfortable for adults.
- **Boot Space**: 209 litres with all seats up; up to 550 litres with 3rd row folded; further reduced by 80-100 litres in CNG due to tank.
- **Trims/Variants**: LXi, VXi, ZXi, ZXi+; CNG available in VXi and ZXi; Tour M for commercial use (petrol and CNG manual only).
- **Infotainment**: 7-inch SmartPlay Pro touchscreen with voice commands (“Hi Suzuki”), wireless Android Auto & Apple CarPlay, Suzuki Connect with 40+ telematics, smartwatch/Alexa compatibility.
- **Convenience Features**: Cooled cupholders, power windows, remote keyless entry, push-button start, armrests, roof-mounted 2nd-row AC vents, cruise control (ZXi+), one-touch driver window.
- **Wheels**: New 15-inch dual-tone machined alloy wheels (ZXi/ZXi+), standard 15-inch steel (lower trims).
- **Exterior Highlights**: Chrome wing garnish on grille, chrome boot strip, LED tail lamps, projector headlamps, six colour choices (Magma Grey, Pearl Arctic White, Oxford Blue, Auburn Red, Splendid Silver, Dignity Brown).
- **Interior Finish**: Beige upholstery, metallic teak-wood dash trim, chrome cabin highlights.
- **Driver Display**: Digital cluster with special CNG graphics, timer for CNG use, fuel distribution pie chart.
- **Safety**: Dual airbags standard, four airbags (ZXi+), ABS with EBD, brake assist, ESP/hill-hold (AT only), ISOFIX, rear parking sensors standard, rear camera (ZXi+), front seatbelt height adjustment, high-speed alert, speed-sensitive auto lock.
- **Service Network**: Supported by extensive Maruti Suzuki network.
- **Unique Selling Points**: First six-speed auto/paddle shifters for Arena models, widest 7-seat/CNG combo in segment.

---

### REVIEW SUMMARY

#### 1. OVERVIEW
- Assessment: The Ertiga update maintains its family-focused, value-packed, and frugal nature, now improved with dual-jet tech, a modern automatic gearbox, richer connectivity features, and a wider CNG range. Review by CarWale (Kaustubh Gandhi).
- Model: Maruti Suzuki Ertiga

#### 2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
- Petrol: 1.5-litre (1462 cc) dual-jet dual-VVT K15C, 103 bhp at ~6000 rpm, 138 Nm at ~4400 rpm.
- CNG: 87 bhp at 5500 rpm, 121 Nm at 4200 rpm; no hybrid.
- Transmission: 5-speed manual (standard), new 6-speed torque converter automatic with paddle shifters (petrol only).
- Acceleration: Not specified.
- Drive experience: Light steering, easy visibility, smooth and adequate performance in both petrol and CNG, but encourages sedate driving style.
- Ride quality: Softer, absorbent over bumps, slightly vertical movement at speed but remains comfortable; suspension revised for CNG weight increase.
- Braking: ABS with EBD and brake assist standard, performance not quantified.
- NVH: Not mentioned in review.

#### 3. EXTERIOR
- Style: Unchanged silhouette, mild updates; chrome wing garnish, chrome boot-lid strip, sharper creases.
- Wheels: New 15-inch dual-tone machined alloys (ZXi and above).
- Lights: Projector headlamps standard, LED tail lamps, fog lamps on ZXi/ZXi+.
- Colors: Six options, including new Splendid Silver, Dignity Brown.
- Size Segment: Compact MPV.
- CNG cues: Subtle, only external CNG sticker/rear fuel port.

#### 4. INTERIOR
- Design: Three-row, beige theme with wood-effect dash, chrome detailing.
- Seat comfort: Large, cushioned, supportive for long-distance, flexible 2nd row, adequate 3rd row space for adults.
- Practicality: Light controls, great visibility, abundant storage areas; 3rd row access restricted (narrow entry, cumbersome seat-folding).
- Cargo: 209L (all seats), ~550L (3rd row folded); CNG tank significantly cuts boot space, pronounced intrusive hump; no official roof box option.

#### 5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
- Infotainment: 7-inch SmartPlay Pro (ZXi+), SmartPlay Studio (lower); voice commands, wireless Android Auto/Apple CarPlay.
- Suzuki Connect: 40+ telematics (vehicle status, security, remote ops, air-con activation, Alexa).
- Instrumentation: Digital driver’s display with CNG specifics, timer, fuel charts.
- Convenience: Push-button start/stop, auto climate, rear-view camera (ZXi+), cruise control (ZXi+), auto headlamps (ZXi+), cooled cup holders, roof AC vents, one-touch window, electrically adjustable/foldable ORVMs, steering-mounted controls.
- Second- and third-row Split/fold seats, sliding/reclining second row, armrests.
- Missing: No factory-fitted reverse camera for lower trims.

#### 6. SAFETY
- Airbags: Dual front airbags standard; four airbags (ZXi+).
- Brakes: ABS, EBD, brake assist standard.
- Assist Systems: ESP and hill-hold on automatics.
- Child safety: ISOFIX anchorages.
- Parking: Rear parking sensors standard, rear camera (ZXi+).
- Other: Front seatbelt height adjust, high-speed alert, speed-sensing door locks.
- Crash Ratings: One-star GNCAP (safety rating below class average).
- Noteworthy: Safety equipment comprehensive for price, but overall crash integrity weak.

#### 7. FUEL ECONOMY
- Petrol MT: 20.51 kmpl (claimed).
- Petrol AT: 20.3 kmpl (claimed).
- CNG: 26.11 km/kg (claimed); 22.41 km/kg (overall tested), 18.01 km/kg (city), 35.6 km/kg (highway).
- Running cost (Mumbai): CNG Rs 3.3/km vs. petrol Rs 5.43/km.
- Fuel tank: CNG tank holds 9kg, ~202km CNG-only range observed.
- Segment comparison: Best/only seven-seat CNG MPV offering at this price.

#### 8. VALUE AND PRICING
- Pricing (ex-showroom): LXi Rs 8.35 lakh; VXi Rs 9.49–10.99 lakh; ZXi Rs 10.59–12.09 lakh; ZXi+ Rs 11.29 lakh (MT), Rs 12.79 lakh (AT); CNG VXi Rs 10.44l, ZXi Rs 11.54l; Tour M (fleet) Rs 9.46–10.41 lakh.
- Value: Strong on features for MPV price band, unbeatable fuel efficiency (CNG), highly practical everyday/fleet choice.
- Warranty, Service: Not specified, but benefits from Maruti’s strong aftersales.
- Maintenance: Not detailed in review.

#### 9. PROS AND CONS

**Pros:**
- Frugal, efficient petrol and CNG engine.
- Smooth automatic with paddle shifters.
- Very practical three-row seating; comfortable, spacious cabin.
- Easy to drive, light controls, good outward visibility.
- Connected tech, robust infotainment (voice, Alexa, wireless CarPlay/Android Auto).
- CNG/petrol switchable while running; real-world savings.
- Strong feature set for money (wireless tech, cruise, more airbags in top trims).
- Maruti’s strong resale and service support.

**Cons:**
- Only one-star GNCAP safety rating; weak crash integrity.
- Boot space heavily compromised in 7-seat and more so in CNG variant.
- Third-row access is a pain (narrow/awkward).
- Dashboard, lower plastics feeling dated/subpar.
- Uninspiring MPV silhouette for some tastes.
- No factory-fitted camera on lower trims, missing some modern conveniences.
- No AT option for CNG.

#### 10. COMPETITORS
- Direct rivals: No seven-seat CNG alternatives in price band.
- Indirect: 5-seat CNG hatchbacks and sedans (Maruti, Hyundai, Tata) for lower budgets.
- Strengths vs. rivals: Only affordable three-row MPV on CNG, best for taxi/fleet/multi-family use.
- Weaknesses: Safety weaker than some newer rivals (notable one-star rating); MPV styling more utilitarian.

#### 11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
- Lineup: LXi, VXi (petrol/CNG), ZXi (petrol/CNG), ZXi+ (petrol only), Tour M (fleet).
- Features: Higher trims (ZXi+) add auto headlamps, 4 airbags, cruise, reverse camera, SmartPlay Pro; CNG now available in ZXi not just VXi.
- Transmission: AT only on petrol VXi+, ZXi, ZXi+; CNG only manual.
- Recommendation: ZXi+ for families (feature-rich), VXi/ZXi CNG for efficiency-focused/fleet buyers.

#### 12. VERDICT
- Summary: The Ertiga remains India’s most sensible, value-oriented family MPV. Updates modernize drivetrain, tech, and connectivity, while space, practicality, and running cost stay segment-leading (especially in CNG form). Safety remains a concern but, for those who prioritise practicality, cost, and seating, it is unmatched in the segment.
- Suitability: Ideal for large families, taxi/fleet operators, and anyone needing maximum value, efficiency, and seating at a sensible price.
- Rating Score: Not provided in review.
model_summary: Spacious, efficient 7-seater ideal for families and fleets; petrol/CNG options, smooth automatic, strong features, but weak crash safety.

summary:
MAHINDRA THAR ROXX – STRUCTURED EXPERT REVIEW

---

KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- Form Factor: Five-door body, substantially longer, wider, and more spacious than the standard Thar; enhanced practicality with increased rear seat and boot space.
- Chassis and Underpinnings: Built on the Scorpio N's chassis and suspension; rugged body-on-frame platform for high durability and off-road capability.
- Powertrains: 
  - Diesel: 2.2-litre 4-cyl mHawk turbocharged, 150bhp/330Nm (manual) or 172bhp/370Nm (6-speed torque converter automatic).
  - Petrol: 2.0-litre 4-cyl turbo mStallion, 150bhp/330Nm (manual), 160bhp/330Nm (manual), 174bhp/380Nm (automatic).
- Transmission: Six-speed manual and six-speed automatic (torque converter); 4x4 offered only with diesel variants.
- Off-road Credentials: 4XPLOR terrain modes (Snow, Mud, Sand), Crawl Smart (auto throttle for obstacles), IntelliTurn (tight U-turns), 650mm water-wading depth, 41.7-degree approach, 36.1-degree departure angles.
- Comfort & Convenience: Panoramic electric sunroof, electrically adjustable and cooled driver’s seat, ventilated front seats, 60:40 split-folding and reclining rear bench, dedicated rear air-con vents, central armrest with cupholders, cooled glovebox, wireless charging pad.
- Infotainment & Connectivity: Twin 10.25-inch displays (infotainment and instrumentation), wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay (pending update), nine-speaker Harman Kardon system, voice commands, AdrenoX connected tech, Alexa built-in.
- Safety: Six airbags, ABS with EBD, ESP, traction control, hill hold & descent, Level 2 ADAS (adaptive cruise, FCW, autonomous emergency braking), tyre pressure monitoring, 360-degree camera with blind view, front/rear parking sensors, rear disc brakes, three-point seatbelts for all seats.
- Boot Space & Cabin: Large usable boot, improved shoulder/knee room in second row, metal roof for insulation, practical interior storage.
- Exterior Highlights: Six-slot grille unique to Roxx, C-shaped LED DRLs, projector headlamps, 19-inch chunky tyres, boxy silhouette with metal roof, angled C-pillar housing rear door handle, sideways opening boot lid, vertical opening rear windscreen.
- Additional Features: Auto-dimming IRVM, soft-touch materials, upgraded fit & finish, steering wheel from XUV700, upmarket dashboard and trim.
- Seating: Officially five seats, supportive large rear bench with recline, reasonable thigh support.
- Limitations: No paddle shifters on automatic, no petrol 4x4, some ergonomic issues with front seat support and rear headrest alignment.
- Notable Segment Differentiators: Only ladder-frame 4x4 SUV in class with such feature spread, family focus without losing Thar’s off-road essence.

---

REVIEW SUMMARY

1. OVERVIEW
   - The Mahindra Thar Roxx is positioned as a larger, more practical, and feature-loaded five-door alternative to the regular Thar, targeting buyers needing family usability without compromising on off-road chops. Review sources: CarWale, reviewer: multiple contributors.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
   - Engine:
     - Diesel: 2.2L, 4-cyl, 150bhp/330Nm (manual), 172bhp/370Nm (auto).
     - Petrol: 2.0L, 4-cyl, up to 174bhp/380Nm (auto).
   - Transmission: Six-speed manual or six-speed torque converter automatic; auto is smooth, fast, and intuitive but lacks paddle shifters.
   - Acceleration: Not explicitly quantified; described as light on its feet, brisk overtakes, strong low- and mid-range torque.
   - Highway: Effortless triple-digit cruising (120+ km/h), but wind noise above 100 km/h; most efficient at 95-100 km/h.
   - City: Light, quick electrically-assisted steering, easy low-speed maneuvers; effortless parking/U-turns; good visibility.
   - Handling: Good straight-line stability, impressive under hard braking, tracks well on highways; steering feels dead and heavy at high speed, constant corrections required.
   - Ride: Firm at low speed (jiggle, harsh over bumps/potholes), flattens at higher speeds but bouncy on undulations; rear passengers may find ride unsettled.
   - Braking: Strong bite, progressive feel, inspires confidence; brake pedal travel is long before engagement.
   - Off-road: Excellent 4x4 chops with Crawl Smart, IntelliTurn, terrain modes; high water-wading and approach/departure angles.

3. EXTERIOR
   - Design: Rugged, boxy SUV stance, extended five-door form; unique six-slot grille, C-shaped LED DRLs, LED projector headlamps, 19-inch wheels.
   - Roof: Full metal, improved insulation, optional panoramic sunroof.
   - Functional: Angled C-pillar (doors), sideways opening bootlid with externally-mounted spare, vertical-opening rear windscreen.
   - Road Presence: Substantial size, commanding stance—stands out among rivals.
   - Dimensions/Color: Not numerically specified; described as larger in all directions.
   - Notable Styling: Upgraded, aggressive details designed to attract family SUV buyers alongside adventure-seekers.

4. INTERIOR
   - Quality: Significant improvement over Thar 3-door; soft-touch, upmarket materials, fit and finish on par with pricier SUVs.
   - Space: Markedly more shoulder and knee room, especially second row; rear headroom tight for 6ft+ passengers; boot roomy and practical.
   - Seating: Five seats, supportive 60:40 split reclining rear bench with armrest/cupholders; front seats ventilated but lack thigh support for long drives; middle rear headrest misaligned.
   - Storage/Practicality: Abundant interior storage, cooled glovebox, large central armrest; utility elements with a comfortable, lifestyle twist.
   - Rear: Dedicated air vents, ample cushioning, bolstering; large boot for family/luggage.
   - Ergonomics: Some front seat support shortfalls; beige upholstery prone to soiling after off-road use.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
   - Displays: Twin 10.25-inch screens for infotainment/instruments as standard on higher trims.
   - Infotainment: Harman Kardon nine-speaker system, voice commands, AdrenoX and Alexa integration.
   - Connectivity: Wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay (pending update for CarPlay), wireless charging, USB ports.
   - Driver Assistance: Level 2 ADAS (adaptive cruise, AEB, FCW), 360-degree camera with blind view, parking sensors front/rear, tyre pressure monitoring.
   - Cabin Tech: Keyless start (no keyless entry), digital climate control, powered and cooled seats, cooled glovebox, rear AC vents, auto-dimming IRVM.
   - User Experience: Setup regarded as modern, competitive with segment best; some user interface updates pending.

6. SAFETY
   - Airbags: Six airbags across range.
   - Active: ESP, ABS with EBD, traction control, hill hold/descent, TCS, three-point seatbelts all seats, rear disc brakes.
   - Passive: High-strength frame (Scorpio N derivatives), expected to score high in BNCAP tests; no official crash test rating yet.
   - ADAS: Included in top trims—autonomous emergency braking, FCW, adaptive cruise with stop-and-go.
   - Others: TPMS, auto-dimming mirror, 360-degree camera, front/rear parking sensors.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
   - Official Figures: Not provided.
   - Real World: Diesel 4x4 struggles to touch 10 km/l city; both petrol/diesel return ~15 km/l highway; FE drops notably at sustained high speed above 100 km/h.
   - Comparison: Jimny (petrol 4x4 rival) returns over 12 km/l city, better than Thar Roxx diesel.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
   - Price Range: Not numerically specified in review.
   - Value: Priced higher than rivals like Jimny, but offers more features, stronger engine, genuine five-seat layout, and off-road capability; more affordable vs. seven-seat Scorpio N with richer equipment.
   - Warranty, Maintenance: Not mentioned in review.

9. PROS AND CONS

   - Pros:
     - Practical five-door layout, genuine five-seater, big boot, improved insulation.
     - Strong, refined diesel and petrol engines; 4x4 with terrain modes, impressive off-road hardware.
     - Upmarket interior, high-grade features (sunroof, 360-cam, powered/ventilated/seated/cooled seats).
     - Advanced safety and ADAS tech.
     - Commanding road presence, rugged iconic style.
     - Intuitive automatic transmission, city-friendly steering, comfortable highway performance.
     - Significant space/comfort improvement for families.

   - Cons:
     - Firm and unsettled ride at low speed or on rough/undulating roads.
     - Steering heavy and uncommunicative at high speed.
     - Noise intrusion (wind) above 100 km/h.
     - Rear headroom marginal for 6'+, middle headrest poorly aligned, front seat thigh support lacking.
     - Petrol 4x4 unavailable, diesel 4x4 only; FE weaker than monocoque competitors.
     - Brake pedal long travel, no paddle shifters.
     - Not as refined or dynamically polished as crossover SUVs (Creta/Nexon).

10. COMPETITORS
    - Mentioned Rivals: Maruti Suzuki Jimny (4x4), Hyundai Creta, Tata Nexon, Kia Carens (seven-seater SUV/MPV niche).
    - Strengths vs. Competitors: Greater space, more modern features, authentic 4x4 hardware against Jimny; better as a family SUV vs. three-door Thar; more off-road and feature-rich vs. monocoque crossovers.
    - Weaknesses: Not as cheap, fuel-efficient, or refined as Jimny (esp. at retail price); on-road comfort, finesse, and economy lag behind Creta/Nexon; petrol-4x4 flexibility missing.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
    - Range: Multiple trims, diesel/petrol options, 4x4 with diesel only.
    - Key Features by Variant: Base trim well equipped (keyless start, climate control), top AX7 L adds ADAS, 360-cam, panoramic sunroof, powered/cooled seats, premium infotainment.
    - Recommendation: Diesel 4x4 top-spec (AX7 L) considered best for buyers wanting all features and genuine off-road ability; petrol 4x2 for those not needing 4x4.
    - Noted: Buyers must clarify fuel and drivetrain priority due to limited combinations.

12. VERDICT
    - The Mahindra Thar Roxx is an ideal choice for those wanting a bold, family-friendly, feature-rich, and genuinely off-road-capable SUV. Excels in practicality, comfort, and technology compared to its three-door sibling, but can’t fully match the polish, ride comfort, or efficiency of crossovers. Best for buyers who need ruggedness, space, and all-weather, all-terrain ability. Pros:

- User-friendly handling, easy urban maneuvering.

summary:
KIA SONET REVIEW SUMMARY

---

### KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- **Engine Options:**
  - 1.0-litre turbo-petrol, 998cc, 118 bhp @ 6000 rpm, 172 Nm @ 1500 rpm; available with six-speed iMT or seven-speed DCT
  - 1.2-litre naturally aspirated petrol, 82 bhp, 115 Nm; five-speed manual only
  - 1.5-litre turbo-diesel, 1493cc, 114 bhp @ 4000 rpm, 250 Nm @ 1500 rpm; six-speed manual, six-speed iMT, six-speed automatic

- **Transmission:**
  - Six-speed iMT (clutchless manual)
  - Six-speed manual
  - Six-speed automatic (diesel)
  - Seven-speed DCT automatic (turbo petrol)

- **Standout Features:**
  - iMT clutchless manual technology: combines manual gear selection with automatic clutch operation, improving city convenience
  - Level 1 ADAS including forward collision warning/avoidance (car, pedestrian, cyclist), lane keep assist
  - Six airbags, electronic stability control, vehicle stability management, hill-start assist, blind-view monitor, disc brakes on all wheels, 360-degree camera, front/rear parking sensors, three-point seatbelts all seats
  - 10.25-inch touchscreen infotainment, digital instrument cluster, Alexa connectivity, connected car suite (Find My Car, remote ops)
  - Air purifier with virus/bacteria protection, LED ambient lighting, seven-speaker Bose sound system

  - Eight monotone and two dual-tone color options, plus unique X-Line colorways
  - 16-inch crystal-cut alloys, signature tiger-nose grille, LED headlamps/DRLs/taillamps, rear skid plates, roof-integrated spoiler

- **Dimensions/Space:**
  - Compact SUV (< 4m), competitive cabin and boot space
  - Rear more comfortable for two adults; shoulder room limited for three; second row tight for tall passengers

- **Notable Tech Omissions:**
  - No soft-touch interior materials, no steering reach adjustment, no illuminated window switches, no auto wipers (at any trim), misses full-sized spare

---

### REVIEW SUMMARY STRUCTURE

#### 1. OVERVIEW
- Kia Sonet, reviewed by CarWale, evaluated as a refreshed, feature-rich compact SUV in diesel iMT HTX+ trim.
- Segment benchmark for features, technology, and powertrain options.
- Praised for premium interior, packed features, broad engine and variant choices.

#### 2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
- Diesel: 1.5L, 114 bhp/250 Nm; iMT delivers manual-like control without clutch pedal; six-speed manual and auto available.
- Petrol: 1.0T, 118 bhp/172 Nm; responsive, strong mid-range, DCT smooth with rapid shifts, iMT offers engagement with ease.
- 1.2 NA petrol: 82 bhp/115 Nm for budget/conservative buyers.
- City: Diesel iMT seamless in start-stop, reduces fatigue, minor steering heaviness vs. petrol, good fuel economy in hard urban use (12-15 kmpl indicated).
- Highway: Diesel iMT excels; strong midrange, low cabin noise at 80-100 km/h, high speed stability praised.
- 0-100 km/h and specific performance metrics: Not mentioned in review.
- Braking: Reassuring, all-wheel discs standard.
- Ride/Handling: Firmer suspension, bouncy at slow speed or over speed breakers, improves at highway speed; well-weighted, precise steering inspires confidence.
- Transmission: DCT (petrol turbo) noted for smooth, fast shifts but slight delay when reversing; iMT clutchless manual deemed highly convenient.

#### 3. EXTERIOR
- Compact SUV segment, modern styling.
- Signature tiger-nose grille, “star map” LED headlamps, sleek LED foglamps, LED-connected tail lamps.
- 16-inch crystal-cut alloys, metallic-accented rear skid plate, rear spoiler.
- Eight monotone colors: Pewter Olive, Intense Red, Imperial Blue, Sparkling Silver, Gravity Grey, Aurora Black Pearl, Clear White, Glacier White Pearl. Two dual-tone: Intense Red/Glacier White Pearl with black roof; X-Line: Aurora Black Pearl, Xclusive Matte Graphite.
- Strong visual presence, updated design to match rivals.

#### 4. INTERIOR
- Premium, upmarket impression; dual-tone and variant-specific color/trim options.
- Digital driver display, 10.25-inch infotainment, tactile switches, chunky steering wheel.
- Front ventilated seats, electric driver seat, sunroof, leatherette upholstery (varies by variant); blends comfort and luxury.
- Second row: Best for two adults, tight shoulder room and space for three adults; legroom/depth adequate if not generous, especially for tall passengers.
- Practical features: folding rear armrest with cup holders, USB charging, multiple storage spaces.
- Boot: 385 litres, easily augmented by split-folding rear seat.

#### 5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
- 10.25-inch touchscreen infotainment, digital instrument cluster, Alexa voice commands, connected car features (remote climate, Find My Car, tyre pressure).
- Seven-speaker Bose audio system; exceptional sound quality.
- Air purifier (virus/bacteria), ambient LED lighting, cooled/ventilated seats.
- 360-degree camera, front/rear parking sensors, blind-view monitor, rear camera (clear/responsive).
- Sunroof, keyless entry, cruise control (feature set varies by trim).
- Omissions: steering reach adjustment, auto wipers, illuminated window switches, full-sized spare wheel.

#### 6. SAFETY
- Six airbags standard, electronic stability control, vehicle stability management, hill-start assist.
- Blind-view monitor, front/rear parking sensors, all disc brakes, 360-degree camera, three-point seatbelts all seats.
- Level 1 ADAS available: forward collision warning/avoidance (car, pedestrian, cyclist), lane keep assist.
- Safety rating: Not tested by NCAP; thus, no official rating yet.

#### 7. FUEL ECONOMY
- Diesel urban real-world: 12-15 kmpl indicated (hard city duty); 18-19 kmpl achieved on highways; translates to range of 600-700km per tank in mixed driving.
- Turbo-petrol DCT: ARAI claimed 19.2 kmpl, competitive for segment.
- 1.2 petrol: Not mentioned.
- Segment comparison: Diesel efficiency especially strong for long-distance, frequent usage.

#### 8. VALUE AND PRICING
- Tested variant (HTX+ diesel iMT): Rs. 14.60 to 16.66 lakh OTR Mumbai, depending on report.
- Value: Strong feature count justifies price; premium vs. hatchbacks offset by engagement, frugality, highway ability, and equipment.
- Warranty, service costs: Not mentioned in review.

#### 9. PROS AND CONS

**Pros:**
- Segment-leading feature list, many normally reserved for higher-priced SUVs
- Superb engine/transmission combos; especially diesel iMT and turbo-petrol DCT
- High fuel efficiency for diesel in both city and highway use
- Standout premium interior, exceptional comfort and tech
- Standard six airbags, electronic aids, available ADAS safety; strong safety suite
- Smooth and refined driving, minimal engine noise at cruise
- Strong connectivity, entertainment, and upmarket cabin experience

**Cons:**
- Rear seat best for two; shoulder and legroom tight for three or tall adults
- Ride quality firm at low speeds; bouncy over poor surfaces, settles at speed
- Visibility: thick C-pillars create noticeable blind spots
- Some practical omissions: no soft-touch dashboard/interior parts, steering reach, illuminated switches, auto wipers, full-size spare
- No official safety rating (NCAP) at time of review
- DCT gearbox: occasional delay in reverse
- Some view pricing as high for the space actual offered (hatchback-like rear room)

#### 10. COMPETITORS
- Direct rivals: Not explicitly named, but competitive set includes Hyundai Venue, Tata Nexon, Maruti Brezza, Mahindra XUV300.
- Strengths vs. rivals: Best-in-segment features, multiple powertrains, premium interior, advanced safety, standout design.
- Weaknesses: Rear seat space below some rivals, slightly firmer ride.
- Unique selling points: Diesel-iMT combo (uncommon), Level 1 ADAS, Bose audio, fully loaded trims, multiple color/trim choices.

#### 11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
- Wide range of variants, multiple petrol/diesel/manual/automatic configurations.
- Top trims (HTX+, GT-Line, X-Line) include most luxury/features/safety tech.
- X-Line offers exclusive exterior/interior treatment.
- Recommended: HTX+ diesel iMT for best blend of daily use economy, equipment, and convenience.

#### 12. VERDICT
- Kia Sonet is a feature-loaded, premium-feeling compact SUV with efficient, powerful engines, and a user-friendly, tech-rich cabin.
- Stands out in feature count, interior feel, tech integration, and safety gear; rear-seat compromises and firmer ride are noted but not deal-breakers.
- Exceptionally well-suited for urban families, frequent travelers, tech-focused buyers, or those wanting a diesel with clutchless convenience.
- Justifies higher price over hatchbacks with equipment, refinement, safety, and flexibility; especially value in diesel iMT or turbo DCT trims.
- Highly recommended in the segment for buyers prioritizing features, tech, and sophistication. Rating score: Not mentioned in review.

   - Engine: 2.5-litre, four-cylinder hybrid petrol; up to 227bhp and 221Nm (petrol), electric motor supplementing to claimed combined output.

   - Handling: Linear, smooth power delivery; soft yet composed suspension prioritizes comfort; maintains composure in corners; light steering at low speeds, firms up at highway velocity; 2.5 steering turns lock-to-lock enable simple manoeuvring.
   - Ride Quality: Comfort-oriented; absorbs rough surfaces well; refined NVH, petrol engine audible under heavy acceleration only.
   - Braking: Not detailed in review.
   - Transmission: e-CVT automatic; seamless shifts; front-wheel drive; responsive for city and highway needs.

3. EXTERIOR
   - Standout styling: Sleek, radical with clean lines, new diamond-cut alloys, all-LED headlights/DRLs and taillights; C-shaped lighting motifs; inspired by Lexus models; sporty bumpers.
   - Dimensions: Not specified; described as large/executive sedan.
   - Colors: Not mentioned.
   - Distinctive design cues: Arrow-like taillights; black roof/body kit for Sprint Edition.

4. INTERIOR
   - Material Quality: Soft-touch elements on dashboard, doors, and seats; some grainy/plastic sections detract from perceived luxury.
   - Space: Exceptionally roomy rear with ample legroom and headroom; slightly tight shoulder room; jumbo boot (not quantified).
   - Comfort: Powered, ventilated, 10-way adjustable front seats; rear seat electric backrest, recline, armrest media/climate controls.
   - Practicality: Armrest has cup holders, rich storage options lacking (e.g., no wireless charger/storage in rear armrest); five USB-C ports, but no USB-A.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
   - Infotainment: 12.3-inch touchscreen, 12.3-inch digital cluster; fast, modern UI.
   - Connectivity: Wireless Apple CarPlay, Android Auto (wireless Android Auto inconsistent in review: available in one section, missing in another); five USB-C charging ports.
   - User Interface: Slick, responsive touchscreen; all controls easy to reach and intuitive.
   - Driver Assistance: Level-2 ADAS (lane departure, adaptive cruise, auto high beam); 360-degree camera; heads-up display.
   - Additional Tech: Keyless entry, electric sunroof (not panoramic), three drive modes, EPB, TPMS, memory driver seat, three-zone climate.

6. SAFETY
   - Safety Ratings: Five-star Global NCAP.
   - Standard Equipment: Nine airbags, ABS with EBD, seatbelt reminders, speed alert, TPMS.
   - Optional/Advanced: 360-degree camera, Level-2 ADAS suite, rear seat ISOFIX (not mentioned, assumed standard).
   - Innovations: Rear seat safety features extensive, especially for segment.

   - Comparison: Among most efficient in class, segment-leading hybrid numbers.

   - Value: High on comfort, tech, and efficiency; considered expensive for segment, but reliability and feature list justify most of premium; some plastics/feature omissions detract at this price.

9. PROS AND CONS
   - Pros: Exceptionally smooth ride; hybrid efficiency; rear seat comfort and features; loaded cabin tech; feature count (ADAS, entertainment, multi-zone climate); five-star safety; bullet-proof reliability reputation.
   - Cons: Expensive; missing some segment expectations—panoramic sunroof, wireless Android Auto (noted as inconsistent), no USB-A ports, some hard plastics inside; storage limitations rear seat; familiar styling inside (not radical like exterior).

10. COMPETITORS
    - Mentioned: Skoda Superb, Mercedes-Benz A-Class Limousine, BMW 2 Series Gran Coupe.
    - Strengths: Hybrid efficiency, expansive space, rear-seat focus, Toyota reliability.

KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- Parallel hybrid powertrain: 3.0L V6 petrol engine (340 bhp) plus electric motor; combined output 462 bhp and over 700 Nm torque, enabling high efficiency and strong performance for the segment.
- Pure electric driving mode (E-Power): EV-only range up to 44 km; starts in electric mode by default – ideal for city commutes, silent operation at low speeds.
- 8-speed Tiptronic S automatic transmission: recalibrated for hybrid use, powers all four wheels; enhances drivability and performance response.
- Adaptive air suspension: continuously adjusts to road conditions for improved ride quality, especially beneficial with standard 19-inch or optional 20-inch wheels.
- Dynamic drive modes: Hybrid, Sport, Sport Plus – full battery energy boost available in sportier modes for sharper throttle response.
- Standard features: Sport Chrono Package, panoramic roof, LED headlights, four-zone climate control, 8-way electrically adjustable front seats, front/side/curtain/knee airbags, front/rear park assist, Apple CarPlay, powered tailgate, semi-digital instrument cluster.
- Generous interior space: high seating position, excellent visibility, supportive long seatbacks/bases in both rows.
- Big boot: highlighted as a strong practicality point compared to rivals.
- Expansive options list (at extra cost): 20-inch sport wheels (Rs 3.80 lakh), Bose surround system (Rs 2.67 lakh), special two-tone interiors (up to Rs 7.80 lakh), adaptive sports seats with 18-way adjustment (Rs 3.93 lakh).
- Price: Rs 1.87 crore (on-road Mumbai), escalating past Rs 2 crore with options; positioned at the higher end of full-size hybrid luxury SUVs.

   - Comparison to segment: Not directly compared numerically but described as offering a unique performance/efficiency mix.

8. VALUE AND PRICING

summary:
KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- Engine Options: 1.5-litre three-cylinder turbocharged petrol (134bhp, 230Nm), 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbocharged diesel (144-147.5bhp, 360Nm)

- Fuel Efficiency: Diesel - 16.14 kmpl city, 27.6 kmpl highway, combined 23.04 kmpl (tested); Petrol - 16.35 kmpl (claimed)
- Range: 1,000+ km on a full tank (diesel, tested)
- Infotainment: Large curved touchscreen and all-digital instrument cluster, BMW OS8 interface, multiple cabin transformation modes, dual-zone climate control, ambient lighting
- Features: Panoramic sunroof, electrically adjustable/memory driver’s seat, front seat massage, auto tailgate, wireless vertical charging pad with display visibility, parking assist, some ADAS functions, rear seat 40:20:40 split flat-folding
- Boot Space: 540 litres standard, expandable to 1,600 litres with seats down
- Safety: Euro NCAP 5-star rating, 6 airbags, ABS with brake assist, dynamic stability and traction control, lane departure warning, front collision warning with brake intervention, Evasion Assistant, front & rear parking sensors, reverse assist, (no standard 360-degree camera except cited in pros/cons)
- Design Highlights: Signature kidney grille, 3D taillamps, sculpted bumpers, M Sport trim includes body-coloured diffuser, roof spoiler, blacked-out elements, dual-tone upholstery, ambient lighting
- Dimensions: Larger in all respects vs prior X1, now exceeds first-gen X3 in size
- Seating/Space: Upgraded interior space, ample rear legroom/headroom, driver seat extensive adjustment, second-row 40:20:40 split, rear seat recline
- Connectivity: Advanced in-cabin tech, all connectivity supported (Apple CarPlay/Android Auto not directly specified but implied as segment norm)
