- Safety: Four-star Global NCAP safety rating for adult occupants (standard and CNG versions). Dual airbags, ABS with EBD, corner stability control, ISOFIX child seat mounts, rear parking sensors, follow-me-home lights, rear defogger, speed alert, seatbelt reminder, speed-dependent door locks. Additional CNG-specific safety features: micro-switch shuts off ignition during refuelling, fire extinguisher, cylinder leak and thermal protection.
- Dimensions: Compact hatchback (kerb weight ~980kg). 168mm ground clearance (CNG version, reduced slightly from petrol).
- Boot Capacity: 242 litres in petrol variants; nearly zero in CNG variant as cylinder occupies most boot space.
- Features (Top-spec XZ+/XZA+): LED projector headlamps and DRLs, 15-inch alloy wheels (petrol), 14-inch steel wheels (CNG), rear wiper and washer, roof-mounted spoiler, illuminated two-spoke steering wheel, rain-sensing wipers, dynamic guidelines for reverse camera, body-coloured trim on air vents, piano-black dashboard inserts, height-adjustable driver seat, tilt-adjust steering, cooled glovebox, all-four power windows (one-touch-down for driver), keyless entry, electric ORVMs with auto-fold.
- Infotainment: Up to 10.25-inch touchscreen, wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto (new), ConnectNext system by Harman, 8-speaker sound system, all-digital monochrome instrument cluster (shared with Tata Nexon). Bluetooth and steering controls standard.
- Climate Control: Automatic air conditioning, rear AC vents absent.
- Seating: Supportive front seats with decent bolster, soft fabric or leatherette depending on variant. Rear headroom and knee-room sufficient for most, but limited for tall passengers; rear headrests non-adjustable. No centre armrest or rear seat split/fold.
- AMT CNG: Segment-first factory-fitted CNG with AMT, smooth take-off, further tuned creep function for city driving ease.
- Colors: New Tornado Blue with contrast black roof introduced; dual-tone options available.
- Other Notables: All versions now include Tata’s new illuminated steering wheel/LED headlamps. CNG versions gain dedicated fuel mode buttons and digital CNG gauges within the cluster.

---

REVIEW SUMMARY STRUCTURE

1. OVERVIEW
- Tata Tiago reviewed across standard petrol, CNG, and CNG-AMT variants by CarWale, with significant improvements post-BS6. Praised for mature styling, rich features for segment, outstanding safety, and value. 

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
- Engine: 1.2L 3-cyl petrol: 85bhp@6000rpm, 113Nm@3300rpm (petrol); 73-74bhp/95-96Nm (CNG).
- Transmission: 5-speed manual (noticeably notchy, takes getting used to), or 5-speed AMT (smooth creep, segment-first with CNG).
- Acceleration: Petrol 0-100km/h in 15.9s; CNG 16.8s. In-gear acceleration: 20-80km/h (petrol) 15.02s, (CNG) 15.5s.
- Drivability: City-oriented with relaxed low-speed pull; ample power at low-mid rpm for urban use, never feels underpowered at typical speeds.
- Steering: Very light at low speeds, good for urban manoeuvrability; weights up adequately at speed. 2.5 turns lock-to-lock.
- Ride Quality: Supple ride, absorbs most bumps well; only large potholes disturb cabin. High-speed stability is strong, well-controlled body roll.
- NVH: Mild, notable vibrations at idle (especially petrol), better when on move. CNG mode slightly less noisy, otherwise seamless transition between fuel modes. AMT reduces typical jerks; NVH expected to improve further.
- Braking: No specific stopping distances mentioned; ABS and EBD standard. Confident, predictable braking.
- Suspension: Tuned to handle extra CNG tank weight; slightly firmer yet comfortable.

3. EXTERIOR
- Distinctive, mature styling post-facelift with Altroz-inspired face. Slim headlamps, shark-nose mesh grille, roof spoiler, swept bumpers, creased side lines.
- Size: Compact segment hatchback. Notable color options (Tornado Blue, dual-tone roof).
- Wheels: 15-inch alloys (petrol top-spec), 14-inch steel wheels (CNG), distinct wheel covers.
- Lighting: LED projector headlamps, LED DRLs (on higher trims), reworked taillamp signature, rear wiper, washer, defogger.
- Build: Feels solid for class; segment-best safety focus.

4. INTERIOR
- Design: Revamped with piano-black and body-color inserts, all-digital instrument cluster, new two-spoke illuminated steering.
- Fit/Finish: Improved, but still hard plastics; door armrest only soft-touch. Some material quality disappoints at price point.
- Space: Good front headroom/shoulder, adequate rear knee-room, rear headroom tight for tall occupants. Rear seat tight for three adults.
- Storage: Small cup holders, large door pockets; boot 242L in petrol but almost nil in CNG due to tank. Spare wheel beneath CNG tank, accessed by folding rear seat.
- Rear Seat: No armrest; no split-fold or flat-folding, fixed headrests, no rear AC vents or seatback pockets.
- Comfort: Supportive seats, ergonomic driving position, height-adjust driver's seat, tilt steering.
- Practicality: Excellent city visibility, entry and exit easy.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
- Infotainment: Up to 10.25-inch touchscreen, wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto (latest), ConnectNext interface by Harman, 8 speakers (incl. tweeters), steering-mounted controls, digital instrument cluster.
- Convenience: Auto AC, rearview camera, dynamic reverse guidelines, follow-me-home lamps, cooled glovebox, auto-fold ORVMs, keyless entry.
- Charging: Type-C ports (AMT CNG), all-four power windows.
- Driver Assistance: Rear parking sensors/camera, rain-sensing wipers (latest), speed alert, seatbelt reminder.
- Lighting: Full LED projector headlamps, new illuminated steering wheel.

6. SAFETY
- Rating: Four-star Global NCAP rating (adults), three-star (children). Unbeaten in the segment.
- Equipment: Dual front airbags, ABS with EBD, ISOFIX child seat mounts, corner stability control, speed-dependent locks.
- Additional (CNG): Micro-switch disables ignition while refilling, fire extinguisher (mandate), cylinder leak/themal protection, pressure-release nozzle.
- Advanced: Rear camera with dynamic guidelines (on higher trims). Stability, rear wiper and defogger standard on top trims.
- Crash results: Entry-level variant tested (with dual airbags) received four stars.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
- Petrol (Manual): 19.8kmpl ARAI claim.
- CNG: ARAI claim 26.49km/kg; tested 17km/kg (city), 33km/kg (highway), 21km/kg (real world mixed). CNG tank range approx. 227km/tank.
- Segment Comparison: CNG/Petrol efficiency on-par or better than rivals (Celerio, WagonR, Santro), especially in CNG mode.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
- Petrol: Noted as one of the segment’s most affordable safe hatchbacks (exact price not mentioned).
- CNG (i-CNG): Rs 6.28 lakh (XE) to Rs 7.82 lakh (XZ+), top-spec XZA+ AMT at Rs 8.9 lakh (all ex-showroom). CNG premium ~Rs 90,000 over petrol.
- Warranty: Not specified.
- Maintenance: Not detailed.
- Value: Excellent safety/feature-per-rupee; CNG versions retain full equipment list.

9. PROS AND CONS
Pros:
   - Four-star NCAP safety (standard and CNG)
   - Mature design, Altroz-inspired styling
   - Comprehensive features (even on CNG/automatic)
   - Good ride comfort, high-speed stability
   - City-friendly dimensions, excellent visibility
   - Affordable running costs, especially with CNG
   - Segment innovation: CNG with AMT
   - Reliable performance in both fuel modes with little difference

Cons:
   - Vibey three-cylinder at idle (especially petrol)
   - Manual gearbox is notchy; takes acclimatisation
   - Inconsistent cabin material quality, some hard plastics
   - Limited bootspace in CNG variant (virtually none)
   - Rear seat lacks armrest, AC vents, adjustability features
   - Long queues needed for CNG refuelling

10. COMPETITORS
- Maruti Suzuki WagonR, Celerio (including CNG), Hyundai Santro, Grand i10 Nios CNG, Renault Kwid, Datsun Go.
- Relative Strengths: Tiago outshines in safety (segment-best NCAP), offers more features across variants, superior ride/handling balance, segment-first CNG-AMT.
- Weaknesses: Boot space less with CNG (~0L vs. >200L in petrol), marginally higher CNG pricing.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
- Trims: XE, XM, XT, XZ+, top-spec XZA+ for petrol, i-CNG across all variants, including AMT.
- Features: All main equipment available CNG-to-petrol, skipped only large alloy wheels in CNG, rest features retained.
- Recommendation: Top-spec XZ+/XZA+ CNG recommended for full features with segment-first AMT/CNG combo.

12. VERDICT
- Strongest points: Class-leading safety, competitive pricing, mature ride and styling, unique segment tech (CNG AMT).
- Trade-offs: Material quality in cabin, CNG boot space.
- Buyer Suitability: Ideal for city users seeking safety, features, and low running cost; perfect family runabout, especially in CNG with AMT.
- Rating: Not numerically stated, but consistently “highly recommended” in segment, particularly for value, safety, and innovation.

summary:
KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- Engines: 1.2-litre petrol available in two configurations. Naturally aspirated (80bhp/115Nm, manual only, CNG option). Turbo-petrol (109bhp/205Nm in automatic, 109bhp/190Nm in manual).
- Transmission: 6-speed manual and 6-speed AISIN-sourced torque converter automatic.
- Seating: Flexible five- and seven-seat configurations; unique removable third-row seats (uninstall/reinstall in under 50 seconds).
- Cabin: All-new premium tan brown leatherette upholstery; soft-touch materials; sleeker dashboard and gold accent detailing; updated gear lever.
- Infotainment & Digital Displays: 10.25-inch touchscreen infotainment system with wireless Android Auto/Apple CarPlay; 7-inch digital instrument cluster.
- Connectivity & Features: CARA AI assistant (52 language voice recognition); Proxi-Sense keyless entry; push-button start; wireless phone charging; footwell and ambient lighting; auto-dimming IRVM.
- Comfort: Ventilated front seats; cruise control; roof-mounted rear AC vents with independent blower; cooled front seat controls on seat sides.
- Safety: 6 airbags standard; ABS with EBD; ESP (electronic stability program); hill-hold assist; tyre pressure monitoring system (TPMS); rear parking sensors; ISOFIX child seat anchors; 360-degree camera (optional, Rs. 25,000); expected 5-star BNCAP safety score supported by C3 Aircross result.
- Exterior: 17-inch diamond-cut alloy wheels; fully LED headlamps and fog lamps; split LED DRLs; black textured tailgate panel; X-badge at rear.
- Ground Clearance: 200mm.
- Boot Space: Up to 511 litres.
- Colour Options: 10 total, including new Deep Forest Green and Deep Forest Green/Perla Nera Black dual-tone (exclusive to Aircross X, with blacked-out roof Rs. 20,000 extra).
- Ambient and footwell lights; wireless charging pad; revised air vents (sleeker design).
- Price: Rs. 8.29 lakh–16.24 lakh (ex-showroom); Rs. 16.24 lakh (on-road Mumbai, Max Petrol AT variant).
- Notable Omissions: No sunroof, no ADAS suite, no powered driver seat, no paddle shifters, no diesel engine option.

---

REVIEW SUMMARY STRUCTURE

1. OVERVIEW
   - The Citroen Aircross X (reviewed by CarWale, Kapil Angane) represents a major refinement of Citroen’s versatile SUV formula for India. Significantly improved cabin quality, equipment list, and perceived value. Balances premium feel, practicality, and comfort.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
   - Engine: 1.2-litre, turbocharged petrol (109bhp/205Nm in AT; 190Nm in MT) or 1.2-litre NA petrol (80bhp/115Nm, manual only).
   - Acceleration: Not specifically quoted; performance described as smooth and strong for turbo; NA version feels underpowered.
   - Handling: Steering is well-sized, light, and offers good self-centering; stability and composure at high speeds; light steering aids city use.
   - Ride: Outstanding ride comfort; absorbs bad roads and speed breakers with ease; 200mm ground clearance prevents scraping; rides better than many rivals when loaded.
   - Braking: Stopping distances not provided; equipped with ABS, EBD, hill-hold, and ESP.
   - Transmission: 6-speed manual/6-speed automatic (AISIN). Automatic is smooth but not the most responsive; comfort-oriented tuning; no paddle shifters or drive modes; manual mode available.

3. EXTERIOR
   - Styling: Timeless SUV form, avoids current trends for oversized grilles; clean and modern design.
   - Lighting: Split DRLs; all-LED headlamps/fog lamps; wraparound tail lamps with black panel connecting them.
   - Wheels: 17-inch diamond-cut alloys (segment standard or above typical rivals’ 16-inch).
   - Colour Options: 10, including exclusive Deep Forest Green shades; dual-tone available at extra charge.
   - Distinctive: X-badge added at rear; exposed keyhole on driver's door is visually out of place.
   - Dimensions: Not specified, but categorised as a mid-size SUV.

4. INTERIOR
   - Quality: Significant uplift—soft-touch materials, gold accents, premium leatherette; dark tan brown theme elevates ambience above segment norm.
   - Fit and Finish: Improved vs. previous models; sleeker, modern dashboard and revised air vents.
   - Space: Exceptionally spacious; flexible five-/seven-seat options; easily removable third-row seats (unique in class); large windows for airy feel.
   - Comfort: Front and 2nd row seats are comfortable for all sizes; ventilated front seats; adjustable air conditioning, roof-mounted rear vents.
   - Cargo: 511 litres boot (with third row removed); among best in class.
   - Ergonomics: Controls logically placed; gear lever updated for easier use.
   - Storage: Not explicitly detailed but noted as practical and flexible; usability praised.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
   - Infotainment: 10.25-inch responsive touchscreen; wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto.
   - Instrumentation: 7-inch digital cluster, clear and readable.
   - Connectivity: CARA AI supports 52 languages for voice recognition, integrates with driver’s phone and infotainment, delivers connected features.
   - Controls: Push-button start/stop, cruise control, physical AC buttons/easy to operate.
   - Lighting: Ambient and footwell lighting; added premium touch.
   - Optional: 360-degree parking camera (display could be broader/higher-res); wireless charging pad.
   - Other: Proxi-Sense keyless entry, auto-dimming IRVM, cooled front seat controls, ventilated seats.

6. SAFETY
   - Safety Rating: Expected 5-star BNCAP (previous C3 Aircross scored 5 stars).
   - Airbags: 6 standard.
   - Features: ABS, EBD, electronic stability program (ESP), hill-hold, tyre pressure monitoring system (TPMS), ISOFIX, rear parking sensors.
   - Advanced: 360-degree camera (optional); absence of ADAS suite noted as a feature gap.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
   - Official and real-world figures: Not mentioned in review.
   - Comparison with rivals: Not mentioned in review.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
   - Price: Rs. 8.29–16.24 lakh ex-showroom; Rs. 16.24 lakh on-road Mumbai (Max Petrol AT).
   - Value: Strong for the segment—top Aircross X variant matches or beats rivals' mid-variants on features/space for price; segment-competitive warranty and maintenance info not mentioned.
   - Optional features: 360-degree camera (Rs. 25,000); dual-tone paint (Rs. 20,000).

9. PROS AND CONS
   - Pros:
     - Best-in-class ride comfort.
     - Practical, spacious cabin; five- and seven-seater flexibility.
     - Versatile, removable third-row (segment-unique).
     - Features: ventilated seats, ambient lighting, cruise control, wireless phone charging.
     - Advanced connectivity: CARA AI, 52-language support.
     - Safety: six airbags, ESP, 360-degree camera, projected 5-star safety.
     - Strong value for money, especially with turbo-AT.
   - Cons:
     - Barely changed exterior design versus predecessor.
     - Naturally aspirated engine underpowered.
     - No sunroof, no diesel option, no ADAS, no powered driver seat, no paddle shifters.
     - Smaller dealer/service network than major competitors.
     - Infotainment system’s graphics/interface feel basic compared to latest rivals.
     - Exposed keyhole on driver’s door a design flaw.

10. COMPETITORS
   - Rivals: Not explicitly named; compared against newer, better-equipped mid-size SUVs.
   - Comparison: Aircross X advantages—ride quality, flexible seating, cargo space, premium interior feel, value; misses out on diesel/ADAS/sunroof, infotainment sophistication.
   - USPs: Removable third row; unique flexibility for boot/seating; premium ride comfort.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
   - Trims: Turbo-petrol AT/MT, NA petrol MT (CNG optional), five- and seven-seat versions.
   - Features: Higher variants bring ventilated seats, CARA AI, wireless charging, 360-degree camera (option), connected features.
   - Recommended: Max Petrol AT highlighted as top value for its equipment/price.

12. VERDICT
   - The Citroen Aircross X is a significantly improved, versatile, and practical SUV. Ride comfort, value, and flexible interior make it a compelling choice for buyers prioritizing comfort over brand or trending features. Shortfalls in engine choice, feature list (missing sunroof/ADAS), and limited service network remain disadvantages. For the price, especially Max AT variant, offers more equipment/space than most rivals’ similarly priced variants. Well-suited for families wanting practicality, safety, and refinement; not for buyers focused on performance or cutting-edge tech. No explicit rating score given in review.
model_summary: Best for families needing spacious, flexible seating, outstanding ride comfort, strong safety, and value—especially in turbo automatic—over flashy features.

summary:
KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- Battery and Electric Motor Options: Standard version equipped with 38kWh IP67-rated battery pack, providing 134bhp and 200Nm torque; Pro (top-spec Essence) variant features larger 52.9kWh battery with same motor output.
- Claimed Range: Standard version - 331km; Pro version - 449km on a single charge.
- Charging Capability: Standard supports up to 45kW DC fast charging (0-80% in 55 min); Pro supports 60kW fast charging.
- Dimensions: Length 4,295mm, width 2,126mm, height 1,677mm, wheelbase 2,700mm, ground clearance 186mm.
- Boot Space: Standard - 604 litres; Pro - 579 litres, both with flexible seat configurations.
- Wheels and Tyres: 18-inch alloy wheels on top variants.
- Rear Seat Highlights: ‘Business Class’ seats with 135-degree recline, flat floor, large windows, panoramic glass roof, rear AC vents, USB charging, three-point seatbelts, adjustable headrests.
- Infotainment System: 15.6-inch touchscreen, wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, OTT apps, games, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, in-built Jio services, Play Store, theme store, phone mirroring.
- Digital Instrument Cluster: 8.8-inch fully digital display.
- Connectivity and Features: Infinity 9-speaker audio, 256-colour ambient lighting, ventilated front seats, powered driver’s seat (6-way), powered tailgate (Pro), keyless entry, one-touch up/down windows, auto wipers and headlamps, cruise control.
- ADAS/Driver Assistance: Level 2 ADAS on Pro trim; 360-degree camera standard.
- Interior Materials: Soft-touch surfaces, premium wooden texture, quilted leatherette seats with electrical adjust (driver), dual-tone ivory seat theme (Pro).
- Climate and Practicality: Auto climate control with physical knobs, large storage spaces, multiple cup holders, panoramic glass roof.
- Safety Systems: Six airbags, ABS, electronic stability control, three-point seatbelts all-round; missing rear wiper; no third-party crash test rating at time of review.
- Other Notable Features: Telescopic steering wheel, multifunction steering controls, customisable ambient lighting, flush door handles, split headlamps with projector units, vertically stacked lamp clusters.

REVIEW SUMMARY STRUCTURE

1. OVERVIEW
   - The MG Windsor EV is a spacious, practical, and well-equipped electric MPV/crossover, targeting families needing space and features at a competitive price. Review from CarWale and user-experience-based publications.
   
2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
   - Two battery options: 38kWh (standard) and 52.9kWh (Pro). Both coupled to a 134bhp/200Nm electric motor on the front axle.
   - No official acceleration or 0-100km/h time quoted, but described as “zippy” and “lively” especially in Sport mode; instantaneous throttle response in all but the most economy-focused modes.
   - Four drive modes: Eco+, Eco, Normal, Sport. Sport mode gives spirited performance, while Eco/Eco+ sap performance noticeably.
   - Three levels of regenerative braking: well-calibrated, especially helpful in dense traffic for energy reclaiming.
   - Ride quality acceptable over minor bumps, but suspension is on the firmer side and feels bouncy/unsettled on rough/broken roads or with multiple passengers; excessive vertical movement on sharp potholes.
   - Not a driver-focused car; instead, prioritizes ease of driving, calm handling, excellent visibility, and predictable range.
   - Steering: Light at low speeds, weights up at higher speeds; overall easy to manoeuvre in city, though not precise or communicative. Some ergonomics issues with steering button layout.
   - Braking: Confident, drama-free, though no detailed stopping distances.
   - No start/stop button: Car ready when brake is pressed; electronic stalk drive selector.
   - Pro variant’s larger wheels add to firm ride.

3. EXTERIOR
   - MPV/CUV styling, with simple, clean AeroGlide design.
   - Blanked-off grille, front fender charging port, flush door handles, projector split headlamps, and continuous LED strips front/rear.
   - 18-inch alloy wheels (Pro has unique design); three new exterior colours for Pro (red, blue, silver).
   - Dimensions position it as a mid-size SUV, maximizing interior space.
   - Features such as panoramic glass roof, integrated spoiler, and large glass surfaces emphasized for looks and function.

4. INTERIOR
   - Standout for quality, space, and plush materials; best-in-class feeling at price point.
   - Flat dashboard, elongated pillars, and raked windscreen add to sense of roominess.
   - Cabin features dual-tone theme (ivory seats in Pro), soft-touch surfaces, wooden textures, quilted leatherette ventilated seats up front (electric adjust for driver, manual for co-driver).
   - Rear seats dubbed ‘Business Class’: 135-degree recline, flat floor, copious leg/head/shoulder room, though some “business class” trappings missing (tray tables, sunblinds).
   - Abundant storage: large centre cupholder, under-console space, armrest bins, and dashboard bins.
   - Rear amenities: rear AC vents, USB ports, large glass roof, adjustable headrests, fixed panoramic glass (not openable), three-point seatbelts all occupants.
   - Boot: 604L (standard), 579L (Pro, due to bigger battery); flat loading floor, flexible for luggage/family trips.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
   - 15.6-inch infotainment touchscreen, extensive features (OTT apps, wireless smartphone integration, theme/app store, Jio connectivity); interface large but can be laggy or unintuitive.
   - 8.8-inch digital instrument cluster; displays range, trip, etc.
   - 9-speaker Infinity audio system with strong sound quality.
   - Wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi.
   - 256-colour ambient lighting, customisable themes.
   - Physical buttons only for climate controls; other functions (ORVMs, headlamps) managed through infotainment screen.
   - Powered tailgate (Pro).
   - 360-degree camera system standard; auto wipers/headlamps, telescopic steering, cruise control.

6. SAFETY
   - Six airbags, electronic stability control, ABS, three-point seatbelts for all, adjustable rear headrests.
   - Level 2 ADAS suite (Pro): advanced driver assist including lane keep, adaptive cruise, emergency braking (details not fully listed).
   - 360-degree camera aids visibility.
   - No rear wiper (noted as a miss), no NCAP crash test rating at time of review.
   - Child safety: ISOFIX anchor points not mentioned.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
   - Claimed range: 331km (38kWh battery), 449km (52.9kWh battery, Pro).
   - Real-world range not detailed for Pro but characterized as “predictable” and easy to manage in city driving for standard model.
   - Charging: 0-80% in 55 mins (standard, 45kW fast charger); Pro supports 60kW chargers.
   - No direct segment consumption comparison, but positioned as competitive.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
   - Price: Standard model starts at Rs. 9.99 lakh ex-showroom; Pro variant Rs. 18.10 lakh (introductory Rs. 17.5 lakh for first 8,000 bookings).
   - Features and quality labelled as strong for the price, especially for space and tech.
   - Battery rental (BaaS) scheme available for savings on cost.
   - No details provided on warranty or maintenance/service intervals.
   - Pro version only available in top variant, reducing affordable access to extended range and ADAS.

9. PROS AND CONS
   - Pros: Spacious and lounge-like cabin, premium fit and finish, feature-rich (large touchscreen, ADAS, ventilated seats), smooth and zippy EV performance, predictable range, strong safety kit, easy drivability, striking value at lower variants.
   - Cons: Ride quality firm/bouncy, especially with 18-inch wheels; infotainment system can lag and controls crucial features (risk if system hangs); too many controls bundled onto steering buttons; rear seat not as luxurious as claimed (missing sunblinds, tray tables, rear entertainment); no rear wiper; Eco modes too restrictive; MPV exterior design seen as plain by some.

10. COMPETITORS
    - Direct rivals: Tata Nexon EV, Hyundai Creta Electric.
    - Windsor EV strengths: Cabin space, features, competitive pricing for standard, unique “business class” rear seats.
    - Weaknesses: Ride quality and ease-of-use not quite as refined as some rivals; Pro’s price brings it closer to better-equipped alternatives.
    - USP: Cabin space, tech, configurable seats, predictable range, overall family versatility.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
    - Standard: 38kWh battery, major features included, best on value.
    - Pro (Essence): 52.9kWh battery, Level 2 ADAS, powered tailgate, dual-tone interior, new alloy wheel designs/colours, 449km range.
    - Pro recommended only if extended range or advanced assist tech are must-haves; standard model presents better value for budget buyers and urban use.

12. VERDICT
    - MG Windsor EV blends massive cabin space, technology, and premium cabin feel for the price; stands out for rear-seat comfort and daily EV usability, especially with predictable range and convenient features.
    - Pro version upgrades address range anxieties and tech gaps, but raise the effective cost.
    - Ride comfort and infotainment ergonomics are clear downsides; some luxury claims for the rear seat are overstated.
    - Best suited to families prioritizing space, tech, and predictable commutes, or those wanting brand assurance with EV ownership.
    - Not ideal for those wanting sporty handling or frequent use on poor roads.
    - No explicit score given, but overall strongly recommended for value/features mix in standard, and for EV buyers needing true five-seater family space.
model_summary: Spacious, tech-rich EV ideal for families needing flexible seating, daily city use, predictable real-world range, and strong feature-value balance.

summary:
KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

Engine and Transmission
- 1.2-litre, four-cylinder, K12 petrol engine; outputs 89 bhp (88.5 bhp specifically stated), 113 Nm torque.
- Idle start/stop technology increases fuel efficiency.
- Transmission: Five-speed manual or five-speed AMT (automatic manual transmission); CNG only available with manual; AMT replaces earlier CVT.
- 76.4 bhp/98.5 Nm CNG variant available (mid-spec trims only).

Fuel Efficiency
- Claimed ARAI: 22.35 kmpl (manual), 22.94 kmpl (AMT).
- Real-world tested: 17.52 kmpl (manual city), 22.3 kmpl (manual highway), 17.34 kmpl (AMT city), 22.23 kmpl (AMT highway).
- Test cycle combined efficiency: 18.57 kmpl.
- CNG model: Not specified, but no idle start/stop functionality.

Exterior Features
- Redesigned front fascia with sleeker grille, chrome line, carbon fibre-esque elements.
- Segment-unique front design, different from Baleno.
- New 16-inch alloy wheels (top variants); 195-section tyres.
- LED projector headlamps, LED DRLs, LED foglamps (top trims).
- Chrome door handles, chrome boot garnish.
- Rear design changes: redesigned taillamps, reworked bumper.
- UV protection film on glass (V variant); especially useful in hot climates.
- Colors: white, silver, blue, black, red.

Dimensions and Practicality
- Just under 4 metres in length; long wheelbase for segment.
- Boot capacity: 318 litres (about 20 litres less than previous gen); 60:40 split-folding rear seat available.
- Kerb weight: 960 kg; Fuel tank: 37 litres.

Interior Features and Comfort
- Dual-tone black-beige theme with gloss black inserts; black-white color theme.
- Piano black flat-bottom steering wheel (upmarket finish).
- High-quality plastics, excellent fit and finish; among the best in segment.
- Height-adjustable driver’s seat, tilt and telescopic steering adjustment.
- Soft fabric seats with adequate cushioning, side support (no leatherette).
- Practical storage: All door pads hold 1L bottles, glovebox, cupholders, front armrest with storage.

- Parcel tray, seatback pockets, USB fast charger at rear.

- Smart Playcast infotainment system; Android Auto, Apple CarPlay, Bluetooth.

- Six airbags (V variant).
- ESP (AMT versions), hill hold function.
- Rear parking sensors and camera.
- Vehicle stability control (selected trims).
- No NCAP crash safety rating yet.

- Standard warranty: 3 years/100,000 km.
- Optional extended warranty: up to 5 years/220,000 km.
- 24x7 roadside assistance.
- Toyota aftersales service known for reliability.

Variants

- Feature distribution well structured across variant ladder.

- CNG approximately Rs 70,000 premium over petrol.
- Glanza ~Rs 10,000-30,000 more expensive than comparable Baleno trims.

REVIEW SUMMARY

1. OVERVIEW
Toyota Glanza, reviewed extensively by CarWale, is a premium hatchback based on Maruti Suzuki Baleno but differentiated through styling, features, warranty, and brand value. Reviewers include Kaustubh Gandhi, Kapil Angane, and CarWale road test team.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
- Responsive, refined 1.2L petrol; best suited for calm, everyday driving.
- Power: 89 bhp, 113 Nm torque; enough for city, relaxed on highways.
- Highway performance feels slightly sluggish when fully loaded or overtaking; not intended for fast driving.
- AMT (AGS) delivers smooth gearshifts, notably less head-nod than other AMTs.
- Manual gearbox: slick, easy clutch, forgiving nature.
- Steering: light for city maneuvering; accurate, but not overtly sporty.
- Ride: soft at low speed (feels a bit bouncy/springy), comfortable otherwise, well-insulated at city speeds; some firmness at low speed, but absorbs bumps and undulations well.
- Brakes: responsive, good pedal feel, easy in city traffic.
- Noted real-world city driving mileage always above 14 kmpl.

3. EXTERIOR
- Modern Toyota styling sets Glanza visually apart from Baleno (front fascia, grille, sharper LED elements).
- UV-cut glass exclusive in segment; carbon fibre style bumper insert.
- New 16-inch alloys and 195 mm tyres on top variants add to stance.
- Automatic headlamps, chrome highlights, LED lighting package; high perceived quality.
- Just under 4 metres in length; similar dimensions to segment rivals.
- Five exterior colors: white, silver, blue, black, red.

4. INTERIOR
- Dual-tone cabin, gloss black inserts elevate ambience; flat-bottom steering.
- Material quality among segment best, tight-fitting panels.
- Highly functional storage (door pads for 1L bottles, centre armrest storage, cupholders, parcel tray).
- Driver’s seat height, steering reach/rake, clear view outside (slim A-pillars, low dash).
- Front seats: soft fabric, supportive but cushioning soft on long trips; no leatherette even top-end.
- Rear seat very comfortable for two (angle/space/charging ports), compromised for third passenger due to AC vent and lack of headrest/armrest.
- Boot: 318 litres, tall/narrow loading lip hampers big/heavy item access; 60:40 split-fold; practical for daily use.
- No rear armrest even on top trims.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
- G trim: 7-inch touchscreen, six speakers, voice commands, Android Auto/Apple CarPlay, rear camera, push-button start, rear AC vents, height adjustable driver seat.
- V trim: 9-inch touchscreen, Arkamys tuning, 360° camera, segment-first colored HUD, cruise control, auto-dimming IRVM, auto folding ORVM, UV glass, LED DRLs/foglamps.
- Toyota i-Connect with remote features, geo-fencing, live tracking, health monitoring.
- Voice assistant slow and sometimes triggers erroneously.
- Touchscreen system easy to use; quick interface, but slow voice control.
- Heads-up display has ten brightness/four font position levels, shows detailed driving/A/C data.

6. SAFETY
- Dual airbags standard; six airbags on top variants.
- ABS, EBD, brake assist, ESP (AMT), hill hold, ISOFIX anchors, auto door lock: Standard/variant dependent.
- Rear middle seat only lap belt, no 3-point; no NCAP safety score yet.
- Rear sensors and camera; 360° camera (V).
- No innovative crash safety features mentioned.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
- Claimed: 22.35 kmpl (manual), 22.94 kmpl (AMT); CNG not specified.
- Tested: ~17.5 kmpl city, ~22.3 kmpl highway (both manual/AMT nearly identical).
- Owner-reported: 14-15 kmpl in regular city use, over 15 kmpl on highway.
- 37L tank, tested range up to 690 km (combined); theoretical maximum ~849 km.
- Efficient compared to segment; idle start/stop helps real-world figures.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
- Rs 6.39 lakh (base E) to Rs 10 lakh (V AMT ex-showroom); CNG Rs 70k more than petrol.
- On-road price (Mumbai, tested): Rs 11.36 lakh (V manual).
- Premium over Baleno, but higher warranty, Toyota service, and some extra features offset higher cost.
- Warranty: 3 years/1 lakh km standard, up to 5 years/2.2 lakh km extension.
- 24x7 RSA included; maintenance/service costs not explicitly mentioned.

9. PROS AND CONS
Pros:
- Distinctive Toyota styling; upgraded design over Baleno—eye-catching front, carbon fibre elements.
- Spacious cabin; high practicality with storage, good for 4 adults.
- Segment-first tech: heads-up display, 360-degree camera, UV glass, i-Connect.
- Excellent fuel efficiency (real-world and claimed).
- Smoothest AMT gearbox in its segment; refined, efficient engine.
- Comfortably equipped—auto climate, cruise control, Arkamys audio.
- Toyota’s brand image, aftersales, and extended warranty.
- Rear seat and front seats comfortable and supportive in routine use.

Cons:
- Higher price vs. Baleno (up to Rs 30,000 more, top trims); some buyers may not see enough differentiation for premium.
- Ride quality a bit firm at low speed.
- Engine feels sluggish on highway or fully loaded; not sporty or quick to accelerate.
- Rear bench awkward for 3rd passenger (AC vent intrusion, no headrest/armrest).
- Rear seat: only lap belt for centre occupant; three-point missing.
- Boot lip high and narrow; hampers loading of heavy items.
- Voice assistant slow/unintuitive; sometimes activates erroneously.
- Middle trims offer fewer premium features; no rear armrest even in V variant.
- Cabin design still very similar to Baleno; not a unique Toyota inside.

10. COMPETITORS
- Competes with: Maruti Suzuki Baleno, Hyundai i20, Tata Altroz, Honda Jazz, Volkswagen Polo.
- Compared to Baleno: slightly more premium, better warranty/service, more Toyota-centric design.
- i20: Glanza smaller on width/wheelbase, less engine option variety but more feature-rich, particularly in tech and warranty.
- Tata Altroz: Altroz offers more engine choices (including diesel), Glanza is more refined and better equipped in top variants.
- Jazz/Polo: Both offer less tech, older design.
- Unique proposition: segment-first tech (HUD, 360° cam), Toyota aftersales, extended warranty, best AMT.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
- Four trims: E (manual only, basic features), S adds music system, G includes alloy wheels, larger screen, more tech/features, V gets complete feature list (HUD, 360°, UV glass, cruise, premium audio).
- CNG option only in S and G (mid).
- AMT available in S, G, V.
- Recommended: G for strong balance of features/equipment; V for maximum technology and safety kit.

12. VERDICT
Toyota Glanza is a well-rounded, user-friendly premium hatchback, excelling in comfort, fuel efficiency, and features, especially in top trims. Standout for city use due to practical cabin, smooth AMT/manuals, segment-first tech, high warranty/support, and Toyota’s reputation. Suited for families, daily commuters, and buyers valuing peace of mind and feature content over sporty driving or specific brand loyalty. Small drawbacks in price premium, rear seat/cargo comfort, and lack of diesel are easy to overlook given otherwise strong package. No official rating score provided in review.
model_summary: Ideal for city-focused families seeking comfort, segment-first tech, excellent fuel efficiency, smooth AMT, Toyota reliability, and comprehensive warranty coverage.

# KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- **Battery Packs**

  - 50 kW DC fast charging: 0–80% in 50 min.

  - 0–100 km/h: 8.3–9.18 seconds (manufacturer/tested figures).

---

# REVIEW SUMMARY

## 1. OVERVIEW

- The Mahindra XUV400 is the brand's mainstream electric SUV aimed squarely at the urban family EV segment, competing primarily with Tata Nexon EV Max.
- Reviewers: CarWale and multiple automotive journalists (named where specified).
- Marketed as Mahindra’s first properly developed modern electric vehicle.

## 2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING

- 147–150 bhp motor; 310 Nm torque; front-wheel drive with single-speed auto.
- Three drive modes: Fun (eco, up to 90 km/h), Fast (balanced), Fearless (sport, full performance).
- 0–100 km/h in 8.3–9.18s (manufacturer/tested); quicker than Nexon EV; top speed 150 km/h.
- Linear, silent acceleration; smooth driving in urban conditions.
- Instant torque offers rapid responses; low-speed creep function for city use.
- ESP and traction control reduce prior issues with wheelspin.
- No manual brake energy regeneration selection; some default regen effect.
- Suspension (with MTV-CL, frequency-dependent damping) delivers segment-best ride quality on poor surfaces.
- Steering: light in city, heavier in sport modes but lacks directness and feels artificial; turning circle 5.3m.
- Braking: all discs, strong pedal response (100–0 km/h in 43.33m/3.06s tested).
- Tested range varies by driving mode: Fun (eco) yields highest real-world range.

## 3. EXTERIOR

- Styling closely follows XUV300 but with longer, more muscular rear, unique copper highlights, and bold checkered grille.
- Copper twin peaks logo, copper roof rails, and copper accents set EV identity.
- Five colour options; two-tone copper roof available.
- 4,200 mm total length, outclasses Nexon EV for internal space.
- Projector headlamps with DRLs, fog lamps added in update, unique alloy wheels, strong SUV stance.
- Bolder proportions and higher stance compared to ICE sibling.

## 4. INTERIOR

- Black cabin theme with copper accents; dual-tone seats (leatherette, copper stitching).
- Dash, switchgear, and console design essentially unchanged from XUV300, widely seen as outdated for the segment.
- Analogue driver display, no full-digital cluster; seven- or 10.25-inch infotainment (latter introduced in update).
- Front seats comfortable, supportive for long drives; rear seats offer best-in-class legroom but floor height increased by underfloor battery causes slightly awkward, knees-up posture.
- No rear AC vents, limited storage behind front seats; cupholders present, limited centre console smartphone storage.
- Great visibility, large mirrors, practical boot (378 litres; highest in segment).
- Armrest and storage in doors; rear seat ingress/egress good.

## 5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES

- Touchscreen infotainment system (7" initially, 10.25" later); six-speaker audio, built-in navigation.
- Apple CarPlay, Android Auto (wired/wireless as per variant), Bluetooth, USB, smartwatch integration.
- BlueSense mobile app for remote functions and vehicle status.
- Keyless entry, push-button start/stop.
- Electric sunroof, updated auto-dimming IRVM, rear-view camera with adaptive guidelines, tyre pressure monitoring.
- Driver performance assessment features, vehicle data displays.
- Wireless charging introduced in feature update.
- Standard cruise control, fog lamps, tyre position display in newer EL variant.
- Lacks modern features like rear AC vents, ventilated seats, or regenerative braking adjustment controls.

## 6. SAFETY

- Six airbags, ISOFIX anchors standard.
- All-wheel disc brakes, ABS, EBD, ESP, traction control.
- Hill hold control, speed/impact-sensing door locks, rear parking sensors.
- Battery is IP67-rated.
- No ADAS, no NCAP crash safety rating reported.
- No lane keep or advanced driver aids; basic safety covered but lacks segment advancements.

## 7. FUEL ECONOMY

- Claimed ARAI range (39.4 kWh): 456 km; (34.5 kWh): 375 km.
- Tested real-world range: ~282–285 km (Fun mode with AC); drops to ~230–261 km in sportier modes.
- Real-world range significantly lower than claimed; still competitive with Nexon EV Max.
- Range monitoring system accurate and gradual in updating during test.
- Comparison: Outranges Nexon EV on paper but lag behind MG ZS EV, Kona in real-world conditions.

## 8. VALUE AND PRICING

- Prices: Rs 17.03–20.21 lakh (OTR Mumbai), competitive for its segment.
- Features like ride quality, segment-best boot, strong performance support value proposition.
- Interiors and missing advanced tech features detract from segment leadership.
- No explicit warranty or service data in reviews.

## 9. PROS AND CONS

**Pros:**
- Excellent real-world and claimed range for the segment.
- Peppy, linear, noiseless performance; best 0–100 km/h acceleration.
- High-quality ride (advanced dampers).
- Spacious cabin, segment-leading boot.
- Rich safety and infotainment features post-update.
- Standout copper EV styling elements.
- Value pricing versus features, direct rival to Nexon EV Max.

**Cons:**
- Outdated dash and cabin design; analogue dials, button-heavy layout.
- Rear seat floor height awkward for some passengers.
- No rear AC vents or ventilated seats.
- No adjustable brake regen setting.
- Lacks ADAS/advanced safety tech.
- Real-world range less than claims.
- Features and interface lag behind some rivals in modernity.

## 10. COMPETITORS

- Main rivals: Tata Nexon EV Max, MG ZS EV Excite.
- Tata Nexon EV: XUV400 edges it on boot space, acceleration, and claimed range; Nexon counters with more modern infotainment and established service network.
- MG ZS EV: Offers more range/features, but at higher price point.
- XUV400’s unique advantages: ride comfort, interior space; weaknesses: cabin modernity, feature set.

## 11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT

- Two battery options: short-range (34.5 kWh, Fun & Fast modes), long-range (39.4 kWh, all drive modes).
- EL variant most feature-rich; receives critical feature updates (ESP, fog lamps, wireless charging, 10.25" touchscreen).
- Recommended: EL Long Range for best performance, features, and practicality.

## 12. VERDICT

- XUV400 sets a new benchmark among urban mainstream eSUVs for range, performance, ride comfort, and practicality.
- Falls short on cabin modernity, missing premium features, and real-world range.
- Strong value for money proposition, especially for buyers needing space, ride quality, and best-in-class acceleration.
- Most suitable for families desiring practical, affordable electric mobility; enthusiastic drivers will appreciate performance but may be disappointed by interior execution.
- Rating (CarWale road test): 379/600 (main deductions for interior, premium features, and real-world range).
- Emphatically recommended over ICE-EV conversions, direct rival to Nexon EV, but future Mahindra EVs may leapfrog it in tech/ambience.
model_summary: Spacious, quick electric SUV with segment-best boot, strong urban ride, practical range; ideal for families seeking value, comfort, daily versatility.

KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

Platform and Body
- Heartect Platform: Advanced, lightweight, provides increased rigidity, improved crash safety, and aids efficiency.
- Dimensions: Length 3,530mm, width 1,490mm, height increased by 45mm over predecessor, wheelbase 2,380mm (+20mm vs previous gen). Compact city hatchback proportions.
- Kerb Weight: 730kg, contributing to nimble handling and fuel efficiency.
- Tyres: 155/65 R13 (current gen), steel wheels with wheel covers; earlier models had wider 150/80 R13 tyres.
- Boot Space: 214 litres, 37 litres more than previous model; practical, well-shaped.
- Turning Circle: 9m, making tight urban manoeuvring easy.

Engine and Transmission
- Engine: K10C 1.0-litre, 3-cylinder, naturally aspirated petrol; 998cc displacement.
- Power Output: 66bhp @ 5,500rpm; Torque: 89Nm @ 3,500rpm.
- Transmission: 5-speed manual or 5-speed AMT (Automated Manual Transmission), smooth, light clutch.
- Power-to-weight Ratio: 90.41bhp/tonne; Torque-to-weight: 121.92Nm/tonne.
- Fuel Tank: 27 litres.

Performance
- 0-60km/h: 5.23s
- 0-100km/h: 12.15s
- 20-80km/h (3rd gear): 11.24s
- 40-100km/h (4th gear): 16.01s
- 100-0km/h Braking: 3.67s/46.23m

Suspension and Brakes
- Front: Independent MacPherson strut; Rear: Torsion beam axle (replaces prior three-link).
- Front Brakes: Discs; Rear Brakes: Drums.
- ABS with EBD standard.

Exterior Features
- Redesigned, rounded shape; large single-piece honeycomb grille, integrated halogen headlamps with indicators, halogen tail lamps.
- No DRLs or fog lamps.
- Retained lift-type door handles, 13-inch wheels.
- Available Colours: Metallic Silky Silver, Metallic Granite Grey, Solid White, Metallic Speedy Blue, Metallic Sizzling Red, Pearl Metallic Earth Gold.

Interior Features
- All-black cabin with silver/brushed aluminium accents.
- Hard plastics; build and fit acceptable for segment.
- Redesigned dashboard, seven-inch SmartPlay Studio touchscreen infotainment system (VXi+), digital instrument cluster with trip meters, fuel, and gear indicators, no tachometer.
- Steering wheel with mounted audio/voice controls.
- SmartPlay Dock (VXi) allows smartphone as screen, dedicated mount.
- Four speakers, multiple audio preset modes.
- Black and beige fabric upholstery, checkered pattern.
- No adjustable headrests or seat height/streeting adjustment.
- Multiple storage spaces: cupholders, cubbyholes, front-only 1L bottle holders, small glovebox.
- Manual front power windows, rear windows manual.

Technology and Features
- 7-inch touchscreen infotainment (VXi+): Supports Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.
- Digital instrument cluster (no tachometer).
- Manual AC, central locking, powered front windows.
- Steering mounted audio/voice controls (VXi+).
- No rear defogger, wiper, or IRVM dimmer on any variant.

Safety Features
- Dual front airbags standard.
- ABS with EBD, front seatbelts with pre-tensioner and load limiter.
- Rear parking sensors; speed-sensitive auto door locks; impact-sensing door unlock; seatbelt reminders.
- High-speed alert.
- Collapsible steering column.
- No NCAP crash rating yet.

Fuel Economy
- ARAI-rated: 24.39kmpl (MT), 24.90kmpl (AMT), among the best in segment.
- Real-World: 14.5kmpl (city), 21.8kmpl (highway, manual), range ~416km/tank.

Pricing and Variants
- Ex-showroom Range: Rs 3.99 lakh (Std MT) to Rs 5.84 lakh (VXi+ AMT).
  - Std MT: Rs 3.99 lakh
  - LXi MT: Rs 4.82 lakh
  - VXi MT: Rs 4.99-5.05 lakh
  - VXi+ MT: Rs 5.33-5.34 lakh
  - VXi AMT: Rs 5.49-5.6 lakh
  - VXi+ AMT: Rs 5.83-5.89 lakh
  - VXi S-CNG: Rs 5.95 lakh (CNG power: 56bhp/82.1Nm)

Review Summary

1. OVERVIEW
- The Maruti Suzuki Alto K10 is a compact budget hatchback offering improved platform, engine, fuel economy, features, and space compared to its predecessor. Reviewed by multiple publications including CarWale and others, with highly positive sentiment regarding first-car suitability and value.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
- 1.0L, 3-cylinder K10C engine; 66bhp/89Nm.
- 0-100km/h in 12.15s; peppy, tractable, especially in city speeds.
- Light clutch, easy-shifting gearbox for manual; AMT version offers hassle-free urban driving.
- In-gear acceleration: 20-80km/h in 11.24s (3rd), 40-100km/h in 16.01s (4th).
- Suspension absorbs bumps well under 40km/h; vertical movement and tire noise above 80km/h, not very stable at highway speeds.
- Braking: 100-0km/h in 46.23m; brakes inspire confidence, especially for city use.
- Steering: Slightly heavy, lacks self-centering; tight turning radius eases city navigation.

3. EXTERIOR
- Fresh, rounded design with prominent honeycomb grille, contemporary headlamp/tail lamp treatment.
- Slight increase in height and wheelbase; compact overall but roomier than before.
- No DRLs/fog lamps; paint quality and panel fit above segment expectation.
- Colour choices expanded; overall looks functional but considered plain by reviewers.

4. INTERIOR
- Significant upgrade: new all-black theme with silver accents.
- Materials: Hard plastics (cost-cutting evident), but fit/finish decent for price.
- Front row: Good entry/egress, appropriate headroom for average-height drivers; no height/streeting adjustment. Tall drivers may find space tight.
- Rear row: Comfort adequate for two adults, three will be cramped; headroom and seat base length limited, fixed headrests; manual windows.
- Storage: Two front cupholders, small glovebox, bottle holders (front doors only), rear storage minimal.
- Boot: 214 litres, easily swallows small luggage; parcel tray without lifting strings, narrow access.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
- 7-inch touchscreen infotainment (VXi+): Segment-leading, supports Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, decent sound; other variants get SmartPlay Dock with smartphone integration.
- Digital instrument cluster: Amber display, lacks tachometer.
- Steering-mounted audio/voice controls: Available on higher trims.
- Manual AC, powered front windows, central locking.
- No basic features like day-night IRVM, rear wiper, or defogger on any trim.
- Basic user interfaces, but ease of use praised.

6. SAFETY
- Standard: Dual airbags, ABS with EBD, driver/co-driver seatbelt reminders, rear parking sensors, speed-sensing auto door locks, impact-sensing unlock, front seatbelt pretensioners, collapsible steering.
- No NCAP crash test results yet (pending).
- High-speed alert, child safety features.
- No advanced ADAS or blind-spot monitoring.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
- ARAI: 24.39kmpl (manual), 24.90kmpl (AMT), segment-best.
- Real-world: 14.5kmpl (city, manual), 21.8kmpl (highway).
- Theoretical range: 416km on full 27L tank.
- Substantial efficiency improvement over outgoing K10B engine (24.07kmpl).
- No idle start-stop feature; CNG version available.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
- Segment’s most affordable starting price (Rs 3.99 lakh); top-end VXi+ AMT competitive at Rs 5.84 lakh, CNG variant Rs 5.95 lakh.
- Lower trims skip essential features. Mid/high variants recommended for value.
- Maintenance costs remain low; backed by Maruti’s extensive after-sales network.
- Warranty: Not specifically mentioned.
- Overall, judged outstanding value given features, efficiency, and reliability.

9. PROS AND CONS
Pros:
- Fuel efficient, peppy performance, easy to drive, light controls.
- Improved cabin, better space for four, boot size practical.
- Touchscreen infotainment and SmartPlay Dock (segment-best).
- Low maintenance costs, Maruti’s service network.
- Practicality through storage, tight turning circle.
Cons:
- Plain/basics-driven design.
- Noisy at highway speeds; insufficient insulation.
- Missing features in all variants, especially lower trims (no day-night IRVM, rear wiper/defogger, rear power windows).
- Build/trim quality clearly budget-centric; hard plastics, average fabric.
- Stability at highway speeds limited, body roll and vertical movement on rough roads.
- Seats: No height adjustment or adjustable steering/headrests.

10. COMPETITORS
- Renault Kwid: Direct rival; Alto K10 offers lower base price, better efficiency, similar compactness—Kwid gets more features and style.
- Maruti S-Presso: In-house competitor; K10 is cheaper by Rs 15-20k, S-Presso perceived as more stylish, similar engines.
- Others mentioned: Tata Tiago EV, Citroen C3, Toyota Glanza, Maruti Wagon R AMT, Maruti Celerio.
- Alto K10 differentiates primarily via value for money, fuel efficiency, ease of driving, extensive network, but loses out on style and certain advanced features.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
- Four trims: Std, LXi, VXi, VXi+.
- High variants (VXi+/AMT) recommended for features like touchscreen, audio controls, and basic conveniences; entry variant (Std) basic, lacking power steering, AC, body-coloured bumpers.
- CNG variant available; only with 5MT.
- Review consensus: Go for mid to high trims for a balance of value and equipment.

12. VERDICT
- The Alto K10 remains the quintessential first car—easy to drive, highly efficient, economical to own.
- Substantial improvements in platform, features, space.
- Downsides: Basic design, feature omissions in lower trims, road noise, plain materials.
- Best suited for city buyers/first-time owners prioritizing cost, reliability, and efficiency over style or feature-richness.
- Overall, an evolved entry-level hatchback, still unmatched in value but with some compromises.
- No specific rating score quoted; verdict heavily positive on value, urban usability, and low ownership costs.
model_summary: Ideal for first-time buyers and city families: compact, fuel-efficient, easy to drive, touchscreen infotainment, Maruti reliability, outstanding affordability.

Pricing

REVIEW SUMMARY STRUCTURE

1. OVERVIEW
The Maruti Suzuki Grand Vitara marks Maruti's serious entry into the premium midsize SUV segment, standing as the brand's flagship and challenging established rivals with broad engine choices including strong hybrid and CNG, feature-loaded variants, and distinctive styling. Reviews by CarWale/Kapil Angane and others indicate it elevates Maruti's product to a competitive premium level.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
- 1.5 K15C petrol (mild-hybrid): 102–105bhp, 137–139Nm; refined at low/mid revs, quiet, smooth; modest acceleration, struggles when fully loaded and at high speed, lacks midrange punch versus turbo rivals.
- 1.5 TNGA petrol (strong-hybrid): 91bhp/122Nm + 79bhp/141Nm electric; 114bhp system output; e-CVT, competent in city, can run purely electric at low speeds, very refined but gets noisy under hard acceleration.
- CNG: 87bhp/121.5Nm (CNG); performance adequate for city use, efficiency-focused.
- AllGrip AWD: Not a hardcore off-roader, FWD most of time, AWD engages when needed; not tested off-road in review.
- Manual: Five-speed unit, light clutch, slick shifts, well-spaced ratios.
- Automatic: Six-speed torque converter; smooth, not quick to react, prioritizes city ease over sporty feel.
- Handling: Steering is quick (2.5 turns LTL), but lacks feel and linear return; not sporty, family-oriented dynamics; stable at high speed, settled ride, effective absorption of undulations, no nervousness at 140+ km/h.
- Braking: No specific data, implied adequate.
- Ride: Cushy, absorbs bumps, comfortable over poor roads.

3. EXTERIOR
- Modern, commanding stance; exclusive Maruti front grille with chrome elements.
- Split LED headlamps with three-point DRLs, LED taillights/light bars.
- Blacked-out pillars, chrome accents, roof rails, and chunky wheel arches.
- Top trims offer 17-inch dual-tone alloys.
- Seven monotone colors: Nexa Blue, Arctic White, Splendid Silver, Grandeur Grey, Chestnut Brown, Opulent Red (plus three dual-tone options).
- Silver skid plates, shark-fin antenna, integrated spoiler, sculpted body lines.

4. INTERIOR
- Dual-tone black/brown cabin, layered soft-touch upper dash/doors.
- Wide doors, high seat positioning for easy ingress/egress.
- Comfortable supportive seats, front armrest with storage, rear armrest, reclining and 60:40 split rear.
- Rear seat: ample knee/lateral room, but tight for three adults (floor hump, AC console).
- Slightly raised boot floor in hybrid due to battery; ~398L luggage capacity.
- Multiple charging points (12V, USB, Type-C), sufficient in-cabin storage, seat ergonomics well reviewed.
- Material and finish superior to older Marutis but some inconsistencies on lower trim switchgear/buttons.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
- Panoramic sunroof (Maruti first), 9-inch floating infotainment touchscreen, Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, Bluetooth.
- Digital instrument cluster (hybrid/Alpha+), configurable menu; HUD on Alpha+.
- 360-degree camera, wireless charger, ventilated seats (hybrid), ambient lighting, cruise control, paddle shifters (auto/strong hybrid), keyless entry, engine start/stop, power-adjustable/foldable mirrors, auto-dimming IRVM, sliding armrest.
- Suzuki Connect telematics, TPMS (Alpha+), rear AC vents, rear USB/Type-C charging, tilt/telescopic steering.
- Alpha+ gets additional features over Alpha (ventilated seats, TPMS, HUD, wireless charging, digital cluster).

6. SAFETY
- Six airbags (top spec), dual airbags standard, ABS with EBD, ESP, Hill Hold Assist/Descent Control (AWD), ISOFIX.
- Rear sensors, reverse camera.
- TPMS on Alpha+.
- No independent crash test ratings mentioned.
- Speed alert, seat belt reminder, standard across range.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
- Strong Hybrid: 27.97kmpl (ARAI, segment leader).
- Mild Hybrid MT: 21.11kmpl; AT: 20.58kmpl; AWD: 19.2kmpl.
- CNG: 26.6km/kg (ARAI).
- Petrol only: Claimed 18.5kmpl average.
- Real-world figures not specifically provided; Maruti’s mileage claims corroborate with segment-best status for hybrid.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
- Expected ex-showroom Rs 10.76–22 lakh; CNG Delta at Rs 12.85 lakh, Zeta at Rs 14.84 lakh.
- Extensive feature/value offering; hybrid tech and AWD unique in segment, justifies premium trims’ prices.
- Superior equipment on strong hybrid and top variants; good value for tech/comfort vs. rivals.
- Maintenance/service cost or warranty not discussed in review.

9. PROS AND CONS
PROS:
- Modern, striking exterior design with SUV presence.
- Segment-leading hybrid efficiency, wide drivetrain choices including CNG/AWD.
- Cushy, absorbent ride; compliant over bad roads.
- Smooth, refined powertrains; quiet cabin.
- Spacious, practical interior.
- Extensive feature set—sunroof, full digital display, 360-degree camera, connected tech.
- Easy ingress/egress, strong safety suite (up to six airbags).

CONS:
- Mild-hybrid lacks mid-range punch, less powerful than turbocharged rivals.
- Rear seat shoulder room limited for three adults; center floor hump.
- Cabin material quality not uniformly premium on all touchpoints.
- Top features restricted to strong hybrid/top trims.
- AWD is not a full-time off-roader.

10. COMPETITORS
- Hyundai Creta, Kia Seltos, MG Astor, Tata Harrier, Skoda Kushaq, Volkswagen Taigun, Toyota Urban Cruiser Hyryder.
- Strong hybrid efficiency and AWD availability are USPs vs. competition.
- Rivals offer turbocharged power for higher midrange and sporty drive.
- Vitara’s value-for-money, feature list, and comfort set it apart; some rivals offer better all-round driving dynamics or richer interior fit/finish.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
- Petrol/mild hybrid: Sigma, Delta, Zeta, Alpha, Alpha+; AWD only on Alpha, Alpha (O), manual only.
- Strong Hybrid (Intelligent Electric Hybrid): Delta+, Zeta Plus, Alpha+; exclusive features (HUD, ventilated seats, digital cluster).
- CNG: Delta, Zeta only; not available on top Alpha or Alpha+.
- Alpha+ and Alpha+ (O) recommended for tech/safety/comfort seekers; mid-level trims still well equipped for price.

12. VERDICT
- Maruti Suzuki Grand Vitara significantly elevates Maruti’s premium credibility, with class-best hybrid efficiency, usable AWD, sophisticated ride quality, rich equipment, and appealing design.
- Ideal for buyers placing emphasis on economy, comfort, features, and family use with strong value retention.
- Not as thrilling for performance enthusiasts or full-time off-roaders.
- Best suited for urban commuters, families, or those wanting a versatile, efficient, feature-laden SUV from a trusted brand.
- Rating score: Not provided in review.
model_summary: Efficient hybrid tech, city-friendly comfort, practical features, AWD variant, and spacious cabin make it ideal for families and urban commuters.

summary:
KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- 1.2-litre, 4-cylinder petrol engine: 82bhp (petrol), 68bhp (CNG), 114Nm torque (petrol), 95Nm (CNG); refined and smooth performance.

REVIEW SUMMARY

1. OVERVIEW
   - The Hyundai Exter is a compact, feature-loaded micro-SUV targeting hatchback and small-SUV buyers with SUV styling, abundant equipment, and efficient petrol/CNG powertrains. Variant-to-variant, it is positioned competitively below the Venue in the Hyundai lineup. Sources: CarWale, Kapil Angane, Haji Chakralwale.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
   - Engine: 1.2L, 4-cyl petrol, 82bhp/114Nm (petrol); 68bhp/95Nm (CNG). AMT calibration rated as excellent—smooth shifting in city, minimal AMT “jerks”. 0-100km/h: 15.26s (0-60km/h: 7.01s); overtaking requires planning. Manual gearbox: light clutch, short throws, easy to use. AMT: paddle shifters add responsiveness; holds gears at low speed without downshifts. Suspension: absorbs potholes/bumps well, vertical movement controlled. Steering: Good weight, progressive, linear, 3.5 turns lock-to-lock; easy city/highway use. NVH: refined, quiet petrol engine; little wind or road noise. Off-road ability: Handles mild rough roads well (185mm ground clearance). Braking: Not specifically quantified in review but described as adequate.

3. EXTERIOR
   - Distinctive parametric jewel design, gloss black bumper, C-pillar, and tailgate accents. Tall SUV stance, generous cladding, roof rails, squared wheel arches, split headlamps, signature H-shaped LED DRLs front/rear; projector lamps. 'Exter' lettering on hood. 15-inch dual-tone alloys. Six mono-tone and three dual-tone shades (notably Cosmic Blue, Ranger Khaki, Atlas White, Titan Gray, Starry Night, Fiery Red). Contrasting black roof on selected colours. Knight Edition: all-black exterior/interior, red accents. Length 3815mm, Width 1710mm, Height 1631mm (with roof rails), Wheelbase 2450mm.

4. INTERIOR
   - Cabin echoing Grand i10 Nios: wave-pattern dashboard, all-digital 4.2-inch cluster, 8-inch touchscreen, 3 interior themes (Light Sage, Cosmic Blue, Silver). Spatially efficient: ample headroom, particularly in rear with scooped roof; legroom generous. Seating: fixed headrests (front), adjustable (rear), best for 4 adults. Practical: cooled glovebox, wireless charging, multiple USB (including Type-C), cupholders, rear A/C vents, power windows, large windows for airy feel. Ergonomically sound (good visibility, tall seating, but no driver's armrest for long trips). 391-litre boot; can fit 3 cabin suitcases, lacks split folding rear seat.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
   - Feature loaded: 8-inch touchscreen, 12-language interface, wired Android Auto/Apple CarPlay, BlueLink (60+ telematics), wireless phone charger, digital instrument cluster standard, cruise control, keyless entry, height-adjustable driver’s seat, voice-enabled sunroof, automatic climate control, footwell lighting. Rear camera with dynamic guidelines, dashcam (front & rear). AMT variants: paddle shifters, metal pedals. Rear A/C vents, cooled glovebox.

6. SAFETY
   - Six airbags standard on all trims; ABS with EBD, ESP, vehicle stability management (VSM), hill-start assist (HAC), tyre pressure monitoring system, rear parking sensors, 3-point seatbelts (all), emergency braking signal. Rear camera, dashcam in higher trims. ESC, VSM, HAC only in high variants. No documented NCAP/crash test safety rating. No ADAS features.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
   - ARAI claimed: Up to 19.4 kmpl (petrol), 27.1 km/kg (CNG).
   - Real-world (CarWale tested, AMT): City 10.8 kmpl, Highway 18.5 kmpl, Combined (75% city/25% highway) 12.64 kmpl.
   - Compared to Tata Punch, Maruti Fronx: Fronx (city 11.8, highway 18.1, combined 13.37) slightly better efficiency overall; Exter competitive on highway, slightly behind in city/combined. CNG offers significantly higher overall efficiency.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
   - Ex-showroom: MT from Rs. 6 lakh; AMT from Rs. 7.97 lakh; CNG S/SX: Rs. 8.24–8.97 lakh; top SX(O) Connect AMT Dual Tone: Rs. 10.36 lakh. OTR Mumbai: Rs. 7.13–12.08 lakh.
   - High value: top trims loaded with segment-first features (six airbags, digital cluster, sunroof, wireless charging, dashcam). Warranty: 3 years/unlimited km (Fronx: 3 years/1,00,000km). Exter offers more features for the price compared to competitors; range-topping trims can feel expensive. Maintenance/service intervals not mentioned.

9. PROS AND CONS
   Pros:
   - Six airbags standard, comprehensive safety package.
   - Spacious/practical cabin for 4, plenty of storage, large boot.
   - Highly equipped: sunroof, wireless charging, digital cluster, rear A/C, cooled glovebox, ambient lighting.
   - Smooth, refined petrol engine; AMT calibration among best in segment, paddle shifters add flexibility.
   - Light controls, easy to drive and park, good visibility.
   - CNG option for low running cost.
   - Uniquely designed, visually appealing to many.
   - Generous warranty coverage.

   Cons:
   - Not engaging for spirited driving; lacks enthusiasm during quick overtakes.
   - 0-100 km/h performance is slow (15.26s).
   - Lacks split-folding rear seat; rear best for two adults.
   - No driver armrest or split-folding rear seat, affects comfort/flexibility.
   - Some hard plastics, interior finishing not as premium as larger Hyundais.
   - Expensive in top trims.
   - No crash test rating or ADAS features.
   - Design could be polarising; tries hard for "SUV" style.

10. COMPETITORS
    - Direct: Tata Punch, Maruti Fronx, Citroen C3, Maruti Ignis. 
    - Tata Punch: broader inside; Punch lacks CNG variant; Exter feels more modern/feature-rich, better AMT.
    - Fronx: bigger, more legroom/width, better ride, more expensive for fully loaded auto; Exter has smoother AMT, more features in top trims, smaller but more headroom.
    - Both Exter and Fronx have six airbags standard, but Exter packs more tech, and wireless Android Auto/Apple CarPlay is wireless only in Fronx.
    - Segment-first: Exter offers standard six airbags and dashcam.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
    - Trims: EX, EX(O), S, S(O), SX, SX(O), SX(O) Connect; CNG in S/SX only.
    - Feature ramp-up with higher trims; SX(O) Connect is most fully loaded, recommended for those wanting all features.
    - Entry trims great for budget buyers seeking core safety/features.
    - Knight variant offers unique aesthetic package.
    - Recommended: SX(O) Connect AMT for best tech and safety; S/SX CNG for max efficiency/economy.

12. VERDICT
    - Exter stands out in the micro-SUV class through segment-first six airbags, excellent feature/tech suite, refined drive, and practical, spacious cabin. Appeals to buyers wanting a compact, easy-to-drive, highly equipped urban crossover with fuel-saving CNG option.
    - Interior flexibility could be improved with a split seat; top trims should offer more premium materials for the price.
    - Design is distinctive and may not appeal to all, but feature-to-rupee ratio among the best.
    - Rated as a well-rounded city/family micro-SUV; recommended for those prioritizing safety, features, ease of use, and value. Not for buyers seeking performance excitement or outright rear space for three.
    - No specific numerical score provided in review.
model_summary: Ideal for urban families: spacious, feature-loaded micro-SUV, segment-first six airbags, smooth petrol/CNG, excellent AMT, top city safety, great value.

   - Engine: 1.2-litre, 4-cylinder, naturally aspirated petrol, 89 bhp, 110 Nm.

   - Design: Sharp styling, strong similarity to Honda City and Elevate; semi-coupe-like tapering roofline; avoids trendy connected taillight strip.
   - Dimensions: Sub-four-metre segment (exact numbers not mentioned).
   - Colors: Not specified.

   - Comparison: On par or slightly better than segment average given size/performance.

   - Value: Strong value-for-money proposition, especially from base variant upwards due to safety/tech inclusion.
   - Warranty/Maintenance: Not mentioned in review.
   
9. PROS AND CONS
   - Pros:
      - Value for money/high feature count.
      - Massive segment-leading boot space.
      - Segment-first Level 2 ADAS and safety suite.
      - Comfortable, quiet ride; relaxed highway cruiser.
      - Refined engine, quality NVH control.
   - Cons:
      - No diesel/factory CNG option.
      - Misses sunroof, ventilated seats, and other feel-good features.
      - Rear headroom/shoulder room tight for taller/three passengers.
      - Cabin plastics and steering/gear finish not premium.
   
10. COMPETITORS
    - Direct Rivals: Maruti Dzire, Hyundai Aura, Tata Tigor.

    - Model Range: Multiple trims, key features include ADAS, automation even in V Variant, top-spec ZX with maximum equipment.
    - Recommendation: Not explicitly stated, but strong equipment from base up makes lower/mid-variants solid value.
   
12. VERDICT
    - Summary: The Honda Amaze sets a new benchmark in active and passive safety, comfort, and boot capacity for sub-four-metre sedans, offering genuine value and a segment-first ADAS experience. While not the most powerful or luxurious, its strengths in refinement, features, and practicality outweigh its few misses. Highly recommended for buyers focused on value, safety, and everyday usability.

- Hyundai Creta; multiple extensive reviews (CarWale, long-term, multiple reviewers, Kapil Angane, Kaustubh Gandhi).

- Ride: Comfortable and absorbent in city, but firm at low speeds, softer but more floaty fully loaded at highway speeds.

- Aesthetic highlights: Black chrome grille, continuous LED lighting signatures, LED DRLs, 17-inch alloys.
- Proportionate, with strong road presence without appearing flashy.
- Puddle lamps with welcome, integrated spoiler.
- Paint: High quality, attractive colour palette.

- Materials: Good quality across surfaces; premium feel, much improved.
- Seating: Front generous, adjustable, comfortable; rear wide, but under-thigh support lacking.
- Rear: Spacious; three adults can fit across, 60:40 split, reclining, sunblinds, Type-C ports.

- Storage: Multiple cup holders, large door bins, cooled glove box, center cubby, rear armrest.

- Rear window sunblinds, two-step seat recline.
- Not wireless CarPlay/Android Auto.
- Keyless entry, push-button start, wireless charging, rear AC vents.

- Six airbags (SX(O)), three-point belt all seats, ESC, VSM, HAC, ABS, all-disc brakes.

- Petrol: Not specified; competitive within segment.
- Better real-world efficiency than most rivals, especially highway.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
- Diesel auto/petrol manual: Rs 11–20 lakh ex-showroom; top-spec diesel manual OTR Mumbai: Rs 22.7–22.8 lakh.
- SX (O): Fully-loaded, but expensive within segment; rivals now offer strong hybrid at same money.
- Ownership: 3-year/unlimited km standard warranty; 7-year extended available; service cost transparent and reasonable (e.g. Rs 4,488/10,000km).
- Maintenance: Routine, low-cost service; positive service experience.

9. PROS AND CONS
Pros:
- Excellent diesel refinement, class-leading fuel efficiency.
- Plush ride (unless full load/highway undulations).
- Spacious, practical, airy cabin.
- Best-in-class features: Panoramic sunroof, ADAS level 2, ventilation, Bose, 360-cam.
- Light controls, easy city/hwy drive.
- Premium feel, resale value, reliability.
Cons:
- Diesel engine lacks punch at lower revs/initial acceleration.
- Firm ride at low speeds, floaty when fully loaded at highways.
- Slow paddle shifter response (auto).
- Under-thigh support at rear seat lacking.
- Premium pricing for top trims.
- No wireless CarPlay/Android Auto.
- No NCAP safety rating yet.

10. COMPETITORS
- Kia Seltos, Honda Elevate, Maruti Grand Vitara (offers strong hybrid), Skoda Kushaq, VW Taigun.
- Creta stands out for diesel + auto option, sophistication, resale, and feature list.
- Some rivals offer stronger hybrid power, better high-speed ride (less floaty).

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
- Trim walk: Multiple (E, EX, S, S+, SX, SX (O)); SX (O) recommended for maximum features/tech.
- SX (O): ADAS, 360-cam, ventilated seats, Bose, advanced safety – best for tech-focused buyers.
- Lower/mid trims offer balanced value; basic features still strong throughout range.

12. VERDICT
- Hyundai Creta remains the benchmark for those wanting a well-rounded, modern, and practical compact SUV.
- Key strengths: Efficient diesel, plush feature-rich interior, high technology, strong ride quality, and real-world usability.
- Best suited for urban users, high-mileage drivers, families seeking top-end features, and strong resale.
- Some limitations: Ride with full load at speed, slow paddle shifters, premium pricing.
- Remains the top-selling, most complete choice in the segment. No specific numerical rating provided in review.

REVIEW SUMMARY STRUCTURE

1. OVERVIEW
   - Jeep Compass (facelifted version) reviewed by multiple automotive publications and reviewers (CarWale among others). Known for blending premium features, strong mechanicals, and top-tier off-road pedigree. Most expensive in its segment, priced Rs 16.99–28.29 lakh ex-showroom, Rs 19.75–34.52 lakh on-road (Delhi/Mumbai), with Trailhawk close to Rs 38 lakh on-road. Recognized for its iconic design, improved interior luxury, and wide-ranging features, but also for high pricing and rear-seat space limitations.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
   - Engine: Petrol 1.4 turbo (163bhp/240Nm), Diesel 2.0 turbo (170bhp/350Nm, 9AT or 6MT)
   - Acceleration: Not specifically stated; “adequate pull”, “good torque right from the word go”
   - Handling: Predictable, reassuringly heavy steering (2.5 turns lock-to-lock), some body roll due to high centre of gravity, but overall stable, manageable even on rougher terrain
   - Ride Quality: Firm but comfortable, easily absorbs regular bumps, slightly harsh over sharp potholes. “Flat” ride at highway speed, little vertical movement
   - Braking: Not detailed numerically, but stability and predictability emphasized – supported by electronic aids
   - Transmission: 9-speed AT smooth and efficient at highway speeds, but slow to respond at lower speeds; driving requires anticipation during overtakes due to lag

3. EXTERIOR
   - Design: Subtle facelift, de-chromed, black and grey accents, slimmer headlamps and grille, signature seven-slat grille, bold angular wheel arches, dual-tone roof options
   - Notable Styling: New 18-inch alloys, Black Shark edition with gloss black accents and badges, dual-tone Techno Metallic Green and Galaxy Blue
   - Dimensions: Not changed from previous version, mid-size SUV
   - Lights: Slimmer, more modern front lighting
   - Color Options: Multiple, including unique new green and blue

4. INTERIOR
   - Quality & Finish: Full overhaul, all-black themes, leather inserts, chrome detailing, multi-layer dashboard, excellent fit and finish, digital instrumentation, robust ergonomics
   - Space & Comfort: Good legroom, wide seat base, comfortable for two in rear, but tight for three adults, high rear seat position, practical cabin stowage, visible improvements in perceived quality
   - Boot: 438 litres, flat floor, practical shape, split-fold capability for flexibility
   - Downside: Gloss black panels prone to dust/fingerprints; perceived snugness can make cabin feel smaller

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
   - Infotainment: 10.1-inch HD touchscreen (UConnect), crisp graphics, wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, Jeep app integration, voice commands, online updates
   - Driver Information: Full 10.2-inch digital cluster, configurable screens and modern graphics
   - Connectivity: Wireless charging, USB sockets, AC vents and 1.0-litre bottle holders in rear
   - Premium: Alpine sound system (on higher trims), powered tailgate, dual-zone climate, panoramic sunroof, electric seat adjustment (8-way front), ventilated front seats, connected car technology, 360° surround camera
   - Ease of Use: Rapid menus, feature-rich, slightly busy interface reported, lacks some segment-pushing features (no 12V up front, missing paddle shifters)
   - Off-road Tech: Selec-Terrain modes on 4x4/Trailhawk, Select Speed Control, low-range transfer (Trailhawk)

6. SAFETY
   - Rating: Euro NCAP 5-star
   - Standard: 6 airbags (dual front, side, curtain), ABS/EBD, ESC, ISOfix, hill start assist, Rain Brake Support, Electronic Roll Mitigation
   - Optional/Advanced: Tyre Pressure Monitoring, park assist, 360-degree camera, hill descent control (4x4), electronic parking brake
   - Chassis: High-strength steel (70%), corrosion-resistant
   - Missing: No ADAS/lane keeping/adaptive cruise control features yet

7. FUEL ECONOMY
   - Figures: Not specified in review; test feedback on “outstanding” efficiency (14–20 kmpl range considered likely in segment, depending on engine/driving conditions)
   - Comparison: Real-world fuel efficiency competitive among diesel automatic mid-size SUVs

8. VALUE AND PRICING
   - Price: Rs 16.99–28.29 lakh ex-showroom, Rs 19.75–34.52 lakh on-road (top S trim); Trailhawk ~Rs 38 lakh on-road
   - Value: Expensive, especially for top-spec and Trailhawk; justified by Jeep brand, luxury, and off-road pedigree but may be considered less spacious and pricier than rivals
   - Warranty/Maintenance: Not mentioned in review
   - Ownership Cost: Not detailed; sparse sales/aftersales network observed as a con

9. PROS AND CONS
   - Pros:
      - Premium interior with modern tech/features
      - Robust off-road capability (especially in Trailhawk)
      - Confident ride and handling for segment
      - Brand status and iconic design
      - Comprehensive safety package (6 airbags, structure, Euro NCAP rating)
      - Highway comfort, long-distance touring ability
      - Electrically adjusted, ventilated front seats, panoramic sunroof
      - 360-degree camera, connected-car tech
   - Cons:
      - Expensive, especially top variants/Trailhawk
      - Less rear shoulder room, tight for three adults in back
      - Feature list not quite as exhaustive as some rivals (missing 12V plug, paddle shifters, greater seat adjustability, etc.)
      - 9-speed AT slow to respond at low speeds; needs anticipation
      - Diesel engine clatter/vibration at idle and under load
      - Gloss black trim requires constant cleaning
      - Sparse sales/aftersales network
      - No ADAS features; showing some age

10. COMPETITORS
    - Segment Rivals: Hyundai Tucson, Skoda Karoq, Volkswagen T-Roc, Tata Harrier/Safari, MG Hector/Hector Plus
    - Comparison: Compass offers superior off-road credentials, premium build, but pricier and less rear space than rivals; Trailhawk pushes up close to larger, more expensive alternatives like Toyota Fortuner and Skoda Kodiaq, but none as focused in off-road capability at this price
    - Unique Selling Proposition: Authentic Jeep 4x4/Trail Rated off-road ability, highest interior quality in class, iconic styling
