REVIEW SUMMARY STRUCTURE

1. OVERVIEW
   - The Honda Amaze is a compact sedan positioned as a practical, value-driven alternative to costlier midsize sedans. Reviews (CarWale, multiple automotive publications) highlight its spaciousness, boot size, ease of city driving, and refined engines as strong points. The latest updates bring mild styling tweaks, new features, and segment-firsts like diesel CVT and ADAS, keeping it competitive in a segment now dominated by SUVs.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
   - Petrol: 1.2L 4-cyl NA, 89bhp, 110Nm; smooth, refined, quiet at idle, gets noisy above 4,000rpm. Manual and CVT gearboxes available. CVT offers seamless shifting, rubber-band effect at high revs, paddle shifters add control; D mode favoured for comfort. 0–100km/h time not specified. 
   - Diesel: 1.5L, 99bhp/200Nm (MT), 80bhp/160Nm (CVT). Diesel CVT masks turbo lag, accelerates quickly for overtakes, muffled diesel noise, especially at idle. L and S drive modes available in diesel CVT. 
   - Ride: Suspension soft and tuned for comfort over rough urban roads; absorbs bumps/potholes well, some suspension noise and vertical movement at high speeds. 
   - Steering: Light, manageable in city, weighs up at speed; lacks sharp feedback, tends to understeer if pushed, some body roll evident.
   - Braking: Confident grip and panic braking performance; stopping distances not specified.
   - Overall: Easy to drive, well-suited for city with enough flexibility for highway cruising.

3. EXTERIOR
   - Highlights: Revised front with new multi-layered chrome grille, LED projector headlamps/DRLs, LED fog lamps, C-shaped LED tail lamps. 15-inch dual-tone diamond-cut alloy wheels (top trims), semi-coupe roofline, sleeker A-pillars.
   - Size: Standard sub-four-metre sedan dimensions; 170mm ground clearance.
   - Color options: Not specifically mentioned.
   - Distinctive styling elements: Borrowed design cues from Honda City and Elevate; improved headlamp/grille integration.

4. INTERIOR
   - Materials/Quality: Dual-tone black and beige dashboard, fabric upholstery only (no leatherette), adjustable front headrests, plastics quality adequate though not segment-best especially in lower cabin areas.
   - Space: Roomy cabin, easy ingress/egress, supportive seats, armrest with cupholders, rear seat comfortable for two, shoulder room tight for three occupants; rear headroom limited for tall passengers.
   - Ergonomics: User-friendly layout, all controls within reach, good visibility, plenty of storage spots; driver position suboptimal for very tall drivers (lacks under-thigh support).
   - Boot: 420 litres, exceptional for segment, can fit two large suitcases and additional bags.
   - Practicality: Flat floor at rear, but bench may be a squeeze for three. Rear AC vents added in newer variants, but missing in lower trims.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
   - Infotainment: 7.0-inch or 8.0-inch touchscreen (trim-dependent), Android Auto/Apple CarPlay, Bluetooth, two USB ports, voice commands; display response and interface merely average.
   - Instrument cluster: Analogue dials with monochrome multi-info display (no fully digital display); commented as outdated.
   - Connectivity: Honda Connect app with vehicle updates, maintenance, service, and offer notifications.
   - Convenience: Automatic climate control, push-button start/stop, keyless entry/boot release, height-adjustable driver seat, remote engine start (top trims), rear camera, rear defogger, wireless charger (top trims), paddle shifters (petrol/diesel CVT).
   - Driver Assistance: Segment-first Level 2 ADAS suite (incl. adaptive cruise control, lane keep assist, lane departure warning, lane watch camera on top ZX variant).
   - Feature Misses: No sunroof, no ventilated seats, no wireless phone charger in lower trims, no 360-degree camera, no ambient lighting.

6. SAFETY
   - Ratings: 4-star Global NCAP (adult occupant), 1-star (child occupant); structure considered stable.
   - Standard Features: Dual front airbags, ABS with EBD, Isofix mounts, parking sensors.
   - Higher Trims: Reverse camera, up to 6 airbags, rear defogger, Level 2 ADAS, lane watch camera.
   - Noted Misses: No ESP/ESC.
   - Unique Safety: 10-year ‘anytime’ warranty with transferability—segment-best.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
   - Certified: Petrol – 18.6kmpl (manual), 18.3kmpl (CVT); Diesel – 24.7kmpl (manual), 21kmpl (CVT).
   - Real World: Petrol CVT – 10.7kmpl (city), 20.3kmpl (highway), avg. 13–14kmpl.
   - Range: Over 450km on a 35-litre tank (petrol CVT).
   - Position: Among segment leaders for efficiency, especially diesel.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
   - Price: Rs. 6.32 lakh (base) to Rs. 13.51 lakh (top diesel AT); most common variants Rs. 8–10.9 lakh (ex-showroom).
   - Value: Offers refined engines, high efficiency, diesel automatic, auto gearbox even on lower trims, and many features at a lower price than mid-size sedans/SUVs; warranty support among strongest in class.
   - Maintenance/warranty: 10-year anytime warranty (transferable).
   - Service costs/intervals: Not detailed in review.

9. PROS AND CONS

   PROS:
   - Spacious, practical cabin and sizable 420L boot.
   - Refined petrol and diesel engines; strong efficiency.
   - Diesel CVT and paddle shifters segment exclusives.
   - Comfortable ride, easy city driving, light steering.
   - High equipment levels in top trims; new ADAS features, wireless charger, and more.
   - High safety (4-star GNCAP), 10-year warranty, keyless features.
   - Value-for-money proposition undercuts rivals on price/features.

   CONS:
   - Some features missing: No sunroof, rear AC vents (on most trims), digital instrument cluster, wireless charger (lower trims), 360° camera, ambient lighting, ventilated seats. 
   - Rear headroom restrictive for tall passengers.
   - Fit and finish below best-in-segment, especially lower cabin plastics.
   - Performance: Petrol CVT slightly lethargic on light throttle; gets noisy above 4000rpm; rubber-band effect notable.
   - No diesel or CNG option in latest update for some variants.
   - Handling: Not very engaging or dynamic compared to some rivals.

10. COMPETITORS
   - Maruti Suzuki Dzire: Top competitor, offers 5-star NCAP rating, comprehensive features, similar space. Dzire’s AMT less refined than Honda’s CVT; Dzire also lacks diesel option.
   - Hyundai Aura: Competes on equipment and efficient diesel/petrol engines; Aura’s AMT and infotainment less sophisticated, but offers CNG variant.
   - Tata Tigor: Strong build, competitive pricing/features; lacks Honda’s engine refinement and space.
   - Unique Differentiators: Amaze only car with diesel CVT, Level 2 ADAS, 10-year warranty; best-in-class boot.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
   - Trims: E, S, VX, ZX (names may vary); VX/ZX receive most features (LED lights, touchscreen, wireless charging, ADAS, etc.).
   - Unique: Petrol and diesel automatics available from base variant, rare in class.
   - Recommended: Top variants (especially ZX) provide maximum features and safety.
   - Boot, engine, and comfort features strong across all trims; feature distribution noted to be proportional to pricing.

12. VERDICT
   - The Honda Amaze stands out for its refined engines (petrol/diesel), outstanding fuel efficiency, spacious interior, best-in-segment boot and warranty, and the option of diesel CVT and ADAS features. It is especially compelling for those seeking a practical, economical, easy-to-drive family sedan with good comfort and daily usability. Lack of some premium features and conservative cabin design may deter tech-seeking buyers, and rear headroom is tight for the tall, while driving dynamics are tuned for relaxed comfort over sporty responses. Nonetheless, it remains a formidable value and should be a top consideration for budget-conscious sedan buyers and small families seeking reliability, comfort, and peace of ownership. Rating scores not explicitly provided in reviews, but overall critical sentiment is positive with caveats over feature misses.
model_summary: Ideal for urban families needing comfort, efficiency, spacious boot, diesel CVT, advanced ADAS safety, and 10-year warranty at value pricing.

summary:
KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- Powertrain: Dual electric motors, eDrive50 variant, combined output of 544 hp.
- Battery Capacity: 101.7 kWh usable, ARAI-certified range of 603 km; tested real-world range of 466.6 km (77% of claimed).
- Acceleration: 0-100 km/h in 4.7 seconds; 10-second boost mode enabling maximum power output.
- Suspension and Ride: Air suspension with adjustable ride height; absorbs road imperfections exceptionally well; 21-inch wheels with 35-section tires.
- Rear-Wheel Steering: All-wheel steering with rear-axle steer; aids significantly in maneuverability; allows sedan-like ease in U-turns and tight urban spaces, despite 5.4m length.
- Automatic Intelligent Doors: All four doors are electrically operated, sense obstacles before opening; facilitate effortless entry/exit.
- Interior Technology: 32-inch drop-down Theater Screen at rear, multi-mode ambient experience (Theatre, Relax, Expressive, Art, Efficient, Personal, Sport).
- Rear Seat Experience: Airline-style electrically reclining seats with heating, cooling, and massage; rear doors house smartphone-sized operation panels for personalized controls.
- Infotainment: Curved display, OS8 system, augmented reality HUD, voice control across major vehicle functions.
- Advanced Driver Assistance: Reversal Assist (auto retracing stored maneuvers), adaptive cruise, all-around parking aids, augmented reality navigation.
- Luxurious Cabin Elements: Extensive glass-crystal-cut switchgear and controls.
- Build and Styling: Length of approximately 5.4 meters; upright stance, illuminated and enlarged signature kidney grille; LED crystal headlights; flush door handles; massive 21-inch alloy wheels.
- Exclusivity: Sold in India as a CBU (completely built unit); unique exterior silhouette similar to Rolls Royce.

---

REVIEW SUMMARY STRUCTURE

1. OVERVIEW  
   - The BMW i7 redefines luxury in the electric segment, blending traditional premium cues with a tech-focused approach. Praised for its opulent interior, advanced tech, and effortless performance. Reviewer: CarWale (multiple contributors mentioned).

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING  
   - Dual-motor setup, 544 hp; 0-100 km/h in 4.7 seconds; has a 10-second boost mode unleashing full power. Instant, silent acceleration; exceptionally refined, nearly noiseless operation. Air suspension offers outstanding ride quality, soaks up imperfections. Large wheels do not hamper comfort. Rear-wheel steering makes maneuverability easy, matches midsize sedans despite size. All-wheel steering provides nimble handling, direct steering feel. Braking: No detailed figures, but stopping inspires confidence. Transmission: Single-speed reduction gear, instant torque delivery; paddle-activated boost mode.

3. EXTERIOR  
   - Silhouette reminiscent of Rolls Royce; upright stance, long bonnet, illuminated oversized kidney grille (visually striking especially at night), sleek LED crystal headlamps, insipid flush-type door handles. Rear styling less distinctive, saved by slim taillights. Stands out for size (approx. 5.4m long), 21-inch alloys. Polarizing design, but strong road presence; attracts attention across age demographics.

4. INTERIOR  
   - Mix of futuristic and traditional BMW elements. Dual curved displays, abundant glass-crystal controls; some trim/bits shared with lesser BMWs noted as low-rent for segment. Front seats: very comfortable with full suite of adjustments, heating, ventilation, massage. Rear: Airline-style recliner seats (heated/cooled/massaging), vast space, smartphone-sized touch controls, 32-inch Theater Screen. Multi-function modes controlling blinds, lighting, massage, audio. Not classically plush but feels technologically advanced and grand.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES  
   - Infotainment: Curved screen with latest OS8, voice and touch controls, complicated interface but extensive features. 32-inch rear Theater Screen, modes to change cabin ambience (relax/theatre/art/personal/etc.). Rear touch panels for functions. Augmented reality head-up display; digital instrument cluster. Driver assist: Advanced parking aids, reverse assistant with path memory. Theatre mode includes screen, blinds, seat, and lighting adjustments.

6. SAFETY  
   - Standard advanced safety kit for segment: airbags, ABS, stability control. Advanced driver aids (adaptive cruise, parking assists, 360 camera implied). Unique: automatic obstacle-sensing doors. No official crash rating mentioned.

7. FUEL ECONOMY  
   - ARAI range: 603 km. Real-world tested range: 466.6 km (77% of claim). Daily 50 km commute used about 10% battery. Charging cost: approx. Rs 3,000 for a week's use. DC fast charging required (issues reported with slow AC charging). Not as efficient as smaller EVs, but range ample for regular urban use; some planning required for longer journeys due to charging infrastructure.

8. VALUE AND PRICING  
   - Price: Rs 2.08-2.14 crore (OTR Mumbai, as tested); only one trim (eDrive50 M Sport) as CBU import. Price difference to petrol 7 Series variant is not very large. Value judged high for occupant experience and tech fest, though some interior bits considered below par for price. No warranty or maintenance details provided.

9. PROS AND CONS  
   - Pros: State-of-the-art tech, phenomenal ride comfort, silent and swift performance, luxurious rear seat experience (especially in Theatre/Relax modes), nimble handling for size. Automatic/intelligent doors, striking design, road presence, advanced rear-wheel steering, extensive ambient/cabin personalization.  
   - Cons: Some interior parts feel unworthy of price; interface usability a learning curve; design divisive; lower ground clearance with long wheelbase can make city navigation/parking challenging. Occasional AC charging issues.

10. COMPETITORS  
   - Main rival: Mercedes-Benz EQS (favoured by traditional luxury seekers). Comparison: i7 offers bolder design, unique tech-laden personality, and slightly higher pricing due to CBU import. EQS strengths: more conventional luxury, potentially better charging/efficiency. i7 stands out for tech immersion, rear seat experience, and performance.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT  
   - Only eDrive50 M Sport trim presently available in India (CBU import). Fully loaded; all standout features included. Reviewer does not specify a recommended variant.

12. VERDICT  
   - The BMW i7 is a showcase of cutting-edge technology, opulent passenger experience, and segment-leading refinement, targeting the modern, tech-embracing luxury buyer. Traditional luxury expectations (plushness, understated design) may not be fully met. Best for urban executives and self-made buyers drawn to innovation and digital extravagance. Not optimal for those who prize conventional controls, understated design, or require ICE-like ease of long-distance travel.  
   - No numerical rating provided.  
   - Standout qualities: effortless acceleration, benchmark ride comfort, showpiece cabin technology, supreme rear seat luxury, and curbside presence. Drawbacks: usability quirks, some value for money questions, mixed charging experience, and polarizing design.  
   - In summary: A uniquely impressive, high-tech flagship EV that reimagines luxury for a new era—BMW’s most advanced sedan for buyers seeking more spectacle than tradition.
model_summary: Opulent, tech-packed electric luxury sedan ideal for chauffeured city families, rear-seat comfort seekers, and executives prioritizing innovation over traditional plushness.

summary:
KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- 2.0-Litre Multijet Turbo-Diesel Engine: 168bhp power, 350Nm torque; four-cylinder unit delivers strong low-end torque and quiet operation; engine clatter well-contained, minimal steering vibrations.
- Transmission: Six-speed manual available on front-wheel drive (FWD) trims; nine-speed torque converter automatic on FWD and 4WD variants; manual mode for more control, but no paddle shifters.

- Ground Clearance & Angles: 203mm ground clearance; approach angle 21.5°, departure angle 23.6°, break-over angle 23.1°; crawl ratio 20.426; water fording up to 16 inches.
- Suspension: Independent front and rear, Frequency Selective Damping (FSD), Hydraulic Rebound Stopper (HRS) for mature ride quality; smooth over rough roads, minimal cabin disturbance.
- Wheels: 18-inch alloy wheels across most variants; distinctive spider-like design; special editions feature diamond-cut alloys.
- Boot Space: Up to 670 litres with rear rows folded; practical flat floor, 60:40 split for second row, 50:50 split for third row.
- Seating: Three-row, seven-seater; powered, ventilated front seats with memory (top trims); one-touch tumble second-row; third row best for short journeys/children.
- Interior: Plush dual-tone brown-black theme; soft-touch materials, brushed aluminium and piano black accents; brown or seal grey leather upholstery with detailed stitching in higher trims; excellent fit and finish.
- Digital Cluster & Infotainment: 10.2-inch digital instrument cluster; 10.1-inch touchscreen infotainment with wireless Android Auto & Apple CarPlay; Alpine nine-speaker sound system; wireless charging pad.
- Rear Entertainment: Optional 11.6-inch Wi-Fi touchscreen rear entertainment package (special editions).
- Practicality: Ample cabin storage (bottle holders, slits for phones, large glovebox, armrest storage); panoramic sunroof, powered tailgate, multi-zone and dual-zone climate control.
- Safety: Six airbags standard, 360-degree camera, ABS with EBD, electronic stability control, traction control, Hill Start Assist, Automatic Vehicle Hold, all-passenger seatbelt alert, curtain airbags, TPMS, electronic parking brake, rain-sensing front wipers. Top trims add ADAS functions (Lane Keep Assist, Collision Mitigation).
- Exterior: Jeep’s signature seven-slot grille, squared wheel arches, dual-tone floating roof, spider alloys, high-quality paint options (Brilliant Black, Pearl White, Magnesio Grey, Galaxy Blue, Techno Metallic Green, Velvet Red, Silvery Moon, special edition colors).
- Special Editions: Meridian X (urban focus—Silvery Moon paint, grey roof), Meridian Upland (adventure focus—roof carrier, sunshades, hood decal, cargo mats), both get unique styling cues and additional lifestyle equipment.
- Pricing: Ex-showroom range approx. Rs. 32.95 lakh to Rs. 38.47 lakh for special editions, Rs. 34.3 lakh for 4x2 automatic; undercuts main rivals on price.
- Warranty: Standard 3 years/1 lakh km, extendable to 5 years/1.5 lakh km; 3-year maintenance program, unlimited towing support, passenger assistance.

---

REVIEW SUMMARY

1. OVERVIEW
   - Jeep Meridian, evaluated by CarWale and other publications, is a three-row monocoque SUV for India, targeting buyers upgrading from Compass and rivalling Toyota Fortuner and MG Gloster. Combines off-road heritage with premium interior and strong value. Reviewer: Kaustubh Gandhi, CarWale.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
   - Engine: 2.0-litre turbo-diesel, 168bhp, 350Nm; four-cylinder.
   - Transmission: Six-speed manual (FWD), nine-speed automatic (FWD and AWD); manual mode but lacks paddle shifters.
   - 0-100 km/h: Claimed 10.8 sec; respectable for 1.85-tonne weight.
   - Response: Smooth, refined power delivery; vibration/clatter minimal; slight lag/shifting delay in automatic on hard acceleration.
   - Ride: Mature, composed thanks to FSD and HRS suspension; soaks up rough roads, minimal cabin disruption.
   - Handling: Steering light at low speeds, heavier at high speeds, good precision; 5.7m turning radius suits city use. Confident at highway speeds and around corners.
   - Braking: Noted as stable and confidence-inspiring, no specific distances given.
   - Off-road: Excellent; approach 21.5°, departure 23.6°, break-over 23.1°, 203mm ground clearance, 18-inch wheels, crawl ratio 20.426; AWD model with hill descent; water fording 16 inches. Articulation and traction praised.
   - NVH: Well-controlled; refined performance in urban and rural settings.

3. EXTERIOR
   - Design: Resembles elongated Compass; squared arches, iconic Jeep grille, unique dual-tone floating roof effect. Special editions bring distinct paint (Silvery Moon, Galaxy Blue), grey accents.
   - Size: Full-size three-row, 4.7m length; larger than Compass by 364mm, wheelbase 146mm longer.
   - Wheels: 18-inch alloys, diamond-cut on special models.
   - Colors: Multiple premium shades; special edition hues highlighted.
   - Features: Chrome and gloss black trim; adventure editions add roof carriers and decals.

4. INTERIOR
   - Layout: Modern, upmarket; dual-tone brown-black, soft-touch dash, brushed aluminium, piano black.
   - Seating: Comfortable, ventilated, powered front seats (driver seat with memory); excellent support in front and middle rows.
   - Third Row: Limited space; tight legroom/under-thigh support, best for children or short trips; one-touch tumble middle row for access.
   - Cargo: Huge boot (up to 670L) with seats folded; usable storage even with all rows up.
   - Practicality: Multiple cupholders, bottle slots, armrest/glovebox storage; vertical mobile slits; wide-opening doors (80°) for access.
   - Special: Optional rear 11.6-inch entertainment; electrical tailgate controls accessible from multiple points; large panoramic sunroof.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
   - Infotainment: 10.1-inch screen, wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto; quick, user-friendly interface; integrated nav/maps; physical AC controls retained.
   - Cluster: 10.2-inch full-digital with color graphics and multi-info display.
   - Sound: Nine-speaker Alpine audio system; good acoustics.
   - Connectivity: Wireless charging pad (front), USB Type-A/Type-C (front), Type-A (rear), no charging for third row.
   - Features: Jeep Life connected tech (tracking, remote features); speed limiter, 360-degree camera with five views, physical parking guides.
   - Special Edition: Wi-Fi rear screen, blue mood lighting, boot mat, wireless keyless entry, rain-sensing wipers, cornering fog lamps.

6. SAFETY
   - Airbags: Six standard (incl. curtain airbags); all-seat belt alerts; detection system for front occupants.
   - Driver Aids: ABS, EBD, stability and traction control, hill-start assist, automatic vehicle hold, electronic parking brake, electronic roll mitigation, TPMS, 360° camera, front and rear parking sensors.
   - ADAS: Top 'Overland' variant features Level 2 ADAS (lane keep assist, collision mitigation, more than ten advanced features).
   - Chassis: Hot-stamped, high-strength steel sections for rigidity.
   - Rating: No NCAP for Meridian yet; Jeep Compass (same platform) scored five stars.
   - Misses: No adaptive cruise, blind-spot, lane departure warning, or HUD (could have been included, given segment trends).

7. FUEL ECONOMY
   - Official Figures: Not explicitly provided in review.
   - Real-World (CarWale test): 10.09 km/l (city), 14.49 km/l (highway) for 1.85-ton FWD automatic version.
   - Comparison: Efficient within segment; praised for balancing power and economy.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
   - Ex-showroom Price: Rs. 32.95 lakh (base special edition) to Rs. 38.47 lakh (top special edition); 4x2 automatic at Rs. 34.3 lakh; undercuts main rivals (Toyota Fortuner, MG Gloster).
   - Value: Strong on features, finish, off-road ability; competitive pricing for equipment level.
   - Warranty: 3 years/1 lakh km standard; extendable to 5 years or 1.5 lakh km. Three-year maintenance plan included; unlimited towing and passenger assistance.

9. PROS AND CONS

   Pros:
   - Excellent off-road capability; advanced AWD system, superior approach/departure/break-over angles, hill descent, water fording
   - Refined, powerful diesel with good NVH
   - Smooth ride quality; robust and mature suspension
   - Premium, well-built, feature-rich interior (ventilated, powered seats)
   - Large boot with flexible storage
   - High safety equipment levels; ADAS in upper trims
   - Competitive pricing relative to rivals
   - Distinct special editions for urban/adventure buyers

   Cons:
   - Automatic transmission slow to downshift under hard acceleration; absence of paddle shifters
   - Third-row space tight for adults; not suitable for long journeys
   - Base versions lack sunroof, ventilated seats, wireless charging
   - Charging/cooling provisions limited for third-row occupants
   - No adaptive cruise, blind-spot, lane warning, other ADAS features on most variants
   - Design not differentiated enough from Compass
   - Limited aftersales/dealer network in some regions

10. COMPETITORS
   - Direct Rivals: Toyota Fortuner, MG Gloster
   - Strengths vs. Rivals: Lower price for similar features; richer feature list at similar or lower price; better on-road manners and off-road capability than many unibody 7-seaters; more luxurious interior than Fortuner
   - Weaknesses: Third-row less usable than Fortuner/Gloster; less brand cachet and network vs. Toyota; no petrol option.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
   - Trims: Core trims include Limited, Limited(O), Overland; special editions “X” (lifestyle/urban) and “Upland” (adventure/outdoors); features vary—higher trims get ventilated, powered seats, ADAS, sunroof.
   - Drivelines: FWD (manual/auto), AWD (auto only)
   - Recommended: Review points to Limited(O) and Overland for wide feature set and value, especially for urban and tech-savvy buyers; special editions add unique cosmetic/practical upgrades; base variants lose some premium features.

12. VERDICT
   - The Jeep Meridian is a premium, refined, and well-equipped three-row SUV that excels in off-road capability and comfort, with excellent ride quality and interior luxury, making it an appealing alternative in the segment. Best suited to buyers seeking Jeep’s ruggedness with on-road sophistication and a lavish cabin but who are willing to compromise on third-row space for occasional use only. Especially attractive for current Compass owners, families needing a flexible boot, or buyers desiring standout design/features at a lower price than Fortuner/Gloster. Rating not numerically specified in review, but sentiment is strongly positive on value and niche appeal; minor shortcomings noted in third-row usability and gearshift speed.

MAHINDRA SCORPIO-N

---

KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- Platform & Build: Ladder-frame chassis, 41% high-strength steel in the body (segment-leading), 81% high-strength steel in the ladder frame for improved torsional rigidity and safety. Body is 13% lighter, ladder frame 10% lighter than predecessor.
- Dimensions: Length 4,662mm, width 1,917mm, height 1,857mm, wheelbase 2,750mm; offers significant road presence and spacious interior for the segment.
- Engines & Powertrains:
    - Petrol: 2.0-litre mStallion TGDi, 200bhp @ 5,000rpm, 370Nm (manual)/380Nm (automatic) torque.
    - Diesel: 2.2-litre mHawk in two states – 130bhp/300Nm (Z2, Z4); 172bhp/370Nm (manual)/400Nm (automatic).
    - Both engines with six-speed manual and six-speed automatic (torque converter) options.
    - 4WD capability with 4XPLOR system (four terrain modes: Normal, Snow, Mud & Ruts, Sand; low and high ranges).
    - Mechanical and brake locking differentials for improved off-road ability.
    - Diesel auto provides three drive modes: Zip, Zap, Zoom.
- Exterior Features:
    - Signature six-slat grille with chrome inserts; double barrel LED projector headlamps; LED DRLs and fog lights; sequential LED turn indicators; vertically stacked LED tail lamps.
    - 17-inch or 18-inch alloy wheels (variant dependent), razor-cut design; contrasting roof rails and skid plates, shark fin antenna.
    - Available in seven colors: Deep Forest, Napoli Black, Everest White, Red Rage, Dazzling Silver, Royal Gold, Grand Canyon.
- Interior Features:
    - All-new cabin, coffee-black (dark brown) leatherette upholstery, soft-touch materials, piano black and brushed metal inserts, metal-finish dual rails for center console.
    - Two seating layouts: 7-seat (bench in middle row) or 6-seat (second row captain seats with walk-through access).
    - Electrically-adjustable driver’s seat in higher variants; large and supportive front seats, high seating position for enhanced visibility.
    - Second row generous in legroom/shoulder room. Third-row front-facing, best for children due to limited space/upholstery, upright backrest, low under-thigh support.
    - Multiple interior storage options: cooled glovebox, large cup holders (1L), bottle holders in doors, large center armrest bin, USB-A and wireless charging pad.
- Infotainment & Tech:
    - 8-inch touchscreen (top variants) with Sony 3D sound system (12 speakers, subwoofer, amplifier).
    - Android Auto and Apple CarPlay (wireless in top trims), Bluetooth, Alexa integration, AdrenoX connected car suite (geo-fencing, remote start, temp control).
    - 7-inch digital-analogue instrument cluster with color MID.
    - Push-button start, auto headlamps, cruise control, two-zone climate control, wireless charging, AC vents with blower control for second row.
- Safety:
    - Global NCAP 5-star crash safety rating.
    - Six airbags (front, side, curtain in upper variants), ABS, ESP, hill hold/descent control, all-wheel disc brakes, driver drowsiness alert, ISOFIX child seat anchors, tire pressure monitoring system.
    - Rear and front parking cameras/sensors on top models.
    - Lacking ADAS and 360-degree camera; no auto-dimming IRVM.
- Variants: Z2, Z4, Z6, Z8, Z8L. Key variant features:
    - Z2/Z4: Second row AC vents, fabric upholstery, LED taillights, basic touchscreen audio, steering audio controls, 17-inch wheels, front airbags, ABS/ESP.
    - Z6: Sunroof, drive modes (diesel), wireless smartphone mirroring, connected car tech.
    - Z8: Push button start, electrically foldable mirrors, side/curtain airbags, dual-zone climate, rear camera, tire pressure monitoring.
    - Z8L: 8-inch Sony infotainment, front parking sensors/camera, 18-inch wheels, captain seats, electric driver’s seat.
- Price & Warranty:
    - Petrol: Rs 11.99 lakh (Z2 MT) to Rs 18.99 lakh (Z8L).
    - Diesel: Rs 12.49 lakh to Rs 19.49 lakh depending on variant; pricing for 4WD/automatic trims not fully announced.
    - Standard warranty: 3 years/unlimited km + roadside assistance; extended warranty available.

---

REVIEW SUMMARY

1. OVERVIEW
   - The Mahindra Scorpio-N is a full-size, body-on-frame three-row SUV, targeting buyers looking for rugged capability, strong performance, and modern features. Significant improvements over previous Scorpio in ride, refinement, cabin quality, and on-road dynamics. Multiple reviewers (CarWale, Kaustubh Gandhi, Dheeraj Giri) praise the SUV’s evolution and appeal across Indian conditions.
   
2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
   - Engine options detailed above.
   - 2.0 petrol: 200bhp/380Nm, six-speed AT, 0-100kmph in 10.44s (auto), 0-60kmph in 4.94s, 20-80kmph roll-on in 5.98s, 40-100kmph in 7.55s.
   - 2.2 diesel: 172bhp/400Nm (auto), 130bhp/300Nm in lower variants; strong low/mid-range torque; smooth up to 3,000rpm then some diesel clatter.
   - Diesel auto quick and responsive; upshifts early under light throttle; three drive modes: Zip (city), Zap (balanced), Zoom (sporty).
   - Petrol delivers smooth, refined, silent operation; never feels underpowered, responds well both in city and highway conditions.
   - Gearboxes: Six-speed automatic (torque converter, quick and seamless at low throttle, relaxed at speed) and six-speed manual.
   - Handling: Much improved steering; light at low speeds, well-weighted on highways, inspires confidence. Remarkable ride comfort for ladder-frame – new double-wishbone front, Watt's linkage rear. Flatter over undulations, lateral movement well controlled, absorbs potholes/speed-breakers with ease.
   - Braking: All-wheel discs, confident performance; stopping distance not specified.
   - Off-road: 4XPLOR system, four terrain modes, mechanical/brake locking diffs, 2WD and 4WD. Shift-by-cable tech on transmissions.

3. EXTERIOR
   - Design: Butch, upright, imposing SUV stance; signature chrome grille, LED headlamps, C-shaped DRLs, sequential indicators, vertical tail lamps.
   - 17/18-inch alloys with razor-cut finish; roof rails/skid plates in contrasting color.
   - Size: Class-leader presence with near-4.7m length, high shoulder-line.
   - Colors: Seven options as described.
   - Stands out for sheer size and presence; compares well to key rivals in visual appeal.

4. INTERIOR
   - Material quality: Coffee-black/dark brown leatherette, contrasting brushed metal and piano black; extensive soft-touch surfaces.
   - Dashboard: Upright, traditional, premium quality, analogue dials with digital MID (not digital panel as in XUV700).
   - Seating: High seating for visibility; spacious and comfortable first/second rows; six-way electronically adjustable driver’s seat (top trims).
   - Second row: Good shoulder/leg room; bench or captain seat option.
   - Third row: Forward-facing, compromised space – best for children, low under-thigh support, knees-up posture, upright backrest.
   - Storage: Usable cubbies, cooled glovebox, door bottle holders, large center armrest bin, two large cupholders, less ideal phone storage when wireless charging.
   - Cargo: Approx. 786L with 2nd/3rd row folded.
   - Practicality: Large, easy-entry cabin (with side steps); ease of access to third row (captain seat version allows walk-through).
   - Ergonomics: Most controls easy to reach; some buttons/knobs lack tactile feedback.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
   - Infotainment: 8-inch Sony-powered touchscreen, 12 speakers/subwoofer/amplifier in Z8L; Android Auto, Apple CarPlay (wireless on higher trims); 7-inch digital-analogue driver cluster.
   - Connected car features: AdrenoX suite, Alexa integration, remote vehicle functions, geo-fencing, vehicle health, wireless charging.
   - Climate: Dual-zone automatic AC, rear AC vents with separate blower.
   - Seating: Electric driver seat adjust, push-button start, cruise control, auto headlamps, front/rear parking cameras and sensors (top trims).
   - Missing: No ventilated seats, no 360-degree camera, no auto-dimming IRVM, steering lacks reach (telescopic) adjustment in all variants.

6. SAFETY
   - Safety rating: 5-star Global NCAP crash rating.
   - Standard features: Six airbags (frontal, side, curtain – variant-dependent), ABS, ESP, hill-hold/descent, four-wheel disc brakes, ISOFIX, tire-pressure monitoring.
   - Advanced features: Driver drowsiness alert.
   - Cameras: Front and rear (top variants); no 360-degree camera, no ADAS.
   - Structure: Heavily reinforced platform and body using high-strength steel.
   - Child safety: Front-facing third-row for improved crash safety.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
   - Diesel AT: 12.16kmpl (city), 14.64kmpl (highway) as tested.
   - Petrol AT: 8.34kmpl (city), 11.17kmpl (highway) as tested.
   - Real-world figures slightly lower than segment leaders; diesel efficiency adequate for class, petrol efficiency below average.
   - Not as frugal as some rivals, particularly with petrol.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
   - Price: Petrol Rs 11.99–18.99 lakh, Diesel Rs 12.49–19.49 lakh (ex-showroom, variant dependent).
   - Warranty: 3 years/unlimited km standard, roadside assistance included, extended warranty offered.
   - Residuals: Predicted to be strong due to Scorpio brand value.
   - Maintenance costs/service intervals: Not specified in review.

9. PROS AND CONS

   Pros:
   - Class-leading road presence and size.
   - Powerful, refined petrol and diesel engines; strong performance for class.
   - Smooth, responsive automatics; improved dynamics and ride comfort.
   - Robust 4XPLOR 4WD system; terrain modes; excellent off-road capability.
   - Upmarket, spacious and practical interior; premium materials.
   - Feature-rich: Sony audio, sunroof, wireless charging, dual-zone AC, connected car tech.
   - 5-star crash safety; six airbags, ESP, child-friendlier third-row design.

   Cons:
   - Cramped third row, best for children; non-sliding second row in bench layout hampers access.
   - Missing some essential and segment-expected features: ventilated seats, 360-degree camera, reach-adjustable steering, auto-dimming IRVM.
   - Petrol versions less fuel efficient; higher running costs.
   - Top-end variants are costly relative to some rivals.
   - Some interior buttons/knobs lack tactile quality; glovebox feels flimsy.
   - Large size can make parking challenging; no 360-degree camera compounds this.

10. COMPETITORS
   - Main Rivals: Mahindra XUV700, Tata Safari, Hyundai Alcazar, MG Hector Plus, Kia Carens, Toyota Innova Crysta (loose size/function overlap), Scorpio Classic (Mahindra's own).
   - Compared to XUV700: Not as agile, more rugged; better for rough/tough use; lacks full digital cockpit/luxury feel.
   - Compared to Safari/Hector Plus: More rugged off-road; similar or better engine performance; less luxury/finesse overall.
   - Unique selling points: Ladder-frame construction (unusual in segment), true 4X4 capability, unmatched road presence, high body/ladder frame strength.
   - Key weaknesses: Efficiency (petrol), lack of some tech/luxury features present in XUV700 or Safari.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
   - Five Trims: Z2 (entry), Z4, Z6, Z8, Z8L (fully loaded).
   - Z6 adds sunroof, drive modes (diesel), wireless smartphone mirroring.
   - Z8/Z8L bring advanced safety, infotainment, and comfort features.
   - Z8L strongly recommended for feature-seekers, those seeking a premium experience.
   - Lower variants deliver core Scorpio-N traits at a more affordable price but lose out on many comfort/convenience goodies.

12. VERDICT
   - The Mahindra Scorpio-N is a transformational upgrade, offering a rare combination of toughness, refinement, and modern features in its segment. It remains the go-to ladder-frame SUV with true go-anywhere ability, improved comfort and usability, and is the best choice for buyers who value robust construction and adventure-readiness over luxury. Not as plush or urban-centric as some monocoque rivals, but unparalleled off-road capability and sheer presence make it hard to overlook. Weaknesses in fuel efficiency (petrol), cramped third row, and some missing features prevent it from being the perfect all-rounder. Highly recommended for families needing a tough, versatile Indian SUV, provided the third row is not a daily necessity for adults and premium features aren’t dealbreakers.
   - Rating score: Not specifically provided in review. Sentiment is strongly positive with caveats on practicality and value for top variants.
model_summary: Ideal for families seeking rugged adventure, strong diesel performance, true 4WD, modern features, and class-leading safety in Indian conditions.

   - Off-road: Terrain Response 2, ground clearance 294mm, wading depth 900mm—true to Land Rover off-road heritage.

   - Rear seat: Tablet module for full rear control, motorized console functions.

6. SAFETY

   - Standard: Up to 9 airbags (some sources state 6), ABS with EBD, ESP, traction control, TPMS.
   - Advanced: Blind Spot Monitoring, Park Assist, Level 2 Advanced Driver Assistance Systems, 360-degree camera suite.
   - Unique: Safety features tightly integrated with luxury/comfort tech.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
   - Official: Not stated in review.
   - Tested (3.0L diesel LWB): City consumption at 9.02 kmpl, highway at 12.26 kmpl—excellent given performance and weight.
   - Comparison: Above expectation for size and segment; specifics versus rivals not quoted.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
   - Price: Rs 2.38 crore–Rs 3.43 crore ex-showroom (Rs 3.16 crore for 3.0L diesel LWB Autobiography).
   - Value: Class-leading in luxury, tech, and comfort; high cost justified by status and content, but options priced steeply.
   - Warranty/service: Not mentioned in review.
   - Maintenance: Not mentioned in review.

9. PROS AND CONS
   Pros:
    - Commanding road presence, standout design.
    - Plush, meticulously crafted, highly comfortable cabin with segment-leading rear seat amenities.
    - Extensive tech and luxury features; true "wow factor."
    - Brilliant ride comfort, exceptional refinement regardless of engine.
    - Massive performance from V8 options, strong across all powertrains.
    - Robust mechanicals for both road and off-road use.
    - Outstanding off-road abilities.
   Cons:
    - Expensive both to buy and especially to option generously.
    - Not sporty to drive; driving engagement takes a back seat to comfort.
    - Size/shape means not agile; not a driver’s SUV.

10. COMPETITORS
    - Closest rival: Mercedes-Benz Maybach GLS.
    - Comparison: Range Rover trumps in exclusivity, price, and "wow factor"; Maybach rivals on price and interior luxury.
    - Unique points: Only full-size luxury SUV with such a breadth of powertrains, off-road pedigree to match on-road comfort, and bespoke customization.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
    - Trims: Multiple trims with variations in features/powertrains; LWB and optional third-row expand range.
    - Recommendation: Autobiography LWB 3.0L diesel highlighted in review as test model, considered a strong all-rounder.
    - Others: Range includes both performance (V8) and eco-friendly (PHEV, incoming electric) options.

12. VERDICT
    - The Range Rover remains the reference for ultra-premium SUVs, blending timeless design, extraordinary ride comfort, unmatched rear-seat luxury, and genuine off-road capability. Pricey but peerless for those seeking pinnacle luxury, technology, and exclusivity on four wheels. Ideal for wealthy buyers prioritizing comfort, status, and customization over keener on-road driving experience. The new Range Rover furthers the legacy—more advanced, more opulent, and more versatile than ever.

summary:
KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- Dedicated Acti.EV Platform: Ground-up electric architecture, not an ICE adaptation; underpins Tata’s new-gen EV lineup, enhances packaging and safety.
- Battery Options: Two choices—25kWh battery (claimed 315km range, 80bhp/114Nm); 35kWh Long Range (claimed 421km range, 120bhp/190Nm); liquid-cooled, IP67-rated for dust and water resistance.
- Motor Performance: 80bhp/114Nm (Standard), 120bhp/190Nm/121bhp (Long Range); instantaneous torque for quick response.
- Charging: 
  - 3.3kW AC wallbox: 10-100% in 9.4 hours (standard); 13.5 hours (Long Range).
  - 7.2/7.4kW AC charger (optional LR): 10-100% in 5 hours (real-world test: 7.5 hours 0-100%; 6 hours 35-100%; 2 hours 65-100%).
  - 50kW DC fast charger: 10-80% in 56 minutes.
- Regenerative Braking: Three levels (L1-L3); configurable with paddle shifters; L3 allows near single-pedal driving experience.
- Drive Modes: Three—Eco (maximum efficiency), City (balanced), Sport (maximum performance).
- Transmission: Single-speed automatic; jewelled rotary dial selector; includes hill-hold/auto-hold and hill-descent control functions.

  - Electric sunroof (segment-first, Hinglish voice command compatible), dual-tone paint options.
- Dimensions: Compact proportions suitable for urban driving; 366-litre boot; no detailed measurements provided.
- Interior Features: Piano black accented dashboard, dual 10.25-inch screens (instrument cluster, infotainment), touch-sensitive haptic AC panel, vegan leather upholstery with blue stitching, 2-spoke multifunction leatherette steering wheel, 90-degree opening doors, cooled and illuminated glovebox, ventilated front seats, adjustable headrests front/rear.
- Storage and Practicality: Multiple cupholders, dedicated frunk for charging cable, wireless charger (front), USB-A and USB-C (fast charging) ports, large door bins, armrest storage, seat-back pockets; rear row: limited legroom, adequate shoulder space, no charging ports or AC vents.

- Segment Standouts: Electric sunroof, frunk (front boot), multiple drive/regen modes, colours/trims diversity, comprehensive safety suite, infotainment with streaming and gaming.

REVIEW SUMMARY

1. OVERVIEW
   - The Tata Punch EV is Tata's compact electric SUV built on a dedicated EV platform. It offers strong safety, modern tech, and practical city usability but comes at a premium price.    - User Experience: Voice assistant integration, touch haptic AC panel, auto-dimming IRVM.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
   - Claimed Range: 25kWh—315km; 35kWh (Long Range)—421km (claimed).

   - Charging Times: 3.3kW AC—9.4–13.5h (10–100%); 7.2kW AC—5h LR (tested: 7.5h, 0–100%); DC fast charger—56min (10–80%).

8. VALUE AND PRICING

   - Warranty/Maintenance: Not specified in the review.

9. PROS AND CONS
   - Pros:
     - Realistic range estimation and accurate DTE display.
     - Extensive safety suite, BNCAP 5-star rating.
     - Modern, distinctive compact SUV styling; feature-rich.
     - Good city comfort, ride quality, and practicality (turning radius, maneuverability).

   - Cons:

     - Higher pricing for upper trims and optional features.

10. COMPETITORS

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT

    - Features: Higher trims get sunroof, larger battery, advanced screens, 360-cam, ventilated seats, etc.
    - Recommendation: Not explicitly stated but Long Range (LR) most practical for maximizing usable range and features, albeit at premium.

12. VERDICT
    - Strengths: Excellent city car with safety, tech, comfort; suitable for buyers prioritizing safety, urban ease, and modern features. Ideal for everyday commuting, errands, single-car families in metro cities with home charging.
    - Weaknesses: Limited highway utility due to real-world range and charging infrastructure gaps; some construction and electronics consistency issues; high pricing for top variants.
    - Overall: Segment-leading features and crash safety make Punch EV a standout among compact urban EVs, but value less compelling for long-distance users or those reliant on public charging. Rating not explicitly given.

If a section is not addressed (“Not mentioned in review”)—Warranty/maintenance costs not discussed. Detailed dimensions/size not provided. No explicit trim recommendation. No numerical acceleration/braking figures beyond 0–100km/h time for LR.

summary:
KEY SPECS AND FEATURES

- Powertrain & Battery: Offered with two battery packs—65kWh (single motor, 235bhp) and 75kWh (dual motor, 390bhp/504Nm QWD AWD or RWD options). Dual-motor QWD provides all-wheel drive, the first AWD Tata since the Safari Storme.

- Acceleration & Performance: 0-100 km/h in 6.3 seconds (75kWh QWD), top speed 180 km/h (claimed).
- Charging: 7.2kW AC home charger—10-100% in 10.7 hours; 120kW DC fast charger—20-80% in ~25 minutes; 250km added in 15 minutes; V2L and V2V (vehicle-to-load/vehicle-to-vehicle charging) enabled.
- Chassis & Suspension: Based on Gen2 Acti.ev platform; independent suspension with Frequency-Selective Dampers; 205mm ground clearance; all-wheel disc brakes.
- Terrain & Traction: Six terrain modes (city, wet, sand, mud/ruts, snow, rough) plus boost and drift mode; drive mode electronics work with ESP.

- Storage: Spacious cabin for five adults, reduced-size spare wheel, generous boot (slight reduction vs ICE version).
- Exterior Standouts: EV-specific blanked-out grille, LED bi-projector headlamps, LED DRLs/connected tail lights, animated lighting, 19-inch dual-tone aero-optimized alloys, dual-tone paint, roof rails, integrated steps, shark-fin antenna, Stealth Edition (blacked-out), four main color options.
- Smart Safety Features: 6/7 airbags, TPMS, EPB with auto hold, all-wheel disc brakes, ESP with i-VBAC, hill descent, traction, roll-over mitigation, reverse camera & sensors, Level 2 ADAS, knee airbag, 540-degree surround camera (segment innovation), AVAS, electronic IRVM.
- Additional Tech: Blind spot monitoring, memory function for front seats/ORVMs, fast charging payments, Arcade.ev app, phygital dashboard buttons, illuminated steering logo.
- Segment-Firsts/Innovations: QWD all-wheel drive, 14.5-inch QLED infotainment, 540-degree transparent view, e-valet and Summon, auto park, Stealth Edition, JBL Dolby Atmos 5.1 system.

REVIEW SUMMARY

1. OVERVIEW
   - The Tata Harrier EV is Tata’s electric flagship SUV, built on the Acti.ev platform, engineered for Indian roads with a strong suite of tech, safety and convenience features, available in Adventure, Fearless, Empowered personas and a Stealth Edition. Review by CarWale, input from Bharat Mobility Expo 2025 coverage.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
   - 65kWh (235bhp RWD, ~505km range), 75kWh (390bhp, 504Nm QWD/AWD or RWD, max 627km). 0-100km/h in 6.3s (75kWh QWD), 180km/h top speed (claimed). Smooth, instantaneous acceleration, strong torque for easy overtaking, with distinct drive modes (Eco, City, Sport). QWD gives strong off-road performance, terrain response modes enhance capability; paddle-shifters adjust regen braking (three levels). Suspension tuned for comfort—independent with FSD, handles rough/uneven roads with composure and restricts cabin movement. Steering light yet connected, responsive at all speeds. All-disc brakes confident with strong bite and progression. AVAS system enhances low-speed pedestrian safety. Real-world range above 400km achievable even under spirited driving; full range not independently tested yet.

3. EXTERIOR
   - High-riding, mid-size electric SUV. Blanked-off grille for EV identity, new bumpers, aero-optimized 19-inch alloys. Enhanced animated lighting, LED bi-projector headlamps, connected tail-lights/DRLs. Dual-tone paint, roof rails, integrated steps, rear spoiler, shark-fin antenna, puddle lamps, contrast skid plate. Distinct Stealth Edition with blacked-out styling. Choice of four colors: Nainital Nocturne, Empowered Oxide, Pure Grey, Pristine White. Maintains bold road presence and stance of ICE Harrier with EV-specific refinements.

4. INTERIOR
   - Sleek, grey-and-white theme, upmarket feel. 14.53-inch QLED infotainment and 12.25-inch digital cluster dominate the dash. Smart digital shifter, illuminated four-spoke steering wheel, intuitive buttons. Ergonomic, spacious for five adults. Powered, ventilated, electronically adjustable front seats (with memory). Boss mode (front passenger), ample storage, dual-zone AC, rear sunshades, large panoramic sunroof. Rear seat supportive but padding/recline could improve. Quality concerns: occasional rough-edged panels, non-smudge-free piano black surfaces, slightly reduced spare wheel size. Boot space slightly diminished vs ICE, but still practical.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
   - 14.53-inch Samsung Neo QLED touchscreen, 12.25-inch digital cluster. JBL 10-speaker audio with Dolby Atmos 5.1, wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, Bluetooth, Arcade.ev apps. Panoramic sunroof, automatic tailgate, 65W USB-C charging front/rear. Connected car suite (iRA, OTA updates, DrivePay for charging/FASTag). Six terrain modes, boost/drift modes, Summon and auto park features, 540-degree surround camera, blind spot monitor, e-IRVM. Level 2 ADAS suite (adaptive cruise, collision warning, lane keep assist, more).

6. SAFETY
   - 5-star safety rating (mentioned). Six/seven airbags including knee airbag, Level 2 ADAS, EPB with auto-hold, TPMS, ESP with i-VBAC, hill assist/descend, traction/roll-over mitigation, all-disc brakes, 540-degree transparent mode, AVAS, reverse camera/sensors, electronic IRVM. Reverse assist, parking assist with sensors/camera standard.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
   - Up to 627km (ARAI/claimed) with 75kWh battery, 505km with 65kWh; real-world for top variant ~480-505km; spirited driving—achievable 400km+. Segment-leading range for Indian e-SUVs of its class. No direct comparison to competitors’ real-world economy provided.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
   - Top-spec models priced above Rs 30 lakh. Flagship status with tech and AWD comes at premium. Value assessed favorably at lower-mid trims for tech, space, performance, and range. Maintenance/costs/warranty/service intervals not mentioned.

9. PROS AND CONS
   - Pros: Genuine high-riding electric SUV; segment-leading features; impressive range and AWD performance; rich safety spec; plush interior; smooth and refined drive; strong real-world range; innovative tech (ADAS, QWD, auto parking).
   - Cons: Inconsistent cabin and panel quality; some electronic glitches; expensive top-spec trims; public charging infrastructure in India still lacking for true long-distance comfort; power modulation tricky in slow off-road use; rear seat comfort not best-in-class.

10. COMPETITORS
   - Rivals: Mahindra BE 6, Mahindra XUV.e9, Hyundai Creta Electric, Maruti Suzuki e-Vitara (upcoming). Unique selling points include QWD AWD, 600km+ range, segment-first tech/features, robust road presence. Competitors may offer lower pricing, more mature charging networks or softer suspension (noted Hyundai/Maruti familiarity), but none match the tech or powertrain breadth.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
   - Available personas: Adventure, Fearless, Empowered; plus Stealth Edition. Two main drivetrains: 65kWh (medium), 75kWh (long range). Recommended variant not specified in review; expectation is for Medium and Long Range trims by launch.

12. VERDICT
   - The Harrier EV combines bold design, genuine SUV capability (incl. AWD), impressive segment-leading range and advanced technology. It is well-suited for tech-savvy buyers seeking a high-riding, premium electric SUV with long range and strong presence. Some quality and price niggles on higher trims, but lower variants offer an excellent balance. Charging network in India remains a limitation for easy long-distance trips, but the Harrier EV raises the bar for the segment in electric innovation and execution. Rating score not specified.

     - Segment-leading wheelbase, best-in-class interior space.

REVIEW SUMMARY STRUCTURE

1. OVERVIEW
   - The fourth-generation BMW X3 represents a comprehensive update in the luxury midsize SUV segment, offering bigger dimensions, advanced tech, and two new 2.0-litre mild-hybrid powertrains. The design is bold and unique, but may polarize. Reviews sourced from CarWale and other Indian automotive outlets.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
   - Both 2.0-litre petrol (approx. 206–208bhp/320–330Nm) and 2.0-litre diesel (197bhp/400Nm) use 48V mild hybrid systems. The diesel achieves 0–100 km/h in 7.7 seconds (claimed), with smooth, refined, and quiet operation. Power delivery is strong at low and mid-revs, with adequate performance for daily drives and highway use, but lacks high-rev excitement or character, especially in petrol. M50 turbo petrol (400bhp) available in limited numbers for enthusiastic drivers. Transmission: 8-speed automatic is quick-shifting, seamless, intuitive in response, with well-calibrated driving modes (Sport preferred for engagement). Ride: Adaptive dampers deliver a notably cushioned, comfortable, and composed ride—improved over run-flats of predecessor. Large footprint and increased track width help stability and grip; handling is agile and planted, with direct but not overly communicative steering. Braking: Responsive; good pedal feel and bite, quick and confidence-inspiring stops.

3. EXTERIOR
   - Styling is chiseled, moving away from previous generation’s rounded contours. Signature BMW kidney grille (less controversial than on other new models), prominent LED adaptive headlights with dual L-shaped DRLs, Y-shaped LED tail lamps. Muscular stance, high-riding SUV proportions, blocky body lines, 20-inch wheels, and strong road presence. Bigger than rivals like Mercedes GLC. Black shade subtly masks size; overall look is unique but not universally appealing. Available color options include Calm Beige and Espresso Brown for interiors; exterior palette not detailed.

4. INTERIOR
   - Cabin design is premium, influenced by new 5 and 7 Series. Features large curved digital display and central screen, contemporary interaction bar, and capacitive touch AC vents. Use of recycled materials championed for environmental focus, but may feel less luxurious than traditional leather; some areas (such as lower dashboard and door pads) show cost-cutting with lower quality plastics. Space: Front and rear seat room is generous – good headroom and shoulder room, adequate knee room for six-footers, comfortable front seats. Rear seat does not recline, upright seatback and short cushion affect thigh support; high central tunnel and AC console hinder center rear passenger comfort. Storage: Deep cupholders, vertical wireless pad, wide-opening, large boot (570L), split-fold seat backs for flexibility. Sunroof and ambient light contribute to spacious, modern feel.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
   - Infotainment: BMW iDrive 9 system on curved touchscreen, crisp graphics and responsive, but AC controls embedded in screen make for a more complex interface. Head-up display large and informative, digital instrument cluster, customizable ambient lighting via interaction bar, Harman Kardon audio system. Advanced features: Augmented reality navigation, Drive Recorder/3D view (captures video pre/post accident), built-in selfie camera, remote vehicle view via app, BMW Digital Key, wireless charging, three-zone climate, optional ventilated front seats, keyless entry, panoramic sunroof. Usability: Rich feature set, but some controls are less intuitive/fiddly compared to physical buttons; multi-mode driver configuration available, comfort and sport adaptive dampers.

6. SAFETY
   - No official NCAP crash test rating yet. Safety equipment includes multiple airbags, ABS with EBD, ESP, hill descent/hill assist control, TPMS, seatbelt reminders, speed warnings, 360-degree camera, reverse parking sensors.    - 1.5L three-cylinder turbo-petrol (161 bhp, 300 Nm); e-Power hybrid (210 bhp, 525 Nm). Three driving modes (Eco, Standard, Sport). Mild hybrid tech aids efficiency. Engine described as strong and quick to three-digit speeds, but noisy under throttle; CVT criticized as sluggish compared to DCT alternatives. Braking decent, details on distances not mentioned.

Dimensions lend full-size D-segment status, boxier than crossover-like predecessor.

4. INTERIOR
   - Three-tone or dual-tone dashboard (black/brown/beige or black/brown), chrome detailing, fabric upholstery (manual seats, no ventilation). Spacious front and rear; excellent legroom/headroom second row, seat slides, reclines, and folds (40/20/40). Third-row access difficult; space tight and suitable mostly for children (low backrest, knees-up, little thigh support). Five- and seven-seat configurations, storage spaces under console, twin cupholders, butterfly centre armrest, generous door pockets, mobile tray. Overall practical, high comfort, ergonomically sound.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
   - 8-inch floating touchscreen infotainment with physical knobs, Apple CarPlay/Android Auto (wired), digital instrument cluster, wireless charger, panoramic sunroof (India-spec), electronic parking brake with auto-hold, climate control (dual-zone), rain-sensing wipers, auto headlamps, 360-degree camera, rear AC vents, multi-function steering with cruise/audio controls. 7. FUEL ECONOMY
   - Official fuel economy figures not specified for India. E-Power variant expected to deliver higher efficiency via unique series-hybrid (ICE only charges battery, battery powers drive motor), emulating EV experience and minimizing NVH. Real-world figures and comparisons not available.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
   - Expected price range: Rs 26–32 lakh (ex-showroom, likely CKD with >90% localization); potential CBU pricing could reach Rs 35–40 lakh. Value judged strong below Rs 30 lakh but competitive set (features, network, perceived value) will pressure pricing, especially if reaching Fortuner territory. Warranty and service intervals not mentioned.

9. PROS AND CONS
   - Pros: Spacious and practical cabin, strong performance, comfortable/planted ride, good second-row space, unique seven-seat and hybrid option, high-quality build and design.
   - Cons: Lack of powertrain options (only turbo-petrol, e-Power not confirmed), no diesel, some missing features (ventilated/electric seats, ADAS, third-row charging), noisy engine, small/awkward third row fit for kids only.

10. COMPETITORS
   - Hyundai Tucson (chief rival), Skoda Kodiaq, Volkswagen Tiguan, Jeep Compass, Jeep Meridian, Skoda Octavia (price overlap), Mahindra XUV700, Tata Safari, Toyota Fortuner (at higher price point). X-Trail offers panoramic sunroof, Type-C ports, ventilated seats, window curtains (over Tucson). Misses power seats, ambient lighting, ADAS, powered tailgate, etc. Stands apart with e-Power hybrid, seven-seat layout, Japanese reliability, understated design.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
   - Five-seat and seven-seat variants available; petrol FWD and e-Power hybrid with 4WD expected. Recommended variant not specified in review.

12. VERDICT
   - Nissan X-Trail is a well-rounded, handsomely designed D-segment SUV with strong comfort, ride quality, spacious second row, and unique hybrid/third-row offering. Pricing is crucial; below Rs 30–32 lakh, it is highly competitive; above Rs 35 lakh, rivals offer stronger brand pull and features. Best for buyers seeking Japanese reliability, comfort, unique tech, and third-row flexibility, but less suited for those needing full-feature luxury or adult-usable third row. Success will hinge on aggressive pricing and localization. No explicit rating score provided in review.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
   - Price: GT Plus 1.5 TSI DSG tested at Rs. 18.71 lakh; Trail Edition at Rs. 16.30 lakh ex-showroom.

9. PROS AND CONS

   Pros:

   - Five-star safety rating, six airbags, and comprehensive safety suite.
   - Engaging handling, highway stability, light but communicative steering.
   - Spacious, premium-feeling interior; comfortable for long journeys.
   - Advanced features: sunroof, digital cluster, large infotainment, wireless charging, ventilated seats (variant dependent).
   - Option-rich customization with distinctive variants.

   Cons:
   - Idle start/stop system calibration intrusive in city driving.
   - No rear-side airbags or ADAS suite; limited rear seat width for three adults.
   - Higher variants' firm suspension can be harsh over sharp bumps/potholes.
   - Some hard plastics in cabin; ventilated seats not standard on all 1.5 trims.
   - Boot access hindered by high loading lip.

10. COMPETITORS
   - Skoda Kushaq, Maruti Grand Vitara, Hyundai Creta, Kia Seltos, Toyota Urban Cruiser Hyryder, MG Astor, Honda Elevate.
   - Strengths: Superior safety, robust performance, engaging drive, premium cabin.
   - Comparison: 1.5 TSI offers unique performance edge versus most rivals; matches or exceeds them on safety. Lags behind some peers on rear seat space for three and absence of ADAS (increasingly common in segment).

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
   - Available trims: Chrome, Sport, GT Plus, Highline Plus (recent feature upgrade), Trail Edition (limited numbers).
   - Trail Edition: Value-oriented with exclusive design features and dash cameras.
   - GT Plus DSG recommended for driving enthusiasts due to best powertrain/feature mix.
   - Not all desirable features standard on every variant (example: ventilated seats).

12. VERDICT
   - Volkswagen Taigun 1.5 TSI remains a top pick in the compact SUV segment for buyers prioritizing fun-to-drive dynamics, robust safety, and premium build quality. Ideal for small families seeking a feature-rich highway cruiser with city usability. Shortcomings include rear-seat practicality, intrusive idle start/stop, and some missing tech, but overall strengths decisively outweigh weaknesses. Highly recommended for those valuing performance and safety; scores strong marks for value and engagement. Rating score not specified in the review.

REVIEW SUMMARY

   - 1.5 NA petrol: 113bhp/144Nm, 6-speed manual/IVT; smooth, refined, best for relaxed driving, negligible vibration, works best under light throttle. Not brisk, engine becomes vocal past 3,000rpm, lacks turbo’s punch for high-speed or overtaking.

3. EXTERIOR

8. VALUE AND PRICING
   - Rs. 10.90–17.38 lakh (ex-showroom), covers base to fully-loaded trims.
   - Feature list, size, tech, and safety justify premium over predecessor. Rising prices par for segment, but value remains strong versus rivals.

9. PROS AND CONS
   - Pros: Striking design, roomy and practical interior, advanced safety/ADAS, extensive features (heated/ventilated seats, switchable panel, wireless tech), strong powertrains (especially turbo), high refinement, five-star safety, refined transmissions, superior build quality, high practicality with large boot.
   - Cons: No diesel option, NA engine feels laidback, not sporty for overtaking, ride firm at low speeds, some hard plastics, rearward visibility slightly compromised, infotainment screen partially obscured, expensive compared to outgoing model, price overlaps with SUVs.

10. COMPETITORS
    - Rivals: Honda City, Volkswagen Virtus, Skoda Slavia, Maruti Suzuki Ciaz.
    - Verna stands out for tech (Level 2 ADAS, ventilated/heated seats), safety, segment-leading boot, performance in turbo trim, and unique design. Loses diesel edge, faces tough competition from value-packed SUVs and sedan rivals.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
    - Four trims: EX, S, SX, SX(O); turbo with unique black/red theme and black alloys.
    - Turbo variant recommended for performance seekers; NA petrol with IVT ideal for comfort and smoothness.
    - Features scale substantially with SX and SX(O), best value near top trims.

12. VERDICT
    - Verna redefines the sedan segment: modern, feature-stuffed, extremely safe, and user-friendly.
    - Spacious, practical, loaded with technological innovations and segment firsts; turbo offers genuine driving excitement, while NA is the sensible choice.
    - Best suited for those prioritizing style, features, and comfort in a sedan over an SUV.

REVIEW SUMMARY STRUCTURE

1. OVERVIEW

- The Tata Tigor i-CNG is a practical, efficient compact sedan targeting city usage, distinguished by its factory-fitted CNG kit, high safety standards, and fully loaded top-spec features. Review from CarWale/Kautsthubh Gandhi.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING

- Engine: 1.2-litre 3-cyl Revotron petrol (84bhp/114Nm); CNG mode (72bhp/95Nm).
- Transmission: 5-speed manual for CNG variant; AMT/manual for petrol.
- Acceleration: No official 0-100 km/h time mentioned.
- Driving: Smooth, seamless petrol/CNG switch. Negligible power loss in CNG unless fully loaded or on inclines. Some coarse note and sluggish response under hard acceleration; otherwise, linear and silent everyday performance. Gearbox is smooth-shifting, clutch light and comfortable.
- Suspension & Handling: Tweaked rear suspension for CNG load, audible over poor roads but rides well. 165mm ground clearance protects over speed breakers. Steering is light, progressive, but not sporty.
- Brakes: No stopping distance provided; presumed adequate for segment.

3. EXTERIOR

- Design: Mature, purposeful styling with new paint options, tri-arrow grille, shark fin antenna, LED DRLs.
- Dimensions: Classified as a compact sedan.
- Wheels: XZ+ trims get 15-inch alloys, CNG variant on 14-inch steel rims.
- Boot: CNG tank installation reduces boot space, higher boot section affects rear visibility.

4. INTERIOR

- Quality: Dual-tone black-beige theme, digital instrument cluster with CNG bar, cloth upholstery.
- Space: Good headroom front and rear, supportive seats for three at the back (though soft and might sag over time), but no adjustable rear headrests.
- Usability: Practical layout, good visibility, multiple storage spaces, folding rear armrest with cup holder.
- Boot: 419L (petrol) drops to 205L (CNG) – enough for duffle bags. High boot section restricts rear visibility.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES

- 7-inch touchscreen infotainment (Apple CarPlay, Android Auto).
- Digital instrument cluster (with CNG information).
- Auto headlamps (projector), rain-sensing wipers, cooled glovebox, auto-fold ORVMs, auto climate control.
- Connectivity: Full suite, including Bluetooth, smartphone integration.
- Top variants feature keyless entry, engine start-stop, shark fin antenna, LED DRLs.

6. SAFETY

- 4-star Global NCAP rating.
- Standard: Dual airbags, ABS with EBD, corner stability control, rear parking sensors with camera, puncture repair kit.
- CNG-specific: Fire extinguisher, leak/thermal protection, microswitch for fuel cap, pressure release nozzle.
- No mention of advanced driver aids (lane keep, adaptive cruise, etc.).

7. FUEL ECONOMY

- CNG: Realistic efficiency ~25 km/kg, ~300 km range.
- Petrol: ARAI 19.2 kmpl (manual), 19.6 kmpl (AMT); 672-686 km claimed range.
- Running costs significantly lower with CNG compared to petrol; competitive for segment.

8. VALUE AND PRICING

- CNG variant priced approx. Rs 90,000 higher than equivalent petrol; available in higher trims (not base).
- Offers full features list, making higher price justifiable for many buyers seeking economy and equipment.
- No explicit mention of warranty or maintenance intervals in review.

9. PROS AND CONS

Pros:
- Practical, cost-effective city sedan.
- Seamless fuel mode transitions.
- Segment-leading safety (4-star NCAP).
- Spacious, well-equipped cabin in top trims.
- Good ground clearance.
- High feature-to-price ratio, especially for CNG.

Cons:
- Power loss in CNG mode, especially under full load.
- Boot space reduced drastically (to 205L).
- Inconsistent fit and finish.
- Rear visibility limited by high boot design.
- Inferior rear seat space versus main competitors.

10. COMPETITORS

- Main rivals: Maruti Dzire CNG, Hyundai Aura CNG.
- Strengths: Tigor i-CNG offered in high-spec trims with full features (unlike rivals focused on base variants); strong safety rating.
- Weaknesses: Boot space lower than Aura CNG (Tigor 205L vs Aura 220L), less powerful in CNG mode.
- Unique selling proposition: Only compact sedan to combine top-trim equipment, factory CNG, and 4-star safety.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT

- Factory-fitted i-CNG available only in higher trims (not base variants), especially XZ and above.
- Top-spec XZ+ most feature-rich; CNG version gets slightly less exterior kit (smaller wheels).
- Recommended: Top trims if seeking full equipment; not specified directly but implied.

12. VERDICT

- The Tata Tigor i-CNG is a safe, value-rich, highly economical city compact sedan. Its strong CNG integration, feature count, and safety standards outweigh performance and space compromises. Best suited for buyers prioritizing low running costs, safety, and modern tech in daily city use. Not ideal for those frequently needing maximum boot space or rear seat legroom.

9. PROS AND CONS
   - Pros:
     - Eye-catching design and distinct coupe-SUV styling
     - Strong safety suite: seven airbags, Level-2 ADAS, electronic aids
     - Competitive real-world range; fast-charging
     - Feature-rich: panoramic sunroof, ventilated seats, heads-up display, premium interior
     - Aggressive pricing anticipated
     - Independent suspension layout (uncommon in segment)
   - Cons:
     - Cabin not as spacious as modern "skateboard" EVs
     - Real-world driving range could cause anxiety for some

10. COMPETITORS

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT

Aggressive pricing and comprehensive safety/tech package make it a strong contender against established rivals, though real-world range and brand unfamiliarity are potential hurdles. Particularly suited for buyers seeking style, features, and safety on a budget; success in India will depend on after-sales support and actual value realization. - Other Standouts: Air suspension with height adjustment for easier entry/exit; heads-up display; air purifier providing real-time air quality breakdown.

---

REVIEW SUMMARY STRUCTURE

1. OVERVIEW
   - The Volvo XC90 remains a benchmark for timeless luxury and thoughtful design in the premium SUV segment. Facelift adds visual freshness and subtle but meaningful enhancements. Review by CarWale (Pictures by Kapil Angane & Kaustubh Gandhi).

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
   - Engine options: 2.0-litre turbo petrol (247bhp, 48V mild hybrid, AWD; 300bhp/400Nm version with FWD). Power output trails rivals by over 100bhp in B5 trim. Acceleration is robust but prioritizes smoothness over outright speed. Transmission: 8-speed auto, responsive and seamless shifts; lacks paddle shifters for manual control. Ride comfort: Air suspension offers adjustability and comfort but is slightly firmer than some class competitors, transmitting more road imperfections than expected. Brakes feel strong and progressive, delivering confident and controlled stopping.

3. EXTERIOR
   - Signature Volvo styling: Tall stance, clamshell hood, familiar silhouette. New diagonal-strut front grille, sleeker 'Thor’s hammer' LED DRLs, refreshed 20-inch dual-tone alloy wheels, and updated dual-element vertical tail lamps. Panoramic sunroof standard. Dimensions unchanged; maintains commanding full-size luxury SUV presence. Multiple exterior color and wheel options available.

4. INTERIOR
   - Upmarket materials and build; minimalist Scandinavian layout. Dashboard and steering wheel design unchanged; perceived as premium and unique compared to German rivals. Electrically adjustable, massage-capable front seats; spacious, comfortable second row; flexible flat-folding third row for children. Centre console receives additional storage. Interior color options create bright, airy ambience. Good ergonomic upgrades; overall comfort remains a highlight.

5. TECHNOLOGY AND FEATURES
   - 11.2-inch Android-based infotainment system with intuitive interface; dual 12.3-inch digital displays (including gauge cluster). Wireless phone mirroring (CarPlay/Android Auto), climate controls for all rows embedded within touchscreen. Heads-up display and air purifier standard. Panoramic sunroof with voice control. Digital instrument cluster clear but limited customization.

6. SAFETY
   - Eight airbags, ABS with EBD standard across all variants. Strong ADAS suite including lane-keeping assist, blind spot monitoring, cross-traffic alert, and 360-degree camera. Tyre pressure monitoring. No official crash test ratings mentioned, but Volvo’s reputation for safety reaffirmed.

7. FUEL ECONOMY
   - Official fuel consumption figures not mentioned in review. No real-world efficiency data provided. Mild-hybrid system expected to offer moderate economy; rivals may have more efficient hybrid/diesel options.

8. VALUE AND PRICING
   - Priced at Rs. 1.03 crore ex-showroom, on par with or above segment competitors. Cabin quality, safety, and refinement contribute strongly to value. Lacks hybrid/diesel choices and has a limited dealer/service network; however, Volvo promises expanded aftersales programs.

9. PROS AND CONS
   - Pros: Elegant and timeless exterior design; outstanding interior quality; superb front and second-row comfort; high standard safety tech; refined driving experience; unique Scandinavian design.
   - Cons: Less advanced technology suite than top rivals; no hybrid or diesel powertrains; ride slightly firmer than primary competitors; scarce service centres; power output lower than German competitors in standard B5 trim; missing paddle shifters.

10. COMPETITORS
   - Direct competitors: German luxury SUVs (unlisted, but implied—likely Audi Q7, Mercedes-Benz GLE, BMW X5, etc.).
   - Compared to rivals: Trails in tech features and outright performance; lacks hybrid/diesel choices and segment-leading infotainment. Excels in safety, elegant design, interior finish, and overall refinement. Value accentuated for buyers seeking understated luxury and safety.

11. VARIANTS ASSESSMENT
   - Details of trim-level differences not fully specified. All feature strong equipment levels including safety, air suspension, sunroof, digital displays, and essential connectivity. Recommended variant not mentioned.

12. VERDICT
   - Volvo XC90 facelift delivers sophisticated looks, best-in-class interior finish, leading safety, and a comfortable, practical three-row cabin. Suited for buyers prioritizing elegance, understated luxury, and safety over outright performance or cutting-edge tech. May not appeal to those wanting the latest powertrains or most dynamic drive. Considered a refined, distinctive alternative to mainstream German rivals. Rating score not provided in review.

REVIEW SUMMARY

1. OVERVIEW
- Toyota Urban Cruiser Hyryder is the segment’s first strong hybrid mid-size SUV, co-developed with Maruti Suzuki. Key publications include CarWale. Designed to appeal to buyers wanting high fuel efficiency, advanced features, Toyota reliability, and modern design in the highly-competitive C-SUV segment.

2. PERFORMANCE AND DRIVING
- Hybrid: 1.5-litre NA three-cylinder petrol (91bhp/122Nm) + 79bhp/141Nm e-motor; system output 114-115bhp/141Nm; eCVT.
